    Chapter 1

    Introduction and concepts

    1.1 · What REMOTIX is

    REMOTIX is a remote desktop for Linux. A server runs on the Linux machine and serves a web page; the page and the server talk a protocol of our own, RCP/1 (Remotix Control Protocol), over WebTransport, that is HTTP/3 on QUIC. There is nothing to install on the device the user connects from: a browser with WebTransport and WebCodecs is the client. SPECIFICHE.md says what the product promises, RCP.md defines the protocol, DECISIONI.md records why; this manual explains how the code does it.

    Every user who logs in gets their own graphical session on the machine — GNOME, KDE Plasma, XFCE or LXQt, whichever desktop the machine has — started headless by REMOTIX, with one virtual monitor as large as the browser window. The session belongs to the user, not to the connection: closing the tab, losing the network or switching device leaves it running, and the next login finds the same windows. Only the user ends it, with “Log out” from the desktop menu or Ctrl+Alt+End in the page, or the server closes it after 60 minutes without input.

    Several users can work on the same machine at once, each in their own desktop (10 by default, set with --tetto-sessioni, the session cap). The video is encoded only on the graphics card (VA-API on Intel and AMD, Vulkan Video on AMD and NVIDIA) in H.264 or HEVC; the audio travels as Opus in QUIC datagrams; keyboard, pointer, touch and the text clipboard travel in both directions.

    Why a protocol of our own, and why a browser. REMOTIX v1 spoke RDP and stopped at its phase 11, after serving GNOME and KDE: the three walls it hit — the H.264 ceiling, an Android client decoding in software and the full colour that RDP could not carry — were walls of RDP, not of the problem (DECISIONI.md §1.1). Dropping Windows as a server removed RDP. On 9 August 2026 the dedicated clients went too (DECISIONI.md §1.6): WebTransport gives a browser exactly the bricks RCP had been designed on — independent QUIC streams, so that a frame can be abandoned without blocking the next one, and datagrams for the audio — and the protocol did not change by one line. The heritage of v1 (about 17,500 lines of C, its test benches and its studies of the desktops) is kept in fondamenta/ and parts of it live on in the server.

    What the user does. He opens https://<machine>:7447, accepts the browser's certificate warning the first time on that device (the server makes its own certificate; whoever has a domain name can install a real one), and types their Linux user name and password. The page shows their desktop, as large as the window.

    What REMOTIX deliberately does not do (SPECIFICHE.md §12): Windows as a server; any application to install on the client; X11 desktop sessions; redirection of disks, printers, serial ports or smart cards; file transfer; images and files in the clipboard (text only); multi-monitor as a feature; stylus pressure and tilt; native multi-finger touch (a place is reserved in the protocol); recording the session to a file; compatibility with RDP, VNC or SPICE clients.

    i
    Goals, not promises. SPECIFICHE.md §3 sets a minimum of 480p, 25 fps, 24 bit, a desired 4K, 60 fps, 10 bit per channel, and a delay of at most 50 ms (target 40 ms) from the input arriving to the frame leaving. Since 30 September 2026 these are design goals, not measured promises (user decision): performance tests depend too much on the hardware. The parameters the product really uses — session cap, clocks, ban, minimum bandwidth — are configuration and hold as written.

    1.2 · Basic concepts

    A few concepts recur in every chapter. Most of them have an Italian name in the code, which the manual keeps inside code spans so that it can be searched for.

    The design is held together by eight invariants, numbered in CODER.md §2 and quoted throughout the code comments as I1…I8; they are listed in 2.1 “Architectural principles”.

    i
    One desktop per machine. REMOTIX recognises the desktop from what is installed (riconosci_desktop() looks for gnome-session, startplasma-wayland, xfce4-session and lxqt-session in the PATH). Machines with more than one desktop are out of scope (DECISIONI.md §0.6): if two are present, one is chosen — GNOME before KDE, XFCE before LXQt — and the ambiguity is written in the log at startup.

    1.3 · Subsystems at a glance

    The server's code is split by job. This is the map the manual follows chapter by chapter; the line counts of every file are in the file map appendix.

    main.c, figlio.c, aiutante.c, sentinella.c, ritrovo.c, comando.c

    trasporto.c, webtransport.c, tls.c, certificati.c, pagina.c
    UDP and QUIC with ngtcp2 and nghttp3, the WebTransport sessions, the two certificates, the page served over TCP (ch. 4 “Transport: QUIC, HTTP/3, WebTransport”).
    rcp.c, rcp.h, autenticazione.c
    The RCP/1 state machine: handshake, credentials, ban, attach, channels, farewell (ch. 5 “The RCP/1 protocol”).

    input.c, wlr_input.c, tastiera.c

    1.4 · The repository

    The nic-fio/REMOTIX repository on GitHub (private) holds everything: the product, the installer, the packages, the test benches, the measurements and the documents. Documents and code comments are in Italian; this manual is in English, and so is most of the page the user sees — but some of the sentences the page shows, such as the reasons of a farewell (MOTIVO in pagina.html) and the ban notice, are still in Italian.

    !
    Old headers. several documents carry a status box at the top that was true on the day it was written: README.md still describes src/ as “not in git” and the project as paused, and the comment at the top of main.c still says “phase 1, no video”. The code and the newest sections of DECISIONI.md win; ch. 20 “Conventions” explains how the documents are kept.

    1.5 · The project in numbers

    How big REMOTIX is, part by part. The lines are counted from the sources every time the manual is generated: files kept by git under src/, installatore/ and packaging/, plus the manual's own sources; the vendored Go modules, the protocol headers generated at build time and binary files are left out. The test benches (banchi/, about 1,800 files) are not counted.

    A large share of the C is comment: by the project's rules every non-obvious line carries the reason, the measurement or the decision behind it, often with the date. The counts in this table and in the file map are never written by hand.

    Chapter 2

    Overall architecture

    2.1 · Architectural principles

    REMOTIX grew out of a few rules, most of them written before the code and each paid for by a measurement or a defect. They explain choices that would otherwise look odd: a root server that never touches the user's desktop, a separate process for every password check, a desktop that outlives the server.

    Eight invariants, inherited from v1 and renumbered in CODER.md §2, are quoted in the comments next to the lines that keep them. A change that breaks one of them is a defect even if every test passes.

    2.2 · The processes of REMOTIX

    REMOTIX is one binary, /usr/libexec/remotix/remotix, that plays several roles. The server forks the others; the children re-execute the same binary with --figlio-interno (internal child) so that they start from a clean process image, as a different user.

    Two facts shape this tree. The desktop is started from inside the user's logind session, so it lives in that session's scope and not in the cgroup of remotix.service: stopping the service (KillMode=mixed) does not kill it. And the child is the leader of that logind session (it opened it with pam_open_session): when the user logs out, logind ends the session and takes the child with it.

    i
    Not processes. the sentinel (sentinella.c) and the found-again search (ritrovo.c) are not processes: they are modules that ask logind synchronously, with a short timeout, from inside the loop of whoever calls them (2.7 “The logind sentinel”).

    2.3 · The parent process

    The server is a single thread around one poll() in main(). Everything that could block — PAM, a user's D-Bus, PipeWire, the GPU — lives in another process, so that one user logging in never freezes the frames of the others.

    The wait is the time to the next QUIC timer (trasporto_attesa_ms()), capped at one second so that clocks that do not wait for an event still fire; with the test tone of --audio-prova it is capped at 10 ms. After every wake-up the loop runs, in this order: trasporto_leggi(), wt_giro_del_padre(), the abandonment clock (abbandono_giro()), ritrovati_ripassa(), the PAM verdicts and expiries, figli_muovi(), figli_ricontrolla(), trasporto_scaduti(), pagina_muovi() and comando_muovi(). Three slower duties hang off the same loop: every 2 s (RIPASSO_LOCALI_MS) the sweep that looks for local sessions, every 60 s a log line with the sentinel's counters, and every 60 s the certificate rotation check.

    Why one thread. Since 12 August 2026 the server process touches neither GLib nor PipeWire nor a user's D-Bus (those moved into the children). So the fork() that creates a child starts from a process with one thread — the only condition in which forking a program that links threaded libraries is safe. The PAM verdict used to block this loop: measured on 11 August 2026 on the test machine (Intel i5-13500T), 1.0 to 2.2 s per attempt, most of it added by pam_faildelay on failed attempts. With video that would have frozen every user's screen whenever someone else logged in (DECISIONI.md §1.10).

    The bridge. main.c is the only file that knows both the transport and the children. A small struct ponte carries the two, and webtransport.c and figlio.c call each other only through hooks registered at startup:

    2.4 · The PAM helper process

    Checking a password is the only thing the server needs root for besides changing user, and PAM can take seconds. So it happens in another process, in a three-tier shape decided by the user on 11 August 2026: a process, not a thread, because PAM is not reliably reentrant.

    The request carries the case number (pratica, 64 bits), the user name (up to 256 bytes), the password (up to 1024) and the client's bare address for PAM_RHOST (taken from the [address]:port form, with an IPv4-mapped prefix removed). The grandchild runs the service remotix with PAM_TTY set to remotix, a conversation that answers only the hidden prompt with the password, then pam_authenticate and pam_acct_mgmt: only when both return PAM_SUCCESS does it write the byte 1.

    The password is in clear in the server's memory, in the request buffer and in the dispatcher: each copy is zeroed as soon as it has been used, and none reaches the log (RCP.md §4.4). The socket pair has no name in the filesystem and dies with the two processes. The helper is started before trasporto_apri() on purpose: a process forked later would inherit the UDP socket and the TCP listener and keep the port busy after the server died.

    i
    MAX_IN_VOLO. the in-flight cap of 16 is not the session cap and was deliberately left separate when every other copy of the session count was unified on 25 August 2026: it is how many password checks run at once, a different quantity.

    2.5 · The per-user child process

    For every admitted user the server forks one child that becomes that user. Two facts measured on 12 August 2026 force this shape (DECISIONI.md §1.10-bis): root cannot connect to a user's session bus — gdbus to Mutter fails with “The connection is closed” — and only root can verify another user's password with PAM, because pam_unix outside root goes through unix_chkpwd. Without the bus there is no capture; without root there is no authentication.

    Before forking, figli_assicura_da() looks for an existing child of that user and returns it (I2: two connections of the same user share one child, and one stage). It refuses, with a log line, a full table, a name that PAM admitted but NSS cannot resolve, and uid 0 (the child exists not to be root). It then adds the user to the GPU's groups if needed (3.4 “Birth of a session”), opens a SOCK_SEQPACKET pair with SO_PASSCRED on the server's end — refusing, again with a log line, if either fails — and forks. In the forked process diventa_ed_esegui() does, in order:

    The child's command line is remotix-figlio --figlio-interno <user> <uid> <gid> <width> <height> <serial> <dir|->, followed by the switches the child must share with the server: --parlantina (verbose log), --journal, --qualita-risale (let the quality climb back), --tetto-banda-mbit N (the bandwidth floor in Mbit/s), --niente-audio-silenzio (do not suppress silent audio blocks) and --codifica vulkan|vaapi (the encoding path). They travel on the command line because the environment is rebuilt from nothing. The server refuses to fork children if its own binary was replaced on disk (/proc/self/exe ends with (deleted)).

    Identity is a fact of the kernel, not a promise of the code. Once running, figlio_vive() sets PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (SIGTERM), checks its ids again (exit 42 if wrong) and introduces itself with MSG_SONO — real, effective and saved ids, parent pid, how many descriptors are still open, whether its runtime directory and bus socket exist. It must do so within 15 s (SCADENZA_SONO_MS) or the server kills it. On every message the server reads the SCM_CREDENTIALS the kernel attached and requires: the child's pid, the user's uid and gid, the child's serial number, the uid declared in the header, and that the user name still resolves to that uid (credenziali_combaciano()). Any mismatch: SIGKILL. Every 60 s (RICONTROLLO_MS) the server asks “who are you” again.

    !
    No idle timeout. the child keeps no deadline after its introduction: a silent child is one nobody is asking anything (I4). Its life is tied to the graphical session, never to a connection.

    2.6 · The server–child channel

    Server and children talk over the SOCK_SEQPACKET pair created at the fork: the kernel keeps message boundaries, so a message can neither arrive in halves nor merge with the next one. Every message starts with the same header.

    Large payloads — frames, cursor images, clipboard text — are cut into pieces of at most 32 KiB (PEZZO_MAX) with total, offset and piece length, and reassembled on the other side. A frame may be up to 16 MiB (FOTOGRAMMA_MAX), the same limit as RCP.md §6.2, so that no limit of ours is lower than the protocol's. The frame's input field is stamped by the child at capture time with the last input it injected: only the child knows what the compositor had actually received, and stamping it in the server would make the measured delay shorter than the real one.

    2.7 · The logind sentinel

    The sentinel answers three questions for which logind is the authority, through the system bus, synchronously and with a 300 ms timeout (ATTESA_MS): a short wait is cheaper than a thread and a mutex in a server that has one thread on purpose.

    A local session is one with a seat. The obvious criterion — graphical type and Remote=no — would make REMOTIX refuse itself: logind marked REMOTIX's own sessions Remote=no as long as no PAM_RHOST was set. The discriminating fact is the seat: a local session sits on seat0, with a real screen and keyboard; REMOTIX's sessions have none, which is also what makes Mutter headless. A session counts as local when it has a seat, a graphical Type, Class user (greeters and lock screens are not the user at work), is not Remote, and is not closing.

    One question for all tenants. The sweep used to call logind once per attached user. Measured on 25 August 2026 on the test machine: with 7 tenants and logind answering in 286 ms, every desktop fell to 1.3 frames per second, silently. ListSessions already returns every session of the machine and cost 2.4–2.6 ms whatever the number of sessions, so sentinella_locali() asks once and answers for everyone; only sessions with a seat are opened one by one, and on a headless machine there are none.

    i
    Asked from the right place. the power-off check must run in the child. Root always gets yes, because logind checks CAP_SYS_BOOT before asking polkit (measured on 15 August 2026): asked from the server, the check would always pass.

    If logind does not answer, the sentinel answers “no local session” and writes one line (not repeated until logind is back): “I don't know” is treated as “there is none”, the only choice that does not punish a user who did nothing wrong (I1). If the system bus cannot be opened at startup, the local-session rule is not applied and the log says so.

    2.8 · Event loops and threads

    Each process has its own loop. Only the child has threads, and they are the libraries' or narrow helpers that never touch the encoder.

    On labwc (XFCE, LXQt) the capture and the virtual devices run on the child's own loop with Wayland calls; on GNOME the D-Bus calls to Mutter iterate a private GLib context. The encoder runs synchronously in the child's loop: capture, encode, send, then the next frame. Encoding frame N while capturing N+1 would raise the frame rate and add delay, and SPECIFICHE.md §3.2 forbids that trade.

    2.9 · Where state lives

    Each piece of state has one owner and one lifetime. The rule in the code is that a global is a second place where something can be alive or dead, so shared things travel in structures (struct ponte) and each table is sized once, at startup.

    One number for the cap. RCP_TETTO_SESSIONI (10) in rcp.h is the default, --tetto-sessioni N moves it at startup, and rcp_tetto() is read once by every table that counts users: the attach slots of rcp.c, the children of figlio.c, the presence table of main.c and the stages of webtransport.c. Until 25 August 2026 these were five hand copies of 16 (one of them 8) while SPECIFICHE.md promised 10.

    +
    Stages, not connections. the cap counts stages, not connections: a user who closed their browser still holds a stage until logout or abandonment. palchi_quanti() adds the children and the found-again desktops; a new user who finds them all taken is refused with 0x0E SESSIONE_NON_SERVIBILE (the session cannot be served) before any process is forked.
    Chapter 3

    Startup and life cycle

    3.1 · Server startup

    The server starts from main() in main.c. Before opening a port it finds out what the machine can do and writes it in the log, so that a missing piece is read at startup rather than discovered by the first user.

    1. Role. With --figlio-interno as first argument the process is a child and goes to figlio_vive(); with --prova-codifica (encoding test) it encodes one frame on the GPU, prints one JSON line and exits (0 the GPU encodes, 1 it opens but no frame comes out, 2 usage error, 3 no GPU can encode).
    2. Options. The command line is read; an unknown option prints the usage and exits with 2. Options that no longer exist (--ritmo-adattivo, --linea-morta, --sblocca — adaptive pace, dead line, unblock) exit with 2 and a sentence saying what replaced them, instead of being silently ignored. Without a real --nome (the name; empty, 0.0.0.0 or ::) the server refuses to start: the certificate must carry the name the browser will use.
    3. Signals. SIGINT and SIGTERM only set a flag that ends the loop; SIGPIPE is ignored. With --journal every log line also goes to the systemd journal (ch. 13 “Logging and diagnostics”).
    4. The GPU. A forked process opens each encoder on a 256×256 frame (figlio_capacita_video()); its answer, or its silence after 30 s, decides the codecs that the ECCOMI will offer. In a separate process because a driver that crashes must not take the server down before it has a port. With no GPU that encodes, the log says so with the reason for each codec and every CIAO (the client's hello) will end in NIENTE_IN_COMUNE (nothing in common).
    5. The desktop. sessione_desktop() recognises the desktop from the programs in the PATH and the log says which, and why; on KDE kwin_verifica_permesso() checks that the .desktop file that lets KWin offer screen capture to this binary is in place.
    6. Clocks and switches. The three session clocks, the five network cures of phase 9, the session cap and the budget are written in the log with the value in force, on and off (I6): a one-hour clock cannot be checked by waiting an hour.
    7. The ban. rcp_ban_carica() reads /var/lib/remotix/ban; if the file cannot be read the server exits with 1 rather than forget who was banned.
    8. The PAM helper (aiutante_accendi()), before any port is open, so that it does not inherit them. If it does not start, the server goes on and every login will be refused — and the log says so.
    9. The children table (figli_accendi()), sized on the session cap; it resolves /proc/self/exe once, for the children's execve.
    10. The unblock socket (comando_apri()), only with --comando-socket; without it the log says that a ban can only expire.
    11. PAM file. guarda_il_servizio_pam() looks for /etc/pam.d/remotix and /usr/lib/pam.d/remotix. It does not refuse to start, but without the file Linux-PAM falls back on the other service — pam_deny on Fedora and Arch, so every right password would be refused as if it were wrong — and the log says exactly that.
    12. Certificates and TLS. certificati_prepara() loads or generates the two certificates in /var/lib/remotix/certificati, then the two TLS contexts are built (one for QUIC, one for the page).
    13. QUIC. trasporto_apri() binds the UDP port; then the hooks between transport and children are registered, the sentinel connects to the system bus, and the desktops left alive by a previous server are looked for (3.7 “Desktops found again after a restart”).
    14. The page. pagina_apri() binds the TCP port. The log line ⭐ pronto: https://NAME:PORT (“ready”), which goes on to say that the WebTransport session lives on /rcp/1, is the moment the server can be used.
    i
    Degrade, and say so. the server goes on when the PAM helper, the children table, the unblock socket, the sentinel or the codec probe fail, because the ban, the page and the certificates still work and stopping everything would put the blame on the wrong part. Each of these failures writes one line that names what will not work.

    3.2 · The systemd unit

    In a package the server runs as remotix.service, a system unit. The packages install it but neither enable nor start it: remotix-install does that once the installation is confirmed (ch. 15 “The installer”).

    packaging/debian/remotix.service (excerpt, without the two EnvironmentFile lines)
    [Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'exec /usr/libexec/remotix/remotix --indirizzo 0.0.0.0 --nome %H \
    --porta "$${REMOTIX_PORTA}" --certificati /var/lib/remotix/certificati \
    --pagina /usr/share/remotix/pagina.html --ban-file /var/lib/remotix/ban \
    --journal $${REMOTIX_OPZIONI}'
KillMode=mixed
LimitRTPRIO=20
LimitNICE=-11
Restart=on-failure
RestartPreventExitStatus=78
RestartSec=2
    !
    Two gaps of the unit. with no --comando-socket in the packaged command line, a banned address can only wait for its 12 hours: the unblock command promised by SPECIFICHE.md §4.2 is there only if the administrator adds the option in REMOTIX_OPZIONI (the tmpfiles entry creates /run/remotix for that socket). No code path of the server exits with 78, so RestartPreventExitStatus=78 never applies today.
    i
    Started by hand. the server must not run inside a user's session. pam_systemd, called by a process that is already in a logind session, does not create a second one and does not say so: the children stay without runtime directory, bus and desktop (measured 16 August 2026, eight bench runs out of eight). As a system unit this cannot happen; on the test machine riavvia-7700.sh starts the server with systemd-run and refuses to report success if /proc/PID/cgroup shows a user@ or session- cgroup.

    3.3 · From password to admission

    A login crosses three processes. The page proves nothing until the server has shown its certificate; the password goes to a PAM process; the yes produces a child; only then does the client attach. The message names are those of RCP.md: CIAO (hello) and ECCOMI (here I am), CREDENZIALI (credentials), AMMESSO (admitted), ATTACCA (attach) and SESSIONE (session).

    The verdict. The server writes the request to the PAM helper and goes back to its loop (2.4 “The PAM helper process”). Every answer to CREDENZIALI — admitted or refused — leaves no sooner than one second after the request arrived (RITARDO_FISSO): without it “user does not exist” would answer in a millisecond and “wrong password” in fifty, and the stopwatch would tell what the reason code deliberately does not. Three failed checks from the same address within 5 minutes ban that address for 12 hours, whatever the user names; a success resets the count; the ban survives restarts (ch. 5 “The RCP/1 protocol”).

    Yes is not yet in. When the helper says yes, consegna_verdetto() asks three questions, in this order, before anything is forked — a refusal after the desktop has started is not a refusal, it is a login followed by an eviction (measured 25 August 2026: a user never admitted had 42 processes and a gnome-shell):

    A user who already has a child, or a desktop found again, skips the first two: they are already counted, and their SESSIONE will say resumed (2) instead of new (1). For a new child the abandonment clock starts now, at birth, not at the first gesture: a session opened and never touched must expire too. Then the verdict is handed to the transport, and only after it the farewell, if any: the verdict is the only place where the failure count of the ban is reset, and a farewell sent first would leave a user who typed the right password with their failures on record. The client never sees AMMESSO followed by an eviction: AMMESSO leaves only when the second has passed, and by then the session is already closed with its reason.

    i
    The price. this tells whoever knocks that the password was right. It is the declared price of not leaving them in front of a black page, the same price paid when the attach table is full.

    The child works during the second. figli_assicura_da() forks and returns at once: the child opens the user's logind session and its bus while the fixed second runs out, which is the only time the protocol guarantees before ATTACCA.

    3.4 · Birth of a session

    The child is born before it knows the canvas, and it must not start the desktop at the wrong size: on Wayland a resize completes only when the compositor delivers a new frame, and a fresh desktop changes nothing. Measured on 16 August 2026: starting at 1920×1080 and resizing 650 ms later left users looking at black bands for 13 to 30 seconds. So the child waits for the client's canvas, at most 1.2 s (TELA_ATTESA_MS), then starts with what it has.

    Once running, figlio_vive() introduces itself, prepares the dconf profile, removes leftovers of a previous session from the user manager (sessione_sgombera_gestore()) and calls prendi_il_palco(). That function connects to the user's session bus, reads the state of the graphical session and, if there is none, asks sessione_fai_nascere() to start it.

    The child does not wait for the desktop. A child that waits 40 s does not answer the server, and the server would deduce a failure from its silence. Instead it tells the server “wait” (MSG_TELA with attendi), which postpones the answer to the client, and retries. While the desktop is being born — up to 12 s after asking (NASCITA_BRIGLIA_MS) — it retries every 200 ms (PALCO_NASCITA_RIPROVA_MS); after that the wait doubles from 1 s to 30 s (PALCO_RIPROVA_MIN_MS, PALCO_RIPROVA_MAX_MS). Both numbers were paid for: on 14 August 2026 a loop that retried without pause wrote 30.8 GB of log in a few minutes; on 16 August a doubling wait made users wait up to four seconds for a session that was already up (GNOME appeared on the bus after about 2.9 s on the test machine, and the tries fell at 3 s and then 7 s).

    First login: the GPU's groups. A user who is not in the groups of the /dev/dri nodes (card* belongs to video, renderD* to render) would get a session that renders in software with llvmpipe — slow, not broken, so nobody would suspect it. Since 20 September 2026 (DECISIONI.md §7.21) the server, as root, runs usermod -aG for the missing groups before forking the child, appends one JSON line per group to /var/lib/remotix/gruppi-iscritti.jsonl (so that uninstalling removes only what REMOTIX added) and, unless the user already has a live REMOTIX desktop, runs loginctl terminate-user so that their user manager restarts with the new groups.

    !
    First login ends the user's other sessions. loginctl terminate-user ends every logind session of that user, an SSH login included. It only happens once per user, at their first REMOTIX login without the groups. Not settled yet: whether only render should be added (video also opens /dev/fb* and webcams), DECISIONI.md §10.36.

    After the first stage the child, once per life, inhibits suspend and idle (on GNOME through org.gnome.SessionManager.Inhibit with flags 4|8, never the logout flag, or the user would lose their only way out; on KDE through PowerDevil; XFCE and LXQt by configuration), then asks the sentinel whether its session has no seat and whether power-off is forbidden, and writes both answers in the log. Written is not in force: the check is the program's, not a configuration line's (I7).

    3.5 · The stage and the virtual monitor

    The stage is what the child mounts on the user's desktop: a virtual monitor, the capture of its pixels, the input devices, the clipboard and the cursor. It belongs to the session and survives every client (I4).

    prendi_il_palco() mounts these in order and times each step (a step over 250 ms is logged). It starts the capture on the GPU path (dmabuf, zero copy) and falls back to the memory path if the compositor refuses the format; it takes a first frame with a 5 s wait; on the very first mount it encodes that frame in HEVC and in H.264 to prove both streams; it reports everything to the server in MSG_PALCO (bus, session state, capture result, monitor name and count, size, stride, bits per channel, streams encoded, failure in words); then it opens the cursor, the input channel — applying a keyboard layout that arrived before it — and the clipboard. On GNOME a monitor with a scale other than 1 is refused: the coordinates of input would no longer match the pixels.

    Why the child keeps everything open. Measured on 27 August 2026 with a real Mutter: in headless mode the virtual monitor is born only when a PipeWire consumer attaches to the stream (65–93 ms after), survives the consumer detaching, and dies when the D-Bus connection that called RecordVirtual closes. The child holds that connection and the stream for its whole life; when nobody is watching, it only stops taking frames. An application opened while no client is attached still has a screen to draw on.

    The capture loop. While a codec is requested, each turn takes a frame with a wait of at most 8 ms. Mutter delivers only when something changes, so most turns on a still desktop find nothing; if a keyframe is owed and nothing came, the child wakes the compositor every 400 ms (RISVEGLIO_MS), unless a key or button is held. A frame of a new size resizes the encoders and the input region, drops the kept keyframes and answers the server with the canvas obtained. A capture failure, or KWin closing its stream, unmounts the stage and the retry starts again. Every second the loop logs its counts: frames, keyframes, empty waits, failures.

    3.6 · Detach and reattach

    Detaching is the normal end of a connection, and it ends nothing else: the slot frees, the stage stays.

    In every case the keys still pressed are released in the desktop, so no key stays down after a drop. If no other client of the same user is watching, the server tells the child to stop capturing — MSG_VIDEO and MSG_AUDIO with codec 0 — and the child, the desktop, the monitor and the audio sink stay where they are. The farewell, the closed stream and the dead connection all lead to the same function, which is idempotent: the child is told once.

    Reattaching. When the same user logs in again, figli_pid_di() finds their child: no fork, SESSIONE says resumed, and the server sends MSG_RIMANDA_PALCO so that the child resends the last keyframe it kept for each codec — the user sees their desktop at once — and owes a new keyframe. The page then asks for its own canvas with ADATTA_TELA (fit the canvas; ch. 9 “The browser page”). A reattach does not renew the abandonment clock: only input does.

    i
    Local wins: what is closed. SPECIFICHE.md §5.1 says that when a local session starts “the remote one is closed”. The code dismisses the remote client; the remote desktop is not ended and, if nobody touches it, ends with the abandonment clock.

    3.7 · Desktops found again after a restart

    Stopping the server does not stop the desktops: the server, the PAM helper and the children die, while each desktop, started with setsid --fork inside its user's logind session, keeps running with its programs (measured 29 September 2026, ten trials with Firefox on the four desktops: stopping the unit, killing only the server, killing only a child). Until phase 17 a new server started with an empty table and counted none of them — not in the cap, not in the budget, not on the abandonment clock.

    At startup ritrovati_all_avvio() calls ritrovo_cerca(), which uses only logind and /proc — the server is root and cannot join the users' buses, and desktops started by an older binary wrote no file of ours:

    1. every logind session whose PAM service is remotix, in any state: the child calls pam_end without pam_close_session, so the session is closing 24 ms after birth and stays so as long as it has processes (measured 29 September 2026);
    2. in that session's scope, a process of the user that leads its own process session (pid = sid) and whose parent is not in the same scope: the signature of setsid --fork, the same on every desktop — gnome-session-binary, startplasma-wayland, labwc, all with parent 1. A terminal's shell also leads a session, but its parent is in the scope;
    3. one desktop per user; at most 256 (QUANTI_RITROVATI_MAX).

    Each desktop found is logged and kept “waiting for reattach”: it counts in the cap and in the budget, and its abandonment clock restarts from the server's start (the last gesture seen by the old server was in its memory). When its user logs in, a new child is born — the old one died with the old server, by design — takes over the same compositor, and SESSIONE says resumed. Every 10 s (RIPASSO_RITROVATI_MS) the server checks that the desktops it found are still there, so that one that died on its own does not hold a place for an hour. If the clock expires with nobody back, the server forks a child just to close that desktop: only a process inside the user's bus can end a desktop properly, and desktops are closed, not killed.

    +
    Upgrades. a package upgrade restarts the server with try-restart only if it was running; the users' desktops survive and the new server finds them again. Before stopping the service by hand, look at who is connected anyway: their clients are dismissed with 0x0C SERVER_IN_CHIUSURA (server shutting down).

    3.8 · The three session clocks

    Three clocks run on different scales — seconds, minutes, an hour — and each ends something different.

    Silence is measured on the last QUIC packet decrypted and authenticated, not on RCP bytes: counting RCP made a user who was only reading lose their slot after 30 s, and a second device take it while they looked (measured 16 August 2026). A switch from Wi-Fi to mobile data is not silence: QUIC carries the connection across the address change. A background tab frozen by the browser falls silent and detaches; the session waits.

    Input means the five gestures a user sends — pointer, button, wheel, letter, key position — and nothing else: not the key release at detach (it would reset the clock at the wrong moment), not a canvas change, not the request to log out. input_al_figlio() feeds the presence table of main.c; abbandono_giro() looks at it on every turn of the loop. The abandonment clock starts when the stage is born and is not renewed by reattaching: someone who attaches and only watches renews nothing (user decision, 16 August 2026, when the clock went from 6 hours without an attach to 60 minutes without input).

    Why an hour. The user asked for the cost of an abandoned session to be measured first. On 16 August 2026, on the test machine (31 GB of RAM), an abandoned GNOME session used 477 MB (PSS) — 182 MB of it gnome-shell, 116 MB the child — and about 0.017 % of a core, without growing over time. Not a leak, a fixed cost; the user chose to pay it for an hour rather than six.

    i
    Logged at startup. all three values are written in one log line at startup; a clock set to 0 is marked (SPENTA) or (SPENTO) (off).

    3.9 · Ending a graphical session

    Only the user ends their session; the server ends it only when it is abandoned. Either way the reason is sent before the desktop dies: when the compositor goes, the stage goes with it, and a reason sent after reaches nobody (finding B-7).

    sessione_termina() asks politely, then insists: on GNOME Logout with mode 1, then mode 2 (forced); on KDE an orderly logout, then forced; on XFCE and LXQt the session manager's exit, then killing the compositor — each followed by a wait for the session to be really gone (up to 10 s). Then sessione_sgombera_scope() sends SIGTERM to whatever of the user is still in the child's own session scope, waits up to 2 s and sends SIGKILL to the stubborn (on Ubuntu 26.04 with XFCE, localsearch-3 and an agent used to stay), and sessione_sgombera_gestore() removes REMOTIX's drop-ins and puts the user manager's environment back as the snapshot recorded it. The child exits with 0.

    A logout is not followed by a rebirth. A child that has seen its session alive and then dead remembers that the user left; it does not start the desktop again until a new attach requests a codec. Without this the desktop the user had just closed came back by itself a few seconds later (bench of 15 August 2026). The page goes back to the login form with its sentence for 0x10 (the session has ended and its programs were closed), out of full screen and pointer lock.

    i
    Why a new reason. 0x01 promises “reattach and you will find everything”, which after a logout is false; 0x10 exists so that the two endings never share a code (DECISIONI.md §4.1-quater).

    3.10 · Server shutdown and cleanup

    When systemd stops the unit, the server says goodbye to every client before it closes QUIC, then lets its children go; the desktops stay.

    1. The signal sets the flag; the loop ends and the log says how many QUIC connections are alive.
    2. Every RCP session receives CONGEDO 0x0C SERVER_IN_CHIUSURA (trasporto_congeda_tutte()). The server keeps reading and running timers until nothing is left to say, for at most 4 s by the clock (it used to count turns, which on a fast machine gave up after three tenths of a second while the safety net for the closing capsule was 3 s).
    3. Then, if every session has said all it had to say, it keeps the connections alive for another 50 turns of 10 ms: a capsule handed to ngtcp2 is not yet on the wire, and without this wait Firefox saw the service vanish with no reason (bench B7, 11 August 2026). The log says how many turns each phase took, or which connections still had something to say.
    4. Clean-up, in this order: the PAM helper (SIGTERM to the dispatcher), the sentinel, the unblock socket, the page, the transport, the children — each receives SIGTERM and is waited for — and the TLS contexts.

    A child also dies on its own when the server disappears, by two independent roads: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (which is lost when credentials change, so the child sets it again after execve) and the end of file on its socket. The child's own SIGTERM handler is the default one, so it dies without unmounting: the desktop keeps running and the next server finds it.

    When a child dies with the server alive — a crash, a kill — congeda_figlio() forgets the size of its stage and its presence entry, and dismisses its clients with 0x10 unless the server itself is stopping (then 0x0C is the right reason, because the session will be found again). The server also kills a child that does not die within 3 s of being told to go.

    3.11 · Files on the machine

    What REMOTIX puts on the machine, and who puts it there. Paths are those of the Debian package; the rpm and Arch packages use the same ones, except where noted.

    The user's own settings are not changed, with the exceptions DECISIONI.md §8.2 allows — lock, reboot, suspend and stand-by removed — detailed per desktop in ch. 12 “The four desktops”. The session log is created with O_NOFOLLOW in a folder that must be the user's, not a link and not writable by others: until phase 17 it lived in /tmp under a predictable name, and another user could pre-create it.

    !
    The belts are off by default. since DECISIONI.md §10.36 (10 October 2026) the installer no longer puts the belts in force: on a packaged machine nobody forbids power-off unless the administrator enables the files in /usr/share/remotix/cinture/. The child checks and writes it in the log at every first stage; SPECIFICHE.md §11.3 still says power-off is taken from everyone.

    3.12 · From symptom to step

    A defect in this chain rarely names its cause: the user sees “black”, “slow” or “nothing happens”. Start from the symptom, find the step, then read the log of the area that owns it.

    Chapter 4

    Transport: QUIC, HTTP/3, WebTransport

    4.1 · The transport stack at a glance

    REMOTIX has no client program: the client is the browser. A web page cannot open a bare QUIC connection, but WebTransport over HTTP/3 gives it the same building blocks the protocol was designed on — independent unidirectional streams, the abandonment of a stream with RESET_STREAM, unreliable datagrams and connection migration. The server therefore speaks QUIC version 1 with mandatory TLS 1.3, HTTP/3 and WebTransport on UDP, and serves the page itself on TCP. There is no clear-text mode, and RCP never runs on TCP.

    Everything runs in the parent process, in one poll loop: QUIC, HTTP/3, WebTransport, RCP and the page server share the thread. The two pieces of work that could block that loop live elsewhere: PAM runs in a helper process (aiutante.c) and everything that touches the user's desktop runs in the per-user child. The transport only moves bytes between the network and those processes.

    4.2 · Why ngtcp2 and nghttp3

    The QUIC library was chosen on 10 August 2026 with a bench (banchi/01-b2-*), not on paper. The question was not «which QUIC» but «which library gets as far as WebTransport on the server side, and how much glue is left to us». None of the candidates implements server-side WebTransport.

    The price is declared in webtransport.h: nghttp3 offers no API to put an arbitrary setting on the HTTP/3 control stream, so the server rewrites the SETTINGS frame while nghttp3 is writing it (riscrivi_impostazioni()). That depends on the shape of the bytes nghttp3 produces, not on a promise of its API, and must be re-tested at every nghttp3 upgrade. The guard is loud: if the bytes are not the expected ones nothing is rewritten, the log says so, and the server has no WebTransport — never a misaligned control stream.

    TLS comes from the system OpenSSL 3.5 through ngtcp2_crypto_ossl, which carries the native QUIC API. Bench B2 had measured with BoringSSL, the default of the ngtcp2 examples; the product does not bundle a second cryptographic library, and tls.h declares the change of stack instead of treating the two as equivalent.

    4.3 · Two listeners on port 7447

    The server listens on port 7447 twice: UDP for HTTP/3 and WebTransport, TCP for the first load of the page. The user types https://address:7447, accepts the certificate warning once per device, and types user and password into the page.

    The two are independent. The first draft of RCP.md required an Alt-Svc header on the TCP response; measurement S1 (9 August 2026) showed that WebTransport does not use Alt-Svc at all — a WebTransport session opens its own HTTP/3 connection to the address it is given. That also removed a feared failure mode, the silent fallback to TCP («the page opens and the desktop never arrives»): there is no fallback to make.

    !
    No SO_REUSEADDR on UDP. the UDP socket is bound without SO_REUSEADDR. With that option, on 10 August 2026 the socket bound to 7447 while another server already held it: two unicast UDP sockets share the port and only one of them receives the packets, so «the server is on and the page does not connect» with two processes both convinced they are listening. On TCP the option stays, because there the kernel refuses a second listener anyway and the option only avoids TIME_WAIT after a restart.

    The port is set with --porta (default 7447, PORTA_PREDEFINITA in main.c). The packaged unit passes --porta "$REMOTIX_PORTA", with REMOTIX_PORTA=7447 in /usr/share/remotix/remotix.conf and overrides in /etc/remotix/remotix.conf.d/; extra options go in REMOTIX_OPZIONI. The number was chosen on 9 August 2026 because it is free in /etc/services of Debian Trixie. Not settled yet: whether 7447 is free in the IANA registry — nobody has checked.

    4.4 · QUIC transport parameters

    Each connection gets the same transport parameters, set in trasporto.c just before ngtcp2_conn_server_new. With a browser as client, RCP can no longer dictate the client's parameters: what stays normative is what the server announces, and what must be measured instead of assumed.

    The stream credit is renewed by cb_stream_close in trasporto.c. Renewal is the peer's policy, not a consequence of closing a stream: on 2 October 2026 a measurement showed 19 streams and then nothing, so ngtcp2 does not raise the limit on its own in this configuration. A server that waited for credit would be counting on someone else's courtesy; the rule instead is that the server must survive a refused stream (4.9 “Streams versus datagrams”).

    • No address validation with Retry: the product is meant for an own network or a VPN (SPECIFICHE.md §4.1). The code declares it as something to restore before exposing the server.
    • No UDP GSO: trasporto.c splits each aggregate and sends one packet per sendto (at most MAX_PACCHETTI_PER_GIRO = 64 packets per pass). It costs system calls, not correctness.
    • The congestion controller was never chosen: ngtcp2_settings_default() leaves cc_algo at ngtcp2's default (CUBIC). See 4.11 “Congestion and the send queue”.
    i
    Stale comment. a comment in rcp.c (above SILENZIO) still says max_idle_timeout is 120 seconds; the code announces 30 s. The 30-second attach-slot rule is enforced by RCP on its own clock either way.

    4.5 · TLS and the two certificates

    There are two certificates, not one, and they are kept apart down to their file names. The page certificate is the one on which the user grants the browser exception, so it must change as rarely as possible; the session certificate is checked by fingerprint, and browsers accept that only for certificates valid less than 14 days, so it rotates on its own.

    • Key type. ECDSA P-256 only (EVP_EC_gen("P-256")): not Ed25519 and never RSA. P-256 is the only key type that keeps serverCertificateHashes open, and a key chosen for convenience would close that road without anyone noticing.
    • The private key is born 0600 (open(…, 0600)), not chmod-ed afterwards: between creation and chmod there would be a window in which it is readable.
    • The name. The subjectAltName is the value of --nome (the packaged unit passes the host name %H), written as an IP address entry or a DNS entry according to its form. A browser that finds a mismatching SAN shows a different warning, and some offer no click-through at all. A user who connects by IP declares it with REMOTIX_OPZIONI=--nome 192.168.1.10.
    • The administrator's certificate is never touched. Every certificate written by REMOTIX has a .nostro marker file next to it; a pagina.pem without the marker belongs to someone else and is never regenerated, not even when it expires. The test is «did we write it?», not «is it self-signed?»: the second is a deduction and would be wrong on a private self-signed CA.
    • The fingerprint is SHA-256 over the DER bytes of the session certificate — not over the public key and not over the PEM text (X509_digest(crt, EVP_sha256(), …)). It is kept in base64 for the page and in hexadecimal for logs and browser error messages; rotazioni counts the rotations since start.
    !
    Never one certificate for both. serving the page with the short-lived certificate would bring the browser warning back every two weeks, and nobody would connect the two facts. That is exactly the defect bench B13.1 exists to see; one SSL_CTX for both listeners would be the same defect written where nobody looks for it.

    4.6 · serverCertificateHashes and the fingerprint

    The page carries the fingerprint of the session certificate, and the browser accepts the WebTransport connection without a warning when the certificate matches it. The user's exception on the page certificate does not extend to WebTransport on either Chrome or Firefox (measurement S1, 9 August 2026), so the fingerprint is the normal road, not a safety net.

    1. The server writes the current fingerprint into the page: pagina.c replaces __IMPRONTA__ in pagina.html on every request for /.
    2. Before every connection the page fetches /impronta with cache: "no-store". A tab left open for two weeks holds the fingerprint of a certificate that has since rotated; without the fresh fetch the browser would refuse the reconnection and nothing would say why. The fetch does not go through RCP — there is no session yet on which to ask. If it fails, the page uses the fingerprint it was served with, and says so.
    3. The page opens new WebTransport("https://" + location.host + "/rcp/1", …) with allowPooling: false and serverCertificateHashes: [{ algorithm: "sha-256", value: … }].

    Measured on 9 August 2026 on two independent engines: a session to a self-signed ECDSA P-256 certificate valid 13 days, with the fingerprint published in the page and no warning, opened on Chrome 151 and on Firefox 140, and the bytes came back identical from both. The server on that bench was aioquic, so it validated the trust model, not our server. WebKit implemented the same mechanism in October 2025, but REMOTIX has never been tested on Safari or iOS, and nothing here claims it works there.

    i
    Accepted risk. the first connection on each device is open to a man in the middle, who would not merely read the page but rewrite it. The risk is accepted for the intended scenario — own server, own network or VPN — and a real certificate from a CA removes the warning altogether (SPECIFICHE.md §4.1, DECISIONI.md §1.7).

    4.7 · The page server

    pagina.c is a small HTTPS/1.1 server: one request per connection, Connection: close, non-blocking sockets inside the same poll loop. It reads pagina.html from --pagina (the packages install it as /usr/share/remotix/pagina.html).

    Every response carries Cache-Control: no-store, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and the cross-origin isolation headers required by SPECIFICHE.md §11.5: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin, Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin. Isolation gives the page full-resolution timers (performance.now() measured at 5 µs grain on Chrome 151, 14 August 2026) and shared memory. The third header is not optional: with require-corp the browser refuses any sub-resource that does not declare it, and the symptom does not mention isolation — the resource simply does not load.

    A banned address still gets the page, with HTTP status 200 and a notice that begins tentativi esauriti (attempts exhausted) and gives the hours and minutes left; the notice is written in Italian in pagina.c. The page is served even when banned because whoever is banned by mistake is almost always the owner, and a server that looks dead for half a day is the worst diagnosis; 200 rather than a 4xx because an intermediary or the browser may replace the body of an error response with its own page, and the sentence the owner must read would vanish. The ban itself is described in 5.7 “Credentials, the fixed delay and the address ban”.

    4.8 · The WebTransport layer

    webtransport.c is the layer on top of ngtcp2 and nghttp3. It covers three holes: WebTransport cannot be announced through the nghttp3 API; WebTransport streams must be taken away from nghttp3, which would read the session number after 0x41 as a frame length; and the bytes going back on those streams have no road, because nghttp3 never schedules streams it does not know.

    • Both drafts are announced. The test client aioquic 1.2 implements draft 02, browsers look for draft 07. A server announcing only one would work with half of the tools — the wrong half to draw conclusions from. An unknown setting is ignored by the other side.
    • HTTP/3 needs three unidirectional streams. If the client grants fewer than three, HTTP/3 is not opened and the connection fails, logged.
    • One session per connection. w->sessione holds the stream id of the CONNECT; WT_TETTO_CANALE_NS (5 s) starts when the session opens: if the client does not open the control channel in time, the session is closed with TEMPO_SCADUTO (timed out) in the closing code (DECISIONI.md §7.17).
    • Client streams are classified by their first bytes (enum genere, the kind): undecided, WebTransport bidirectional (the control channel), HTTP/3 (handed to nghttp3), WebTransport unidirectional for input (0x01), for clipboard (0x02), lawful but not served, or already judged a violation. The channel is recognised by the high byte of the first RCP tipo (message type) after the preamble, never by the stream number (5.3 “RCP: channels and stream identification”).
    • The closing capsule goes inside a DATA frame. Written bare, its first byte 0x68 makes the browser read a two-byte frame type 0x2843, an unknown HTTP/3 frame that RFC 9114 requires to ignore; the page saw only the FIN behind it, which closes the session with code 0 — the one value RCP forbids.
    • The capsule is delayed. It is queued only after the send queue of the session has drained, plus WT_ATTESA_CHIUSURA_NS (500 ms): bench B11 (10 August 2026, real browsers) found that Chrome drops a message sent immediately before the session is closed.
    • A capsule from the client is parsed into its code and handed to rcp_chiusa_dal_client(); a code outside 0x01–0x0F is logged as a violation of §3.1 and recorded as ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO (protocol error).

    4.9 · Streams versus datagrams

    Each RCP channel uses the QUIC piece that matches its needs. The single most important design choice is that a video frame is a stream: a late frame does not hold up the next one, and the server can abandon a frame that is no longer useful with RESET_STREAM so that its unsent bytes never leave.

    On a single stream a slow frame would block all the following ones (head-of-line blocking) and on a mobile network the session would accumulate its own past. On datagrams the server would have to rewrite fragmentation and retransmission — QUIC inside QUIC. One stream per frame gets independence for free, and abandonment for the price of a key frame (5.10 “RCP: the video frame”).

    Audio datagrams. A datagram cannot be fragmented: it must fit in one packet. RCP sizes PCM blocks at 5 ms (960 bytes + 12 of header = 972) for that reason, and the server caps its datagram at WT_DGRAM_BYTE = 1024 bytes. That number is the one measured on 17 August 2026 with the probe banchi/07-b40-*: the largest datagram browsers accepted against our server was 1024 bytes on Chrome 151 (fixed) and 1024 growing to 1214 on Firefox 140esr after about 800 ms. PCM fits by 52 bytes on the stricter engine. At most WT_DGRAM_MAX = 8 blocks wait to be sent; a block that has not left within WT_DGRAM_ZITTO_MAX_MS = 10 ms of the queue being blocked is dropped and counted. Losses and acknowledgements of datagrams are tracked in pairs (wt_dgram_perso(), wt_dgram_riscontrato()): ngtcp2 can declare a datagram lost and later see it acknowledged, which is reordering, not loss.

    Stream credit for video. The browser grants unidirectional streams to the server at its own pace. The server must survive a refused stream instead of treating it as fatal, and when the credit is missing it drops the frame — but never a key frame, which waits. WT_UNI_RISERVA = 2 streams are left unused by video so that the client's own streams are never starved, and at most WT_INVOLO_MAX = 32 frames are in flight per session. A frame dropped for lack of credit is invisible to the client (no stream, no gap in the numbering), so the server owes a key frame on its own; that rule exists because of defect B-18, 13 August 2026.

    !
    The send buffer belongs to us until acknowledged. ngtcp2_conn_writev_stream() does not copy the bytes: it keeps our pointer and re-reads it to retransmit. Until 23 August 2026 a frame was freed once serialised, and a 525 298-byte frame served by mmap crashed the server (SEGV in memmove); smaller frames silently retransmitted garbage from the heap. A queue element now has two states: consegnato (delivered: all bytes handed to ngtcp2, kept allocated) and morto (dead: freed), reached only from an acknowledgement covering the bytes, the closing of the stream or its reset.

    4.10 · Keep-alive, silence and the dead line

    Three different clocks watch a connection, and they measure different things: QUIC's idle timeout measures the silence of the network, RCP's 30-second clock decides who holds an attach slot, and the dead-line detector decides when a line has stopped carrying anything.

    Transport PINGs. While the RCP state is anything but finita (finished), the server arms ngtcp2's keep-alive (ngtcp2_conn_set_keep_alive_timeout()) every WT_TIENILA_VIVA_NS = 10 s, or half of the dead-line silence when the detector is on — 5 s with the defaults. They exist for two reasons. RCP.md §4.6 gives the user 60 s to type the password, but nothing travels while they type and the 30-second QUIC idle timeout would kill the connection first (finding R1.8). And without our own PINGs the liveness margin belongs to the browser: on an idle scene packets arrived every 15 002–15 005 ms, Chrome's keep-alive, half the 30 s ceiling. PINGs carry no information and have no reply to interpret, so they are not the application heartbeat that RCP forbids.

    Why the silence clock looks at packets, not RCP bytes. Counting RCP bytes, a user who was only reading lost their attach slot after 30 s and a second device took it (measured 16 August 2026: detached at 30 013 ms with the connection alive). The 30-second clock now looks at the last decrypted and authenticated packet; the minutes-long inactivity clock (5.20 “RCP: session clocks”) is the one that looks at what the user sends.

    Why the dead line looks at stall, not loss. The first version on 23 August 2026 used ngtcp2's pkt_lost / pkt_sent and ordered the two reference lines backwards: a line that held for ten minutes declared 512‰ and one that did not hold 123‰, because ngtcp2 counts an overtaken packet as lost and on a reordering line the ratio measures reordering. Output stall separated the two cases sixtyfold (0.50 s against 30.06 s). The ratio survives only as a witness in the log line. The detector is on by default since 24 August 2026 (--niente-linea-morta turns it off).

    Why the idle timeout stays at 30 s. The value is negotiated, so 10 s would also make the browser drop us after 10 s of our own silence, and frozen images up to 14.26 s were measured on 23 August 2026 under heavy bursty loss; ngtcp2 expires at max(idle, 3·PTO) anyway; 30 s is normative (DECISIONI.md §4.4); and the PINGs every 10 s would fire at the same instant as a 10 s timeout.

    4.11 · Congestion and the send queue

    QUIC measures the line continuously, which v1 had to do by hand. REMOTIX uses that measurement and adds three mechanisms of its own on the video queue; the policy built on them — quality, frame-rate reduction, budget — is the subject of the chapter «Quality, degradation and budget».

    i
    Defaults. the threshold and the regulator are on together by default since 24 August 2026 (the user's decision after watching them). With the threshold off the delta queue empties at every frame and the regulator can never trigger; the start-up log line says so. Their declared price, measured on 23–24 August 2026 with bench 09-b79: up to +160 ms of drift on a bad line, zero on a healthy one.
    i
    Stale floor. WT_PAVIMENTO_BYTE_MS assumes 20 Mbit/s, while the declared network floor became 30 Mbit/s on 23 August 2026 (SPECIFICHE.md §8.1). It only applies before the first RTT sample.

    4.12 · A connection from first packet to close

    One QUIC connection carries at most one WebTransport session and one RCP session. The figure follows a connection from its first datagram to its close; the RCP steps inside it are in 5.5 “RCP: the handshake”.

    1. First packet. trasporto_leggi() receives with recvmsg (with the destination address from IP_PKTINFO/IPV6_RECVPKTINFO), ngtcp2_accept checks the Initial packet, and a new connessione is created with an 18-byte server connection id. The source address in text form becomes the provenienza (provenance) used for the ban and the logs.
    2. Handshake keys ready. wt_app_pronta() opens HTTP/3: three unidirectional streams of our own (control, QPACK encoder, decoder) with the rewritten SETTINGS.
    3. CONNECT. The session opens on /rcp/1 and the 5-second deadline for the control channel starts.
    4. Control channel. The first bidirectional WebTransport stream from the client becomes RCP's control channel; rcp_apri() creates the rcp_sessione with the provenance and the current millisecond clock.
    5. Life. Stream data goes to rcp_ricevi(), rcp_ricevi_input() or rcp_ricevi_appunti() according to the stream's class; frames, audio blocks and cursor shapes from the child are fanned out by user name (wt_video_diffondi(), wt_audio_diffondi(), wt_cursore_diffondi()), each reaching only the connections whose RCP user is that user.
    6. Close. RCP decides why (5.18 “RCP: the farewell”); the WebTransport layer sends the capsule. At shutdown trasporto_congeda_tutte() says goodbye to every session with SERVER_IN_CHIUSURA and waits for queues to drain before the process exits.
    +
    Verdict routing. the PAM verdict reaches the right connection through trasporto_verdetto(): the helper returns a ticket number, the transport offers it to every live session, and exactly one takes it. A ticket that finds nobody is lost on purpose — the connection died while PAM was answering.
    Chapter 5

    The RCP/1 protocol

    5.1 · RCP: the protocol model

    RCP/1 — the Remotix Control Protocol, version 1 — is what the page and the server say to each other inside the WebTransport session. The name says control, not display: besides pixels it carries input, clipboard, geometry, the farewell and the state of the session. Its specification is RCP.md, written before the first line of code and precise enough to prove an implementation wrong.

    Three properties are built into that order. The server proves who it is (TLS with the pinned certificate) before the password leaves the browser. Authentication comes before attachment: whoever is not admitted cannot even name a session. And the canvas is agreed at attach time. A message that arrives in a state where it is not expected is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO (protocol error) — the protocol says «you got the order wrong» instead of punishing each permutation with a different error, which was trap 1 of the v1 lessons.

    The message names are those of the code and of RCP.md, in Italian: CIAO (hello) and ECCOMI (here I am) exchange versions and capabilities, CREDENZIALI (credentials) carries user and password, ATTACCA (attach) asks for a desktop and SESSIONE (session) grants it.

    Why the specification is the referee. In v1 the referee was mstsc: if Microsoft's client drew it, it was right. In REMOTIX client and server are both ours, and two programs written by the same hand that agree with each other confirm nothing — they repeat the same assumption. So client and server are never tested against each other: they are tested against RCP.md, by programs that were written reading only the specification (5.23 “Testing against the specification”).

    i
    Why hooks and not includes. because the twin is compiled inside the ngtcp2 examples, rcp.c cannot include input.h, cursore.h, gio or xkbcommon. Everything it needs from the product — PAM, streams, input injection, keyboard layouts, the stage, local sessions, the clipboard — reaches it through the function pointers of rcp_ganci. The pointers are optional; a missing hook is logged, never treated as a client violation.

    5.2 · RCP: the rigor rule

    An implementation that receives something it does not understand must close with ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO and log what it did not understand. It must not ignore it, guess or continue. The rule covers an unknown message type, a length that does not add up, a field out of range, a message in the wrong state and a channel used in the wrong direction.

    It is the first rule of the document, not a footnote, because a lenient parser is convenient on day one and poisonous forever: if the server starts emitting a wrong field and the client politely ignores it, the defect stays invisible until it produces a distant, incomprehensible symptom — and with no foreign client left to complain, nobody sees it.

    Every tolerance is logged: a silent tolerance is indistinguishable from a defect. Rows 7 and 8 entered on 13 August 2026 when it was found that other sections already ordered them while this list claimed six — since then, whoever writes a tolerance elsewhere adds its row here in the same change.

    1. Log what was not understood: the type, the length, the state — not «protocol error».
    2. Send CONGEDO (farewell) with the reason on the control channel, if the control channel is still usable.
    3. Close the WebTransport session with the application error code equal to the reason code (5.19 “Disconnect reasons”). Not the QUIC connection: a page can only close its session.

    Step 3 is the one that saves diagnoses: if the farewell cannot arrive — broken stream, unreadable message — the reason still travels inside the close. In v1 the server logged «dismissing the client» while the client logged «network error» for three phases. Code 0 means «closed without reason» and must never be used. In rcp.c the three steps are congeda() (dismiss); the host's chiudi (close) hook performs step 3.

    5.3 · RCP: channels and stream identification

    Whoever receives a stream must know what is inside before reading it. The channel is given by the high byte of the first tipo (type) field of the RCP payload — never by the stream number, which WebTransport does not even expose to a page.

    • Any other high byte is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO; so is a channel in the wrong direction (0x01 from the server, 0x03 from the client), 0x00 on a unidirectional stream, 0x03 on the control stream, and 0x04 on any stream.
    • The client must not open bidirectional streams beyond the control channel, and the server must not open any.
    • The server opens no video stream before it has sent SESSIONE; the client opens its input stream only after receiving SESSIONE, exactly one, and keeps it open.
    • In rcp.c the control channel accepts only high byte 0x00 (drena(), «drain»); a second input stream while the first is alive, or input bytes before SESSIONE, are violations (rcp_ricevi_input()).
    !
    The preamble is not RCP. on WebTransport every stream starts with a preamble — the stream type 0x54 (unidirectional) or 0x41 (bidirectional) as a QUIC variable-length integer, on the wire 40 54 and 40 41, followed by the session number. The «first two bytes» are the first two bytes of the RCP payload, after the preamble that the transport consumes. The test client read the first two bytes of the stream literally on 12 August 2026, found channel 0x40 and closed every frame; server and page had agreed only because the same hand wrote both (finding P18).

    5.4 · RCP: elementary types and framing

    Byte order is network order (big-endian). No field is aligned and no padding is allowed: fields are read and written in sequence. An extra byte that «makes the sums work» in a C struct is exactly the defect corrected in the video header on 9 August 2026, when a drawing gave eight bytes to a u32.

    Framing on the control, input and clipboard channels
     0        2        6                    6+length
 ├────────┼────────┼─────────────────────┤
 │ tipo   │ length │ body                │
 │ u16    │ u32    │                     │
    • length is the exact number of body bytes. For every control type whose shape is known, misura_campi() parses the fields and compares: a length that disagrees with the fields is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO, and the log names both numbers.
    • No message may exceed 1 MiB including the 6 framing bytes: MAX_MESSAGGIO = 1 048 576, MAX_CORPO = MAX_MESSAGGIO - 6 (defect B-14, 10 August 2026: the body was compared with the whole cap, so 1 048 582 bytes on the wire were accepted).
    • The length is checked before allocating. The control-channel accumulator grows on demand up to MAX_ACCUMULO = 1 MiB; the input accumulator is I_ACCUMULO = 32 bytes forever, because the five input types have fixed lengths known from the type alone — whoever announces a megabyte on the input stream is dismissed after six bytes.
    • Every integer has a single declared meaning of «absent»; there are no implicit sentinels (numero = 0 (number), id = 0 and istante = 0 (instant) are each declared where they are used).

    5.5 · RCP: the handshake

    The handshake has five steps and runs on the control channel. Every message has a deadline (5.9 “Handshake deadlines and session states”) and every wrong turn ends in a reason the page can show.

    1. Control channel. The page opens the first bidirectional stream. Its closing is the end of the session.
    2. CIAO → ECCOMI. Version and capabilities; the server picks codecs (5.6 “CIAO and ECCOMI: capability negotiation”).
    3. CREDENZIALI → AMMESSO (admitted) / RESPINTO (rejected). One attempt per connection. The server asks PAM through the helper process and answers no earlier than one second after receiving the message (5.7 “Credentials, the fixed delay and the address ban”).
    4. Capacity gate. Between PAM's yes and AMMESSO, the parent checks that the user can have a stage: if all stages are taken (SESSIONE_NON_SERVIBILE, «session cannot be served»), the composition budget says no (BUDGET_PIENO, «budget full»), or the stage cannot be started, the page receives CONGEDO with that reason instead of AMMESSO (consegna_verdetto(), «deliver the verdict», in main.c). The child is not spawned for a user who is about to be dismissed.
    5. ATTACCA → SESSIONE. Canvas, view and keyboard layout; the server takes the user's seat and answers with the granted canvas (5.8 “ATTACCA and SESSIONE: attaching to a desktop”).
    6. Channels. The first video frame is a key frame; the page opens its input stream and, since 15 August 2026, sends one ADATTA_TELA with the size of its own window (DECISIONI.md §5.0-sexies).

    5.6 · CIAO and ECCOMI: capability negotiation

    CIAO (client → server) carries the highest major version the client speaks and its capabilities; ECCOMI (server → client) carries the version chosen and the server's capabilities. Both bodies have the same shape.

    Body of CIAO and ECCOMI
    CIAO / ECCOMI
 ├── u16  versione   (version)
 └── list of capabilities
       u16 count
       for each:  string name · string value

    Form of names and values, enforced in tratta_ciao() (handle CIAO) so that «ignore what you do not know» does not become «guess»:

    • a name is a-z, 0-9, . and _, 1 to 64 bytes (the underscore was added on 10 August 2026 when the validator, at its first run, rejected video.misura_massima — a name defined by the specification itself);
    • a value is printable UTF-8, 1 to 256 bytes; empty is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO (whoever has nothing to say omits the capability);
    • a list is comma-separated without spaces; an unknown item inside a known list is discarded and logged, like an unknown name;
    • a name repeated twice is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO — «last wins» and «first wins» would be two implementations of the same text;
    • a capability from the wrong side (banco.marca from the client) is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO.

    Negotiation. The server chooses, inside the intersection, following the client's order of preference (prima_comune(), «first in common»), and logs the choice. pcm and depth 8 must be declared by both: a client that omits them is dismissed with NIENTE_IN_COMUNE (nothing in common), not ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO — it did not write badly, it has nothing in common. An empty intersection, or a server whose GPU encodes nothing (empty video.codec), also ends in NIENTE_IN_COMUNE; the server never falls back to a codec nobody declared. AV1 left the negotiation on 20 August 2026 (Firefox for Android had neither HEVC nor AV1, AV1 had no hardware encoder anywhere in the setup, and Firefox painted rectangular blocks on bytes that Chrome and dav1d decoded cleanly); its number 2 is never reused.

    Version. CIAO must carry exactly RCP_VERSIONE = 1, the number in the path /rcp/1; anything else is VERSIONE_INCOMPATIBILE (incompatible version). The page checks the version in ECCOMI the same way and dismisses with the same reason.

    i
    What ECCOMI says. ECCOMI carries the server's offer (for example video.codec=hevc,h264), not the single codec it chose. The page takes the first item of the server's list that it can paint; the server chose the first item of the page's list that it can encode. The two agree today because both lists are in the order hevc,h264 (PREFERENZA, «preference», in the page, the start-up probe in the server); the codec actually used is the one carried by each frame header.

    5.7 · Credentials, the fixed delay and the address ban

    A single CREDENZIALI message carries user and password; the server hands them to PAM (service remotix) and answers AMMESSO (empty body) or RESPINTO with a one-byte reason. There is one attempt per connection: a second attempt needs a new connection.

    Bodies
    CREDENZIALI
 ├── string utente     (user) 1..256 bytes, printable UTF-8
 └── string parola     (password) 1..1024 bytes, no NUL byte
AMMESSO                (empty)
RESPINTO
 └── u8 motivo         (reason) CREDENZIALI_ERRATE 0x07 · TROPPI_TENTATIVI 0x08
    • No distinction between «no such user» and «wrong password»: both are CREDENZIALI_ERRATE (wrong credentials).
    • RESPINTO is the farewell of authentication. After it the server closes the session with the same code and sends no CONGEDO. The client may still send one CONGEDO — §8.1 obliges whoever closes to say why — but anything else, in particular a second CREDENZIALI, is the violation §4.4 forbids. giudica_dopo_la_fine() (judge after the end) tells the two apart in the log.
    • The password is wiped (memset) as soon as it has been handed on, and never appears in any log at any level.
    • The empty strings are a protocol error, not a PAM attempt: otherwise an attacker sending empty credentials would never increment the ban counter.

    PAM runs outside the loop. Until 12 August 2026 PAM blocked the server's single poll loop for one to two seconds per attempt (bench B8, 11 August 2026), most of it pam_faildelay; with video flowing, every screen would freeze whenever someone else logged in. Now chiedi_verifica (ask for verification) hands the question to a helper process (aiutante.c, «helper») and returns a ticket; the verdict comes back through rcp_verdetto() (verdict). A process, not a thread, because PAM is not reliably re-entrant. Two deadlines guard the answer: the helper's own at 8 s, and TETTO_VERDETTO (verdict ceiling) = 12 s in rcp.c, which counts as a no. If the question cannot even be sent, the answer is RESPINTO at once and does not count as a failed attempt — the fault is ours.

    The fixed second. The server never answers CREDENZIALI earlier than RITARDO_FISSO (fixed delay) = 1000 ms after receiving it, AMMESSO included; the answer leaves from rcp_tempo() once both the delay has passed and the verdict is in. The ban removes whoever guesses; the fixed second removes timing as a channel — without it «no such user» would answer in a millisecond and «wrong password» in fifty. Not settled yet: PAM's own delay is not constant (median 2636 ms over 42 rejected attempts, bench B8, 10 August 2026), so the fixed second does not fully hide whether a user name exists.

    • Only failed authentication counts. Not protocol errors, version or codec mismatches (they can come from a defect of ours or a stale tab), not timeouts, and not GIA_ATTIVA_REMOTA (already active remotely): counting the latter would let a user ban themselves by retrying from the phone while their session is alive. The user name does not matter: three names count three.
    • A banned address is answered without asking PAM, but still with RESPINTO(TROPPI_TENTATIVI) (too many attempts) after the fixed second — a ban answered in a millisecond would itself be a timing channel. The page is still served, with the hours left.
    • The key has no port because there is one attempt per connection and the port changes at every attempt: bench B5 found that the earlier counter, keyed with the port, was always 1.
    • Nobody can get someone else banned: reaching CREDENZIALI requires a completed QUIC handshake, so the source address cannot be forged.
    • Unlocking. The ban lives in the memory of the serving process, so a second process that rewrote the file would leave the server answering TROPPI_TENTATIVI and exit 0 as if it had worked; --sblocca (unlock) was removed for that reason and now prints why. The live process answers a one-line protocol on a Unix socket created 0600 with --comando-socket PATH (command socket): SBLOCCA <address> → TOLTO (removed) or NON-BANNATO (not banned), and PING → PONG. Every unlock is logged.
    !
    Unlock on installed systems. the packaged units do not pass --comando-socket: it is listed among the bench options that costruisci-rpm.sh refuses in a unit. On an installed system the documented way out of a ban is the 12-hour expiry; editing /var/lib/remotix/ban only takes effect after a restart. Not settled yet: an unlock command for installed systems.

    5.8 · ATTACCA and SESSIONE: attaching to a desktop

    ATTACCA asks for a desktop: the canvas the client would like, the view it will draw into and the keyboard layout. SESSIONE answers with the canvas actually granted.

    Bodies
    ATTACCA
 ├── u32    tela_larghezza       canvas width requested (a preference)
