 ├── u32    tela_altezza         canvas height requested
 ├── u32    vista_larghezza      view width: the size the client will draw at, >= 1x1
 ├── u32    vista_altezza        view height
 └── string disposizione         layout (XKB), e.g. it, us, de(neo); <= 64 bytes
SESSIONE
 ├── u8     stato                state: 1 = NUOVA (new), 2 = RIPRESA (resumed)
 ├── u32    tela_larghezza       the GRANTED canvas width
 ├── u32    tela_altezza         and height
 └── string desktop              gnome · kde · xfce · lxqt · sconosciuto (unknown)

    The canvas is the desktop's resolution; the view is the browser area it is drawn into. The canvas belongs to the session and survives the client; the view belongs to the connection. tratta_attacca() (handle ATTACCA) applies, in order:

    1. Above the maximum is not an error. A side over RCP_TELA_L_MASSIMA = 4096 or RCP_TELA_A_MASSIMA = 2304 (in these names L is the width, A the height) is brought to the maximum, the other side unchanged (5120×2880 → 4096×2304, 5120×1440 → 4096×1440), and logged. The page applies the same rule in tela_da_chiedere() (canvas to ask for), so both arrive at the same number.
    2. Below the minimum, or odd, is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO: 320×240 minimum (RCP_TELA_L_MINIMA, RCP_TELA_A_MINIMA), both sides even. A view side of 0 is also an error; any view from 1×1 up, odd included, is legal.
    3. Layout form: [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ optionally followed by (variant) of the same alphabet; out of form (including an empty variant it()) is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO. A well-formed layout the machine does not know (asked to XKB through the disposizione_esiste hook, «layout exists») is SESSIONE_NON_SERVIBILE. Upper case and underscore are allowed because the system uses them: of 589 layout/variant pairs on a Debian machine (21 August 2026), 9 have a capital and 102 an underscore.
    4. A local graphical session of the same user (sessione_locale hook, «local session») → GIA_ATTIVA_LOCALE (already active locally).
    5. The seat. One remote client per user (invariant I2). If the user's seat is held by a live client, the newcomer gets GIA_ATTIVA_REMOTA — whoever arrives is refused, never whoever was there. If the holder has been silent longer than --sfratto-ms («sfratto» = eviction; default 15 000 ms, half the silence clock) the seat is taken from it (the «ghost eviction»). If the server's table is full (--tetto-sessioni, «session cap», default RCP_TETTO_SESSIONI = 10) → SESSIONE_NON_SERVIBILE.
    6. The decoder cap. If the canvas exceeds video.misura_massima, it is reduced keeping the proportions and parity; if not even 320×240 fits, SESSIONE_NON_SERVIBILE.
    7. The stage wins. If the user's stage already exists at another lawful size (it survives the client), SESSIONE grants that size, so pixels flow at once; the page then asks for its own with ADATTA_TELA.
    8. SESSIONE says RIPRESA when the user's stage existed before PAM admitted them, NUOVA otherwise, and names the desktop of this machine. The client must not change behaviour on the desktop name: it is for diagnosis only.

    Why 4096×2304. Until 1 October 2026 the maximum was 7680×4320. The user lowered it (phase 19: «4096 max width is plenty»), and the reason is video: H.264 on the Intel VA-API low-power entry point accepts 32–4096 px per side (measured 22 August 2026: 4096×2160 yes, 4112×2160 no), and Firefox on Linux only receives H.264. 2304 is 16:9 at 4096 and 4096×2304 is 36 864 macroblocks, exactly the MaxFS of H.264 levels 5.1 and 5.2. The change was compatible: no number added or reused, and a client asking more simply receives less.

    Why even sides. Encoders work on blocks and 4:2:0 halves chroma; an odd size would be rounded by the encoder in silence — two sizes under the same label. Better to refuse it where the reason can be said.

    i
    The canvas survives the session. three attaches in a row with ATTACCA(1920×1080) received 1920×1080, 1264×800 and 1600×900 (21 August 2026): each time, what the previous connection had left. Asking for a canvas in ATTACCA does not obtain it; only ADATTA_TELA changes the canvas.

    5.9 · Handshake deadlines and session states

    A connection stuck halfway through the handshake holds a place and declares it to nobody. Each step therefore has a ceiling, and an expired ceiling ends with TEMPO_SCADUTO (time expired) — not with QUIC's 30-second idle timeout, which measures the network rather than a client that does not do its job.

    The first ceiling counts from the opening of the control channel, the instant the server really observes; the end of TLS is not usable, because a second session on a reused connection would start with its budget already spent. The ceiling before the channel was the last way to hold a place without saying who you are, and was decided by the user on 11 August 2026 (DECISIONI.md §7.17). The 60 seconds for the password are reachable only because the server sends transport PINGs while it waits (4.10 “Keep-alive, silence and the dead line”). A 10-second ceiling after AMMESSO had been written as 60 000 by copying the line above (finding R9.9).

    5.10 · RCP: the video frame

    One stream, one frame. There is no length: the end of the stream is the end of the frame — but only if the stream ended with a FIN. A reset stream carries an incomplete frame.

    Video frame header (28 bytes, no padding; tipo = type, numero = number, istante = instant)
     0      2      4        8        12       16       24       28
 ├──────┼──────┼────────┼────────┼────────┼────────┼────────┼── data …
 │ tipo │codec │ width  │ height │ numero │istante │ input  │
 │ u16  │ u16  │ u32    │ u32    │ u32    │ u64    │ u32    │

    rcp_video_apri() (open a video frame) writes the header itself: width, height, codec and number are not parameters, so the rules on them cannot be broken by a caller. The caller passes chiave, the data length (declared first, so the cap is checked before a byte leaves), the capture instant and the input id; rcp_video_pezzo() (piece) writes data, rcp_video_finisci() (finish) ends with FIN only if every declared byte went out, and rcp_video_spedisci() (send) does all three. The server must never produce a frame over 16 MiB (V_TETTO, «tetto» = cap): it re-encodes at lower quality and logs it. Measured on 22 August 2026: at a user canvas of 2560×1080 the largest of 404 real key frames was 21 433 bytes, so the cap is unreachable there; at 7680×4320 uniform noise exceeded it, which is one more reason the maximum canvas is now 4096×2304.

    • The client discards a frame whose numero precedes the last one delivered to the decoder (signed difference modulo 2³²) — and this ordering rule applies before the size rule.
    • A stream closed with FIN before the 28 bytes is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO, not a short frame.
    • A frame at a size never in force is held while an ADATTA_TELA sent by the client is unanswered, and re-judged when the TELA arrives; with no request in flight it is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO at once.
    i
    Held frames. RCP.md §6.2 requires the client to cap the frames it holds and to drop the oldest as a gap when the cap is exceeded. The page has no such cap (it counts held frames but never drops them), and the specification leaves the number open. Not settled yet: the cap.

    5.11 · Key frames and abandonment

    Video is compressed with prediction between frames: losing a delta frame ruins every following frame until a key frame arrives, and a decoder fed a missing delta raises no error — it paints progressively more broken images. Abandoning a frame is cheap only if the cure, a key frame, is guaranteed.

    • The first frame after SESSIONE must be a key frame, and so must the first frame at a new canvas — a real one, with its parameter sets in front. Measured on 12 August 2026 (Chrome 151, VA-API): an HEVC decoder given a delta at the new size raises nothing and keeps emitting frames at the old size.
    • The client reconfigures its decoder on the first key frame at the new size, not on the TELA message; a VideoDecoder reconfigured early demands a key frame anyway.
    • The server never abandons a key frame (rcp_video_abbandona(), «abandon», and rcp_video_abbandonato_a_valle(), «abandoned downstream», refuse and log). Abandoning the cure is not a cure.
    • While a key frame is still in the send queue, the deltas behind it are not abandoned for the queue threshold: they would not shorten it, and each one would open a gap asking for another key (22 September 2026, the spiral seen with a 4K video).
    • The client sends RICHIEDI_CHIAVE with ultimo_numero (last number: the last decoded frame, 0 if none) on a gap or a decoder error — one per gap, and another after 1 s without a key, never one per frame.
    • The server may ignore a request within V_GRAZIA_CHIAVE (key grace) = 200 ms of the last key it sent — counting from requests instead, insistent clients would push the clock forever. But a request whose ultimo_numero is at or after the last key frame says the gap came after it, and is always served (22 September 2026: ignoring it left the page frozen for good).
    • Until a key frame arrives the client shows the last good image: a frozen image for a tenth of a second is better than a broken one.

    Temporal sub-layers, which would allow dropping frames without breaking anything, were checked on 22 August 2026: the Intel low-power encoder does not offer them (7 profiles out of 7), and B-frames cost 67 ms of reordering. So «every abandonment costs a key frame» stands, and the remedy on a line that keeps abandoning is to lower the frame rate, not to send keys in a loop.

    5.12 · Canvas changes: ADATTA_TELA, TELA and VISTA

    ADATTA_TELA is the only message that changes the canvas. Since 17 August 2026 the page sends it only at attach and re-attach, with the size of its own window — live resizing left the product (DECISIONI.md §5.1-bis). The protocol still admits it at any time, from anyone, and the server must always answer.

    Bodies
    ADATTA_TELA                        client → server
 ├── u32 larghezza      width
 └── u32 altezza        height
TELA                               server → client
 ├── u8  esito          outcome: 1 = ADATTATA (adapted), 2 = RIFIUTATA (refused)
 ├── u8  motivo         reason: 0 if adapted; 1 = COMPOSITORE_INCAPACE (compositor
 │                      cannot), 2 = MISURA_FUORI_LIMITI (size out of limits),
 │                      3 = NON_ORA (not now)
 ├── u32 tela_larghezza the canvas in force AFTER this message
 └── u32 tela_altezza
VISTA (view)                       client → server
 ├── u32 larghezza      any size from 1x1, odd included
 └── u32 altezza
    1. Admissible size. rcp_misura_ammessa() (admissible size) brings each side over the maximum to the maximum and truncates to even; below 320×240 → TELA(RIFIUTATA, MISURA_FUORI_LIMITI). The decoder cap of the client also applies. The guard is mandatory: beyond 16 384 per side gnome-shell dies, and labwc at 32768×32768 dies with no log line (14 August 2026).
    2. The request goes to the stage through the ritela hook («re-canvas»). Its true means only «asked»: labwc answers success for a size it already has without any event, and a compositor may grant another size. No hook → TELA(RIFIUTATA, COMPOSITORE_INCAPACE).
    3. The proof is a frame. The child answers with the size asked and the size obtained (rcp_tela_dal_palco(), «canvas from the stage»); TELA(ADATTATA) leaves when a frame at the new size exists, which opens the key-frame debt and the one-second grace. Zero obtained → NON_ORA at once.
    4. The answer is never silence. If no proof arrives within RCP_TELA_ATTESA_MS (wait) = 3000 ms the server answers NON_ORA; the child can postpone that deadline while the stage is still being born (rcp_tela_rimanda(), «postpone»), which cured black bands after a logout on 16 August 2026. Resizing itself took 41.6 ms on Mutter and 5.1 ms on labwc (14 August 2026).
    5. A stage elsewhere on its own is recalled to the canvas in force every RCP_TELA_RICHIAMO_MS (recall) = 500 ms, doubling up to RCP_TELA_RICHIAMO_MAX_MS = 8000 ms. An unsolicited TELA is forbidden — except one, before the first frame of the session has left (since 22 September 2026): after a server restart a KWin --virtual stage that cannot resize would otherwise leave the screen black forever.

    The grace second. After TELA(ADATTATA) the server accepts for TELA_GRAZIA (canvas grace) = 1000 ms input coordinates valid on the previous canvas, clamping them to the new one and logging it; after that they are violations. It is the only moment when the two sides legitimately hold two truths. rcp_tela_adattata_ora() («canvas adapted, now») opens it; rcp_tela_adattata() has no clock and declares that it does not.

    VISTA updates the view and must not change the canvas; in RCP/1 it does not even change what is encoded — the server sends the whole canvas and the client scales. The server validates it, keeps it for the bit budget and logs it. DISPOSIZIONE (layout; 0x0009, one string in the ATTACCA form) changes the keyboard layout without detaching; an unknown but well-formed layout is logged and the previous one stays in force, because the open work is worth more than the fault. The current page sends neither: the layout and the window size are renegotiated at each attach.

    5.13 · RCP input messages

    The input channel is one unidirectional stream opened by the client after SESSIONE. Every message starts with the same two fields; the five types have fixed lengths.

    Input bodies (0x0101–0x0105): PUNTATORE = pointer, PULSANTE = button, ROTELLA = wheel, LETTERA = character, POSIZIONE_TASTO = key position; codice = code, premuto = pressed, asse = axis, carattere = character
    common:          u32 id        increasing over the whole channel, starts at 1; 0 is reserved
                 u64 istante   microseconds of the CLIENT's monotonic clock
PUNTATORE        + u32 x · u32 y              canvas pixel indices        (20 bytes)
PULSANTE         + u16 codice · u8 premuto    evdev code; 1 down, 0 up    (15 bytes)
ROTELLA          + i32 asse_x · i32 asse_y    120 units per notch         (20 bytes)
LETTERA          + u32 carattere              Unicode scalar value        (16 bytes)
POSIZIONE_TASTO  + u16 codice · u8 premuto    evdev key code              (15 bytes)
    • Codes are evdev's (BTN_LEFT = 0x110, KEY_A = 30): libei works in evdev, and any other convention would add a translation table that fails in silence.
    • Coordinates are canvas pixel indices: 0 ≤ x < width; on 1920×1080 the bottom-right pixel is 1919, 1079. The client converts from its view rounding down; the server applies no transformation and rejects out-of-range values, except during the grace second.
    • The wheel uses 120 units per notch and half notches (60) must not be rounded away. The sign was measured on 10 August 2026 on Mutter: the client sends +120 when the user turns the wheel up, and the server must invert the vertical axis before ei_device_scroll_discrete. The inversion happens once, inside input_rotella() (wheel input) — never in rcp.c, where a second inversion would cancel it.
    • LETTERA for text, POSIZIONE_TASTO when a command modifier is held (Ctrl, Alt, Super); Shift and AltGr make letters and stay on the LETTERA path. A character outside 0..0x10FFFF or a surrogate is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO; a character the session's layout cannot produce is logged and never replaced by another.
    • The id grows by at least one per message across all five types — it is what comes back in the frame's input field — and premuto other than 0 or 1 is a violation.
    • The istante is consumed by no rule; it records when the hand moved, for diagnosis. The page writes real microseconds (performance.now() has 5 µs grain when the page is cross-origin isolated).
    !
    Release everything at detach. when a connection ends — farewell, silence or error — the server must release every key and button still down. A Ctrl left pressed in a session that survives the client makes the desktop unusable at the next attach, and nobody connects the two. The input_rilascia_tutto hook («release everything») answers a true count, RCP_RILASCIO_SENZA_CONTO (release without a count: asked; the child knows the count and logs it) or RCP_RILASCIO_IMPOSSIBILE (release impossible: could not ask: whatever was down stays down). Until 16 August 2026 it answered 0, logged as «nothing was down», while the child released two.

    5.14 · Cursor shape and clipboard messages

    The pointer position belongs to the client, which draws the pointer itself; only the shape travels, on the control channel. The clipboard is plain UTF-8 text in both directions, announced first and pulled on demand.

    Cursor shape
    CURSORE_FORMA   0x000A   cursor shape; server → client, control channel
 ├── u16 larghezza      width <= 256; 0 with altezza 0 = hidden cursor
 ├── u16 altezza        height <= 256
 ├── i16 attivo_x       hotspot, 0 <= attivo_x < larghezza; 0 when hidden
 ├── i16 attivo_y
 └── image              larghezza x altezza x 4 bytes, premultiplied BGRA, no row padding
                        message length = 8 + larghezza x altezza x 4 exactly

    rcp_cursore_forma() (cursor shape) takes the number of bytes really available behind the image and refuses to send rather than read on trust: a malformed message would make the page close the session, and the server's log would know nothing. The limits themselves are enforced once, in cursore.c. The function is called from the loop thread, never from PipeWire's real-time thread.

    Clipboard messages (APPUNTI = clipboard: ANNUNCIO = announcement, CHIEDI = request, TESTO = text; trasferimento = transfer, lunghezza = length)
    APPUNTI_ANNUNCIO  0x0201  ├── u32 trasferimento   chosen by whoever announces, from 1
                          └── u32 lunghezza       bytes of text available
APPUNTI_CHIEDI    0x0202  └── u32 trasferimento   the announcement being answered
APPUNTI_TESTO     0x0203  ├── u32 trasferimento   the request being served
                          └── bytes               to the end of the message, valid UTF-8
    • Each side numbers its own transfers; an APPUNTI_CHIEDI matching no live announcement, or an unrequested APPUNTI_TESTO, is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO. A request that arrives after a newer announcement is served with the current text and logged — two people copying is a race, not an error.
    • The transfer id exists because the three messages travel in both directions on unidirectional streams: without it two transfers open at once in opposite directions swapped their texts (finding R1.11).
    • Cap RCP_APPUNTI_TETTO (clipboard cap) = 1 000 000 bytes, not 1 MiB, so that a text exactly at the cap still fits in a 1 MiB message with its 10 bytes of overhead. Longer text is not announced at all, and logged: a truncated text pasted into a terminal is worse than a missing one.
    • One stream per message (DECISIONI.md §5-ter.7): an announcement and its text can be far apart in time, and a stream kept open between them would stay open forever in most cases. The server keeps at most A_STREAM_MAX = 8 clipboard streams alive and drops the oldest idle one, logged; pending paste requests time out after APPUNTI_FONDO (clipboard deadline) = 8000 ms.

    5.15 · Audio datagrams

    Audio travels only on datagrams, one block per datagram, with no retransmission and no reordering: the receiver discards blocks that arrive after ones already played.

    Audio datagram header (12 bytes), after the WebTransport prefix
     0      2      4                12
 ├──────┼──────┼────────────────┼── samples …
 │ tipo │codec │ istante        │
 │ u16  │ u16  │ u64            │

    PCM is little-endian on purpose: it is payload, like the HEVC bytes, not a protocol field — the only declared exception to network order. Its 5-ms blocks are a correction of 9 August 2026: at 20 ms a PCM datagram would have been 3852 bytes and would never have left on any network, and PCM is the positive control for Opus. A datagram shorter than 12 bytes or with another tipo is discarded and logged, not fatal (exception 2). Volume does not travel: it belongs to the session (invariant I5).

    5.16 · The bench marker: BANCO_MARCA

    BANCO_MARCA (bench marker) and BANCO_ESITO (bench outcome) were added on the night of 9 August 2026 for the latency bench: the bench asks the server to paint a 16×16 square of a given colour after a known delay, and checks that the measured median rises by exactly that delay.

    Bodies
    BANCO_MARCA   0x000F   client → server
 ├── u32 id          grows by at least 1; 0 reserved
 ├── u32 colore      colour, 0x00RRGGBB
 └── u32 ritardo_ms  delay, 0..10000
BANCO_ESITO   0x0010   server → client
 ├── u32 id
 ├── u8  esito       outcome: 1 = ACCETTATA (accepted), 2 = RIFIUTATA (refused)
 ├── u8  motivo      reason: 0; 1 = FUNZIONE_SPENTA (function off),
 │                   2 = RITARDO_FUORI_LIMITI (delay out of range)
 └── u64 istante     server microseconds when painted; 0 if refused

    In the product BANCO_ACCESO (bench on) is 0: ECCOMI declares banco.marca=no, and every BANCO_MARCA in state attiva is answered BANCO_ESITO(RIFIUTATA, FUNZIONE_SPENTA) — or RITARDO_FUORI_LIMITI above 10 000 ms — never silence and never a close. The accepting branch has never been completed: the known-delay check of phase 3 was done outside the product (N = 25 → +25.08 ms, N = 60 → +58.58 ms) and is better that way, because the clock anchor does not pass through the injected path.

    !
    Present, not absent. DECISIONI.md §7.16 (11 August 2026) says the bench function must be absent from the delivered binary — not compiled, not findable by searching its marks. The code still compiles it in, switched off. Not settled yet: whether to complete the accepting branch or to remove the two types, whose only declared reason was met without them.

    5.17 · TERMINA_SESSIONE: logging out

    TERMINA_SESSIONE (end the session; 0x0011, empty body) is the only message by which the client ends the session: the graphical session finishes and the user's programs close. CONGEDO closes only the connection and leaves the session alive (invariant I4). The two exits are DECISIONI.md §4.1-ter; a client with a single way out would force the user to choose between never leaving and losing their work.

    • The page sends it only after an explicit gesture: the Ctrl+Alt+End shortcut and its confirmation. «Log out» from the desktop's own menu does not pass through here; the child reports it and the parent dismisses every client of that user with SESSIONE_TERMINATA (session ended).
    • Valid only in states attiva or staccata-per-silenzio; elsewhere ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO.
    • The answer is CONGEDO(0x10 SESSIONE_TERMINATA), sent before the session finishes dying — when the compositor falls the stage falls with it — and then the termina_sessione hook is called. All connections of that user receive it, not just the one that asked. Without the hook the client is still dismissed with 0x10 and the log says the session was not touched.
    • There is no «terminating» reply: the outcome is the farewell. A client that receives 0x10 must not re-attach; it would open a new session, not find the old one. The page returns to the login form.

    5.18 · RCP: the farewell

    Whoever closes must send CONGEDO with a reason before closing the WebTransport session, if the control channel is still usable, and must repeat the reason in the session's application error code. The second road has no condition: it travels inside the close itself. The farewell is always verified from the side that receives it.

    Body
    CONGEDO   0x000C   both directions
 ├── u8     motivo     a reason of the table below (code 0 is forbidden)
 └── string dettaglio  detail, for the log, never shown to the user; may be empty
    • The condition (DECISIONI.md §7.15, decided by the user on 11 August 2026): «if a connection drops nobody can tell the server I am closing because I have finished». A rule that cannot be obeyed is a defect of the document; what is lost is only a byte on a dead channel, and the reason still arrives by the second road.
    • Whoever receives a FIN is not «whoever closes» and sends nothing more on any channel (§7.14). The decision was made by a measurement: on 10 August 2026 Chrome dropped a message sent just before closing the session, so a farewell owed by the receiver would have been a rule one engine out of two cannot honour.
    • The one exception is RESPINTO, which is itself the farewell of authentication.
    • The page builds the sentence from the code; dettaglio is for whoever diagnoses. Every reason must be expressible to the user as a sentence: BUDGET_PIENO is not «error 6».
    • A second farewell is never sent. rcp_congeda() (dismiss) on a session already ended does nothing: two reasons for one fact would be two truths. Bytes arriving after the end are judged by giudica_dopo_la_fine(): a single CONGEDO is a legitimate leave-taking, anything more is logged.
    • The seat is released immediately on a client close (rcp_chiusa_dal_client(), «closed by the client»), without waiting for the transport to finish tearing down — otherwise whoever reconnects at once would find it taken.

    5.19 · Disconnect reasons

    The reasons are a single numbering shared by CONGEDO, RESPINTO and the WebTransport closing code (enum in rcp.h).

    0x01 and 0x10 describe two gestures with opposite outcomes: the wire that falls carries the promise «re-attach and you find everything», the logout makes that promise false. 0x0F is the remote twin of 0x05 and applies invariant I2 to the letter: the second connection is refused with an explicit message. The boundary with «whoever is silent is detached» is the silence clock: a client silent for 30 s holds nothing, so the newcomer enters; the declared price is that after a laptop dies without a farewell the phone enters after 30 s — 15 s with the ghost eviction.

    i
    Range check. the server accepts a CONGEDO or a closing code from the client only in 0x01–0x0F (motivo_di_82(), «a reason of §8.2», and the range check in webtransport.c): a client sending 0x10 would be treated as ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO, although §8.2 defines it. Harmless today — only the server sends 0x10 — but it is a divergence from the specification.

    5.20 · RCP: session clocks

    Three clocks govern an attached session (SPECIFICHE.md §5.3), and a fourth rule shortens the first one when somebody is waiting for the seat. The values in force are written to the log at start-up, because a one-hour ceiling cannot be verified by waiting an hour.

    The ghost eviction exists because on 23 August 2026 a client killed with -9 kept its seat for 30.5 s and eleven reconnection attempts were refused with «you already have a session elsewhere» — about the user's own dead session. Lowering the silence clock to 10 s would have broken a reader who only watches: the browser's keep-alive was measured at 15 s. The eviction acts only within the same user (across users it would be a security hole), only when someone is asking, and never below 15 s, the point beyond which no live client was ever measured. Measured on 23–24 August 2026: the ghost went from 32.13 s and 14 refusals to 16.83 s and 7.

    i
    Inactivity counts more than input. SPECIFICHE.md §5.3 defines inactivity as «what the user sends, not what they watch». The code refreshes the 30-minute clock on any RCP byte from the client, so automatic messages such as RICHIEDI_CHIAVE also keep it alive; the 60-minute abandonment clock counts only the five input gestures.

    5.21 · Versions and how RCP grows

    The major version lives in two places, and they must coincide: the path /rcp/1 and the versione field of CIAO. A CIAO(2) on /rcp/1 is VERSIONE_INCOMPATIBILE, not a negotiation.

    • The path is the most upstream place where the server can say «I do not speak this version», since ALPN is h3 and belongs to the browser. An unknown path gets 404. The check in CIAO remains mandatory: a path can be typed by hand, and a check that can be bypassed by typing is not a check.
    • Within a major version RCP grows only through capabilities — never by adding fields to existing messages or new types the old side would have to ignore, because ignoring is forbidden. A new mandatory type is a new major version.
    • The window in which the document could still be completed closed with the first byte of code, 10 August 2026. It let through four types (RICHIEDI_CHIAVE, TELA, BANCO_MARCA, BANCO_ESITO) and three reasons (TEMPO_SCADUTO, SESSIONE_NON_SERVIBILE, GIA_ATTIVA_REMOTA).
    !
    A type added after the window closed. TERMINA_SESSIONE (0x0011) and SESSIONE_TERMINATA (0x10) entered on 15 August 2026, after the window had closed, without a version change. Client and server are updated together today, so nothing breaks; but RCP.md §9 still says the window let through only four types and three reasons, and does not record this exception.

    5.22 · What RCP does not do

    What RCP/1 deliberately leaves out, so that nobody looks for it on the wire.

    5.23 · Testing against the specification

    Client and server are tested against the specification, not against each other. The decisive tool is the wire validator, a third program that reads a recording of a connection and says which byte does not conform.

    Recording format (RCP.md §11.1)
    header (16 bytes)
 ├── 8 bytes  magic          "RCPREG" 0x00 0x03
 ├── u32      block count
 ├── u8       clock          1 = client's, 2 = server's
 └── u8[3]    reserved, 0
each block
 ├── u8  direction (1 c→s, 2 s→c) · u8 channel (high byte) · u8 end (0 continues, 1 FIN, 2 RESET_STREAM)
 ├── u32 istante_ms          milliseconds since the first block, recorder's monotonic clock
 ├── u64 stream · u32 length (the TRUE length)
 ├── u16 redacted ranges, each: u32 start · u32 count · 32-byte SHA-256 of the true bytes
 └── payload (redacted bytes replaced by 0x2A)

    The format solves one problem: recording the bytes as they were would put the password in a file, and replacing it while keeping or rewriting the length would make the validator either fail forever or validate a document rewritten by the bench. So the true length is kept, the secret bytes are replaced by 0x2A (not zeros, which a field can legitimately contain) and the file declares which ranges are redacted, with their fingerprint. The end byte (added 12 August 2026) lets the validator tell an abandoned frame from a truncated one; istante_ms (magic 0x03, 21 August 2026) lets it judge the grace second in one direction: if a client-side recording shows more than 1000 ms between TELA and a stale coordinate, the server should have refused; below that it says «not judgeable», because a referee that stays silent acquits. Old validators refuse new files instead of reading them askew; all recorders and readers in banchi/ are now at 0x03.

    Chapter 6

    Screen capture per compositor

    6.1 · Capture at a glance

    REMOTIX does not grab the physical screen: every session has its own virtual output, and the capture reads that output from the compositor that draws it. There are three compositor families behind the four desktops, and they deliver frames in two opposite directions. GNOME and KDE push frames through a PipeWire node; labwc (the compositor REMOTIX runs under XFCE and LXQt) has no node at all, and frames are pulled one by one. All three end up behind one interface, cattura.h (capture), which the per-user child process (figlio.c) uses in the same way on every desktop.

    Which family is in use is decided once per process by sessione_desktop() (see ch. 12 “The four desktops”); there is no per-compositor switch inside the capture. Where a compositor cannot do something (KWin cannot resize its virtual output), the behaviour is the same for everyone that cannot: the stream keeps its size and the page rescales.

    6.2 · The capture contract

    The capture has one job, written at the top of cattura.h: deliver a frame with the declared buffer type, never a deduced one. Three rules from REMOTIX v1 survived the rewrite, and each one exists because breaking it produces no error at all.

    The negotiated facts are exposed in CatturaConsegna (capture delivery; read with cattura_consegna()), four groups that the code downstream reads instead of recomputing:

    • buffer type — requested (strada_chiesta, buffer_chiesto) and declared by the producer (buffer_dichiarato), in separate fields: what arrives is the answer to the question REMOTIX asked, not a discovery about the compositor;
    • bits per channel — from the negotiated format; 0 means unknown and is written as 0;
    • geometry — size, the stride read from the chunk (stride_letto says whether it is a fact or still empty), the DRM modifier;
    • colour — range, matrix, transfer and primaries as the producer declares them, “not declared” included; plus what REMOTIX measures itself on the pixels (min/max per channel, black, uniform).

    The pixel measurement (misura_i_pixel()) is diagnostic only. It runs on the first frame and then at most every MISURA_PIXEL_OGNI_MS = 500 ms, because on 22 Aug 2026 it cost 5.34 ms of a 21.61 ms capture-to-bytes path (25 %) on the test server at 1920×1080, to fill one log line. pixel_misurati sits beside the results so that “not black” and “not looked at” cannot be confused. Sampling one pixel in eight (0.10 ms) was measured and rejected: a frame black except for one region would be reported as black.

    !
    Real-time thread. the PipeWire callbacks run on PipeWire's own real-time thread (pw_thread_loop). Nothing may wait inside them, cattura_ferma() must not be called from the end callback, and the pixels live only for the duration of the callback: the copy into REMOTIX's buffer is made there, and frames that arrive while nobody is waiting are only counted, not copied.

    CatturaFermo (the captured frame) also carries the timing of the part of the path that precedes the encoder, in microseconds of CLOCK_MONOTONIC (the same clock as figlio.c and codificatore.c): us_arrivo (when the frame was parked), us_copia (the memcpy in the callback), us_allocazione (0 when the buffer was reused), us_nel_posto (how long the frame waited for a taker) and us_misura. They were added in phase 8 because about 16 ms of a 30.37 ms capture-to-first-byte path had no owner.

    The damage regions (SPA_META_VideoDamage) are information about how much changed, not a condition for reading the buffer. v1 believed Mutter repainted only the damaged part of recycled buffers; on 12 Aug 2026 (Mutter 48.7, memory path, 410 frames) damage was partial on every frame and the SMPTE bars were whole in every one. The buffer is always complete.

    6.3 · GNOME: the Mutter D-Bus sequence

    On GNOME REMOTIX talks to Mutter's direct D-Bus interfaces, org.gnome.Mutter.RemoteDesktop and org.gnome.Mutter.ScreenCast, not to xdg-desktop-portal: the portal asks permission of a user sitting at the screen, and a headless session has nobody there. It is also the path gnome-remote-desktop uses.

    The order admits no permutation, and each wrong order is punished with a different message that never says “wrong order”: starting the control session before step 2 gives “Remote desktop session already started”; starting the capture with Session.Start gives “Must be started from remote desktop session”. Closing follows the same logic in reverse: mutter_chiudi() stops the control session and the capture follows it. The PipeWire node is announced by a signal emitted during Stream.Start, so mutter.c subscribes before calling it (without a sender filter, to avoid the window in which GDBus resolves the owner of a name).

    The virtual monitor is mounted by the program every time the stage is mounted, never by configuration. In v1 the GNOME branch lost width and height and the monitor lived in a provisioning script; on 12 Aug 2026 a session ran for two days alive, complete and black. Putting the protection in the program means removing it takes intent.

    Our monitor is identified by name, never by index or size. On the test server there were two virtual monitors, Meta-0 («MetaVirtualMonitor», the session's) and Meta-1 («Virtual remote monitor», ours), both 1920×1080@60. mutter_monitor_cerca() compares the connectors before and after RecordVirtual and the product name; if the two do not agree on exactly one new monitor, the answer is “unknown”, not a guess. It must be called once the stream is active: measured, the monitor does not exist after RecordVirtual, nor three seconds after Stream.Start — Mutter creates it when a consumer actually starts reading.

    !
    Scale guard. with org.gnome.desktop.interface scaling-factor = 2 the stream keeps the requested pixels but the logical monitor gets scale 2.0, and its layout is the coordinate space of input: the pointer lands elsewhere with no log line. mutter_scala_nostra() reads the scale of our monitor (a HiDPI laptop panel is not a defect); if it is not 1.0 the child refuses the stage and logs the one-line cure. A scale that cannot be read (−1) is declared and the session proceeds.

    The bus connection belongs to the MutterSessione and is lent out by mutter_bus(): the clipboard uses the same RemoteDesktop session (a second connection would be a second sender that Mutter does not recognise as the owner). The input channel opened here with ConnectToEIS and its recovery mutter_eis_riattacca() are described in ch. 10 “Input”.

    6.4 · KDE: the KWin screencast protocol

    On Plasma the capture is a Wayland request to KWin: the private protocol zkde_screencast_unstable_v1 (version 5 on KWin 6.3.6), asked for the output Virtual-0, answers with the id of a PipeWire node. From the node on, the path is the GNOME one: cattura_avvia(node).

    The gate. KWin announces zkde_screencast_unstable_v1 only to a client whose executable (/proc/<pid>/exe, canonical) appears in the Exec= line of a .desktop file that lists the protocol in X-KDE-Wayland-Interfaces. Measured on 18 Sep 2026 in the kde test box: without the file the global is absent (58 others are there), with the file it appears, even when written while the session is running. Since phase 17 the package installs /usr/share/applications/org.kde.remotix.desktop and the server only verifies it at startup with kwin_verifica_permesso() (file present, Exec= pointing to the running binary, protocol declared); it never writes it. The child is an execve of the same binary, so it is the process KWin recognises. KWin's environment also needs XDG_MENU_PREFIX=plasma-, or its service index is built empty.

    The size. KWin on a machine without a seat starts only with the --virtual backend, and there the output is decided by the command line: kwin_wayland_wrapper --xwayland --virtual --width W --height H --no-lockscreen, written by sessione.c with the size of the client that creates the session. A virtual output cannot be resized afterwards, so misura_del_palco() captures the size KWin reports (kwin_misura()) and logs that the page will rescale.

    The cursor. The mode is fixed for the life of the stream; REMOTIX asks for metadata (4), like Mutter. The price is that every pointer movement produces a buffer without new pixels marked SPA_CHUNK_FLAG_CORRUPTED; cattura.c discards those and counts them as solo_cursore. With --virtual KWin draws the pointer into the image, so the session runs with REMOTIX's encoded cursor theme (6.10 “The encoded cursor theme”), and the child calls cattura_cursore_mai_nascondere(): an empty metadata image is never forwarded as “hidden”, otherwise the page would remove the browser's own pointer too (the user's test of 20 Sep 2026: “the pointer is gone”). The declared price: on Plasma an application that hides the cursor does not hide it for the viewer.

    6.5 · PipeWire negotiation, resize and wake-up

    On GNOME and KDE the capture is a PipeWire consumer created by cattura_avvia() on the node the compositor announced. Everything is declared in the format proposal (proposta()) and in the consumption parameters (parametri_di_consumo()).

    i
    The card that refuses linear. NVIDIA with GNOME 50 (6 Oct 2026): the proposal LINEAR + INVALID ended in «no more input formats» — Mutter agreed on INVALID, could not allocate it and withdrew it — and the session was black. Now modificatori_per_la_strada() asks the card whether it refuses a linear render buffer (vulkanvideo_scheda_rifiuta_il_lineare()); only then it passes the modifiers the Vulkan encoder can import to cattura_modificatori_scheda(), and they are proposed between LINEAR and INVALID. Measured: modifier 0x300000000606014 agreed, zero copy. On Intel and Radeon the proposal is unchanged.

    Buffer generation. Every time PipeWire reallocates its buffers (renegotiation, wake-up) su_buffer_aggiunto()/su_buffer_tolto() change a generation counter that travels with every frame (generazione). The encoder caches the import of each DMA-BUF, and file descriptor numbers are recycled: a cache keyed on the descriptor alone would hand the encoder a surface pointing to a freed buffer, i.e. an old image, with no error. When the generation changes, the cache is thrown away.

    Retention. On the GPU path the pw_buffer is kept until cattura_fermo_libera(), which the child calls only after codificatore_comprimi_scheda() has returned — after the GPU has finished reading, not after the work was queued. Releasing earlier is the defect recorded in LEZIONI.md §8: two screens alternating and no error. rendi_ritenuta() gives the buffer back only if its generation is still current.

    Resizing a live stream

    cattura_ridimensiona() rebuilds the proposal at the new size and calls pw_stream_update_params() — what gnome-remote-desktop does — without touching the session or the virtual monitor. It returns CATTURA_RITELA_CHIESTA, CATTURA_RITELA_GIA_COSI (the size is already in force: renegotiating it would chase its own tail) or CATTURA_RITELA_GUASTO. “Requested” is not “done”: the truth is told by the next frame at the new size, a rule taken from neatvnc. Measured with banchi/04-in8-misura.c on 14 Aug 2026: first new frame after 41.6 ms on Mutter, no black, 20 resizes in 2 s all exact; 5.1 ms and 0 lost frames out of 25 on labwc. A size the producer cannot hold kills the stream about 2 ms later («no more input formats», PipeWire 1.4.2); cattura_prendi() looks at the state before waiting, so the failure surfaces in one loop turn (8.1 ms measured) instead of a timeout. The size rule itself (320×240 to 4096×2304, even sides, larger requests reduced) lives in rcp_misura_ammessa(), see ch. 5 “The RCP/1 protocol”.

    Waking a still desktop

    A Wayland compositor delivers only when the scene changes, and a desktop just started is still. Measured on 14 Aug 2026: 4.4 s between login and the first frame, with a key request every 200 ms and 659 empty waits. Wayland has no “repaint now”, but restarting the stream makes a buffer arrive. cattura_risveglia() repeats the current parameters at the negotiated size; on labwc it asks for the next frame whole (wlr_forza_intero()). The child calls it only when a keyframe is owed and the capture returned zero, and at most every RISVEGLIO_MS = 400 ms.

    !
    Wake-up and held buttons. on Mutter the renegotiation recreates the absolute input devices (viewports-changed → remove_viewport_devices(), which does not go through drop_device()). Measured with banchi/06-b33-risveglio.c: three wake-ups, three device replacements. If a button is held at that moment it stays pressed inside Mutter and the desktop never takes another click. The child therefore does not wake the stream while input_premuti() reports a key or button held; the price, declared, is that a client just attached may see a blank page until the user lets go.

    When the compositor refuses the GPU path. In a machine without 3D acceleration (a VM with virtio-vga without virgl) the compositor renders in software and has no DMA-BUF to offer; the GPU proposal dies with «no more input formats» (measured 29 Sep 2026 on 7 VMs out of 7). cattura_formato_rifiutato() recognises the facts (stream in error with no format ever agreed, or a format agreed and no frame ever delivered) and cattura_avvia() returns G_IO_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED when it sees the refusal itself. ripiega_se_rifiutata() in the child then switches to memory, logs it, and never tries the GPU again in that process. The two paths are never offered together: the compositor would choose, and zero copy would be lost where it works. Silence (no frame in 5 s) does not trigger the fallback; only a refusal does.

    6.6 · XFCE and LXQt: wlroots screencopy

    labwc has no PipeWire node. It offers zwlr_screencopy_manager_v1 (version 3), and every frame is a full round trip: capture_output → buffer → copy → ready. The frame rate is therefore REMOTIX's loop, not a property of the compositor — the user's decision of 20 Sep 2026 (“we ask for them”), which also bought control of the pointer and of the output size.

    Why a separate module. cattura.c was built on the push direction and figlio.c uses it in dozens of places; rewriting them two ways would have put GNOME and KDE at risk to serve the new desktops. The shape copies the clipboard's precedent (appunti_apri() / appunti_apri_kde()): a second constructor, cattura_avvia_wlr(), and every public function of cattura.c hands over to wlroots.c at the top when the capture is a wlroots one. Everything downstream (cattura_prendi(), cattura_consegna(), the counters) sees no difference.

    The first draft of wlroots.c passed its bench (530 frames) and still had seven defects; they were found by an adversarial review on 21 Sep 2026 and shaped the file: wrong format numbering, frames thrown away at every timeout, three unbounded wl_display_roundtrip calls, failed and cancelled in one branch, head discovery depending on event order, a configuration enabling one head only, and leaks on close.

    6.7 · Slabs: zero copy on labwc

    On labwc the zero-copy path is a copy into a DMA-BUF that REMOTIX owns: a “slab” (lastra) is a GBM buffer allocated on the compositor's render node, its DMA-BUF descriptor and the wl_buffer that names it. It is enabled by wlr_chiedi_la_scheda(), which says no in writing if it cannot, leaving memory as a declared fallback.

    • Three slabs (WLR_LASTRE): one in hand, one in flight, one as cheap insurance (8 MB at 1080p). If all are in hand the frame stops and says so; a slab in hand is never recycled.
    • Linear modifier. The linux_dmabuf event carries format and size, not modifiers, so slabs are LINEAR, which every card can read and write. The exception is a card whose GBM refuses LINEAR|RENDERING (NVIDIA, driver 595): there the slab is allocated with one of the modifiers the Vulkan encoder imports (measured 5 Oct 2026 on an RTX 4090: 0 of 34 frames before the cure, 28 of 28 after; about 22 ms capture-to-bytes at 60/s against about 90 ms and 11/s from memory).
    • Exact format. The slab is allocated in exactly the format and size of the linux_dmabuf event; anything else is invalid buffer, a protocol error that kills the connection.
    • Synchronisation. wlroots ends the blit with glFlush() and sends ready at once, and labwc offers no explicit-sync protocol. After ready REMOTIX extracts the fence from the DMA-BUF (DMA_BUF_IOCTL_EXPORT_SYNC_FILE with DMA_BUF_SYNC_READ) and poll()s it; the wait is us_attesa_gpu. Without the ioctl (kernel older than 5.20) it is said once and implicit sync is trusted.
    • Generation. Every slab that is born or dies changes the generation, for the same descriptor reuse reason as on PipeWire.
    • Switching off. Three consecutive failed on the GPU path (WLR_SCHEDA_FALLITI_MAX) turn it off, and the log says so; the first slab birth may take up to WLR_LASTRA_NASCITA_S = 1 s.
    !
    Slabs and the Radeon GPU hang. when the encoder is Vulkan, slabs are born at the maximum canvas, WLR_LASTRA_L × WLR_LASTRA_A = 4096×2304, and a resize changes only the wl_buffer, never the GBM object. On the Radeon, GBM (radeonsi) and Vulkan (RADV) in the same process share one amdgpu_device, one GPU address space; freeing a GBM buffer right before a new Vulkan encoder is created at the new size caused a page fault inside the new input image, VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST and a MODE1 reset of the card for everybody (a driver defect, avoided here). Measured on 1 Oct 2026 (test F-018, LXQt, Radeon RX 6800, Vulkan): 10 faults in 14 runs with slabs freed on resize, 0 in 5 with slabs kept, 0 in 5 on the memory path. The cost is 3 × 4096 × 2304 × 4 = 113 MB per session even at 1080p, so it applies only when the child's encoder is Vulkan: lastre_per_la_strada() decides once, before the first stage, through wlr_lastre_alla_tela_massima(). With VA-API the slabs keep the canvas size.

    6.8 · Zero copy and the memory fallback

    “Zero copy” means the frame never leaves the GPU between the compositor and the encoder. It is the default (COPIA_ZERO = 1 in figlio.c; a build-time -DCOPIA_ZERO=0 exists only to rebuild the “before” for A/B benches, it is not a product switch). It is not zero work: the RGB→YUV conversion still happens, on the GPU.

    Why it matters, measured inside the product on 22 Aug 2026 (test server, 1920×1080, 2,450 frames, HEVC on the GPU): on the old memory path the frame left the GPU, was copied (1.65 ms), converted in CPU (8.15 ms) and uploaded again (1.16 ms) — 10.96 ms of an 18.86 ms path, 58 %. After zero copy (phase 8, same day, alternated A/B runs): capture → bytes out 6.41 ms, with copy 0.00, conversion on the GPU 2.98 and upload 0.00; the user's measure of pointer lag dropped to 0.16 title-bar heights, 1.23 times the local desktop (0.13). Those numbers were taken with libavcodec; phase 18 later showed the GPU path gives identical bytes and times without it (7.12 “Removing ffmpeg and the CPU path”).

    The 64-byte stride. The Intel iHD driver, importing a DMA-BUF, does not honour a stride that is not a multiple of 64 bytes: it reads rows at its own pitch and the desktop comes out blurred and slanted while the milliseconds look perfect. Measured on 22 Aug 2026 with the certified mark reader (banchi/03-marca.py): 1920×1080 (stride 7680) and 1552×888 (6208) read with contrast 1.000; 1544×888 (6176) and 1560×888 (6240) do not read (0.617 and 0.510). 1552 and 1544 are eight pixels apart with opposite verdicts. The colour statistics of the two streams matched within 0.17 levels out of 255 while the mark was readable on 0 frames out of 869: an instrument looking at averages says green on this defect. The producer makes the stride equal to width × 4, so the code refuses the path and declares it, rather than sending a wrong image.

    Remounting only the capture. Switching path does not tear down the stage. rimonta_solo_la_cattura() stops and reopens only the Cattura (and its cursor hook), keeping the input channel, the clipboard and the RemoteDesktop session: on 25 Aug 2026 a full teardown 33 ms after the EIS channel was opened crashed the child inside ei_disconnect() (SIGSEGV, core read with gdb). On labwc the capture is the source, so remounting means cattura_ferma() and cattura_avvia_wlr().

    i
    One frame rate, short waits. the frame rate is one number, MOVIMENTO_FPS = 60, used both for the capture maximum and for the encoder; the capture asked 60 and the encoder declared 30 until both were tied to the same name. The child waits MOVIMENTO_ATTESA_S = 8 ms per turn: it was 250 ms, and on a still desktop a click could wait up to a quarter of a second in the socket (measured 15 Aug 2026 on 25 real clicks: median 136 ms, worst 502 ms).

    6.9 · The cursor channel

    The pointer is drawn by the page, not baked into the video: the image stays clean (two pointers are worse than one) and the shape travels as a side channel, the CURSORE_FORMA message of RCP/1. The capture's only addition to its interface is cattura_cursore(), which registers the receiver; cursore.c sits between PipeWire and the wire.

    After a hidden period Mutter sends “unchanged” when the pointer comes back, so cursore.c keeps the last visible shape and re-sends it; otherwise the pointer would stay invisible with no error. A cursor larger than 256 would make the receiver close the session with ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO, which is why the limit is enforced on this side. A malformed metadata block is declared in the log and nothing is sent.

    6.10 · The encoded cursor theme

    Until 24 Sep 2026 the real pointer shape (resize arrows on a border, the I-beam on text, the hand on links) reached the browser only on GNOME. The user decided it must reach it on all four desktops, and the design approved was an encoded theme plus a dictionary (forma.h, forma.c, «forma» = shape).

    KWin and labwc draw the pointer into the captured image, so their sessions already ran with an invisible cursor theme made of 1×1 transparent images. The compositor drew nothing, and the metadata carried the same nothing. In the encoded theme each shape is still a 1×1 image, but opaque and of a colour of its own. The server writes the theme before the desktop starts; the child reads the colour and looks up the real image in a real theme on disk.

    The labwc probe. wlr_sonda_puntatore() runs a capture_output_region of 3×3 pixels around the hotspot into a 36-byte wl_shm buffer (3×3 because the normalised virtual pointer lands on a fractional pixel); the centre is checked, then the neighbours. Three rules: only one probe in flight, coalescing to the last position; a plain copy, never with damage; and a tail probe SONDA_CODA_US = 120 ms after the hand stops, because a client changes shape after the enter event that the movement caused. Cost measured on 24 Sep 2026 (LXQt box, 1344×870, pointer at about 55 Hz for 30 s over qterminal): labwc 4.9–5.1 % CPU without the probe, 6.3–6.4 % with it, the child +0.5 points, painted frames unchanged (55.0–55.3/s). Under the 2-point threshold, so thinning (SONDA_MINIMO_US) stays at 0.

    !
    The declared price. the compositor now paints one coloured pixel under the hotspot into the image. The browser's pointer covers it and the encoder smears it; whether it is ever visible is not settled until the user looks. If the real theme is missing, forma_immagine() fails once in the log and the client keeps its own arrow.

    6.11 · Capture constants

    The constants of the capture, where they live and what set them.

    Every capture line in the log carries the area cattura (also from kwin.c and wlroots.c: whoever reads the log looks for pixels under one word). The log line written when the stage is mounted says which path was mounted, because a “conversion 0.9 ms” on the GPU path and one on the memory path are not the same quantity; see ch. 13 “Logging and diagnostics”.

    +
    Benches. the benches that prove these rules are in banchi/: 06-b5-esiti-cattura.c (capture outcomes, resize failures), 04-in8-misura.c (live resize), 06-b33-risveglio.c (wake-up and held buttons), 14-f1-forma.c (every colour of the encoded theme), 03-marca.py (the mark reader used for the stride limit). See ch. 16 “Testing”.
    Chapter 7

    Video encoding

    7.1 · Encoding at a glance

    REMOTIX encodes every frame on the GPU, in H.264 or HEVC, into Annex-B that the browser's WebCodecs VideoDecoder decodes. codificatore.c (the encoder) is the front: it chooses the GPU path by capability — Vulkan Video if the card encodes that codec through Vulkan, VA-API otherwise — and keeps everything that works on the bytes (shape checks, keyframes, the 16 MiB ceiling, quality steps, the level check) in one place for both paths. ffmpeg left the product in phase 18 and the software encoders in phase 19: a server without a capable GPU says so at startup and offers no video codec.

    7.2 · Codecs and their negotiation

    RCP/1 numbers the video codecs in the frame header: 1 = HEVC, 2 = AV1, 3 = H.264. The enum CodecVideo uses the same values so that no conversion table can drift. AV1 is no longer negotiated, but its number is reserved forever: an old client hearing “2” and receiving H.264 would paint garbage without an error.

    What the server offers is measured, not written. At startup main.c calls figlio_capacita_video(), which forks a short-lived process (a driver that crashes must not take the server with it before it has opened its port) that opens each codec through the same codificatore_di() a session uses and encodes a 256×256 test frame until bytes come out (at most 8 attempts). The result is passed to rcp_video_codec_imposta(): hevc,h264, hevc, h264 or empty. With an empty list every CIAO ends in NIENTE_IN_COMUNE and the startup log says why, with the remedy. A browser must never be offered a codec the server cannot keep: negotiating HEVC and then failing to open it was a black screen with no line naming it.

    The codec string the page passes to VideoDecoder.configure() is built by stringhe_codec(): for H.264 avc1.6400 plus the level in hexadecimal (5.1 → avc1.640033; decimal would give the invalid avc1.100051), with avc1.64001f (level 3.1) as second choice; for HEVC hev1.1.6.L<level·30>.B0 (Main) or hev1.2.4… (Main 10), with L93 as second choice. The server composes its own string from the SPS it produced (stringa_codec in the confession): since phase 18 the H.264 SPS sets constraint flags 4 and 5 (High, no B frames), so the server reads for example avc1.640c15 (the 256×256 probe, level 2.1); the profile and level bytes are what decoders use.

    i
    Depth. the H.264 encoder is High, 8 bit only. profilo_va() returns VAProfileNone for H.264 at 10 bits instead of trying (vainfo on the test server lists VAProfileH264High only), and the Vulkan path refuses it in vulkan_adatta(). HEVC is Main or Main 10. The capture is 8 bits per channel on every desktop, so a 10-bit stream would be 8 bits promoted; the confession declares it (promozione_8_a_10).

    7.3 · Choosing the GPU path

    The encoder is asked for by name, and the name says how the path is chosen. A name that is not one of these six is refused by codificatore_nuovo() with the reason; there is no silent fallback to another component, profile or depth, because two measurements under one label are worse than none.

    figlio.c builds the name from the codec and the path in force (componente_di()); the path is scheda (by capability) unless the server was started with --codifica scheda|vulkan|vaapi, which the parent repeats on every child's command line (the child is an exec, a static of the parent would not reach it). The name actually opened — h264_vulkan or h264_vaapi — is what codificatore_nome() and the log report, together with the node, the vendor string and the entry point.

    The node is declared, not guessed. NODO_RENDERING is /dev/dri/renderD128, fixed in figlio.c; no environment variable moves it (a node from a variable would vanish the day someone started the service by hand, and the symptom would be a different encoder under the same label). Only --prova-codifica --nodo … uses another node, to test a second card. On the test server the two nodes are two vendors: renderD128 the Intel iGPU (iHD, VAEntrypointEncSliceLP), renderD129 a Radeon RX 6800 (radeonsi, VAEntrypointEncSlice). Measured 13 Aug 2026 at 1920×1080: Intel 3.16–3.24 ms, Radeon 3.43 ms per frame.

    The VA-API entry point is a declared rule, CODIFICATORE_POTENZA_LA_DICHIARATA: low-power EncSliceLP if the driver declares it for the profile, full EncSlice otherwise, failure if neither. The pair is read with vaQueryConfigEntrypoints() before opening (three outcomes: present, absent, could not look). On the Radeon only EncSlice exists, and with the old fixed low-power request sessions fell back to software. Before opening the driver is also asked for the maximum size (vaGetConfigAttributes(); H.264 on Intel EncSliceLP accepts 32–4096 px per side, measured 22 Aug 2026) and the rate-control modes.

    When opening fails the child does not retry at every frame: the wait doubles from CODIF_RIPROVA_MIN_MS = 500 ms to CODIF_RIPROVA_MAX_MS = 10 s, and the log says the next attempt time (retrying freely once wrote 30.8 GB of log in minutes, 14 Aug 2026). A full card is not a missing codec: on an RTX 4090 (driver 595, 6 Oct 2026) the driver gives 12 encode sessions for the whole card, the thirteenth vkCreateVideoSessionKHR returns VK_ERROR_TOO_MANY_OBJECTS, and the log says “the card is there but has run out of encode slots”; the session gets its first frame by itself when a slot frees.

    The certification probe: remotix --prova-codifica

    The installer asks the product itself whether this machine encodes a frame on the GPU. remotix --prova-codifica [h264|hevc] [--nodo /dev/dri/…] [--codifica vaapi|vulkan|scheda] goes through codificatore_di() (H.264, 8 bits, no level ceiling, BGRx), encodes a 256×256 frame until bytes come out, and prints one JSON line on stdout (the log goes to stderr):

    The probe's answer (shape)
    {"esito":"hardware","codificatore":"h264_vaapi","strada":"vaapi","nodo":"/dev/dri/renderD128",
 "motivo":"…","codec":"h264","offerti":"hevc,h264","hevc":"hardware","h264":"hardware",
 "hevc_strada":"vaapi","h264_strada":"vaapi"}

    esito (outcome) is hardware or nessuno (none); strada is the path that encoded; offerti (offered) is what the server would offer the browser with the same arguments; hevc/h264 and hevc_strada/h264_strada give the same answer per codec. The installer reads esito and the exit code.

    “hardware” is said only if the component accepts GPU surfaces, a frame came out with bytes, and the bytes were read back (letto_dal_flusso, read from the stream). Permissions matter: without the node's group (render) a user sees nessuno (none) where root would see hardware, so the probe must run with the identity in question. How the installer uses it is in ch. 15 “The installer”.

    7.4 · VA-API without libavcodec

    Until phase 18 the VA-API path was libavcodec's h264_vaapi and hevc_vaapi. vadiretta.c talks to libva (MIT) directly and does the four things they did: configure the driver, fill the sequence/picture/slice parameters, write the stream headers, and run begin/render/end for each frame. Its governing rule is to reproduce exactly what ffmpeg 7.1 did, field by field, so that the browser receives the same kind of stream.

    Headers are passed to the driver as packed headers; VaDirettaDichiarazione records the mask the driver declares and the one in force, the surface alignment (16 for H.264, the CTB for HEVC), whether HEVC P frames are coded as generalised-B slices (p_come_b, iHD) and the input fourcc (NV12 or P010).

    i
    Radeon rewrites the headers. on Mesa radeonsi the driver reads REMOTIX's packed headers and regenerates them (measured 30 Sep 2026: log2_max_mv_length 16, transform_8x8 0 in H.264; a VPS without timing, temporal_mvp 0, cabac_init_present 1 in HEVC). It did the same to ffmpeg, so the stream is unchanged. For the same reason the cropping window that Mesa 25.0.7 does not write is fixed afterwards on the bytes (7.8 “Bytes, levels and the confession”).

    7.5 · The Vulkan Video encoder

    Vulkan Video is the path the user asked for first (1 Oct 2026: “with standard tools, preferably Vulkan, which all four architectures share”): the NVIDIA proprietary driver does not encode through VA-API, but every vendor exposes Vulkan Video. vulkanvideo.c uses VK_KHR_video_encode_queue with VK_KHR_video_encode_h264/_h265, the Vulkan loader (Apache-2.0) and the system driver; nothing else.

    NVIDIA and linear buffers. The NVIDIA GBM refuses a LINEAR|RENDERING buffer (vulkanvideo_scheda_rifiuta_il_lineare() asks exactly that); vulkanvideo_modificatori() lists the non-linear modifiers the card can import and sample, and the capture offers them (see 6.5 “PipeWire negotiation, resize and wake-up” and 6.7 “Slabs: zero copy on labwc”). On the RTX 4090 the memory comparison was 12 of 12 good (PSNR 38.6–46.2 dB, 1080p and 4K) before zero copy worked, and 28 of 28 from the GPU after.

    The bench switch. REMOTIX_VULKAN_CONVERSIONE=copia forces the shader to write into an intermediate image that is then copied, even where it could write the encoder's input directly, to measure that branch. It is for benches only; the product's choice is the one read from the driver.

    7.6 · BT.709 colour conversion

    The capture delivers RGB, the encoders want YUV 4:2:0. The conversion is always BT.709, from full-range RGB to limited-range YUV (Y 16–235, Cb/Cr 16–240; at 10 bits 64–940 and 64–960), and the stream's VUI says so. Who converts depends on the path.

    The arithmetic (colori709.c and the shader): Kr = 0.2126, Kb = 0.0722; coefficients in fixed point with 15 fractional bits so each fits an int16 for pmaddwd; luma (5983, 20127, 2032) sums to 28142 = 219/255 · 32768, so white gives 235 and black 16; Cb (−3298, −11094, 14392) and Cr (14392, −13072, −1320) each sum to 0 — the green coefficient of Cr is 13072, not the rounded 13073, so that every grey is exactly 128 (verified on all 256 greys). Chroma is the sum of each horizontal pair, filtered vertically with a 1-3-3-1 tent over four rows (swscale's filter), rounded to nearest, no dithering. At 10 bits the matrix is computed at 10 bits (876 luma levels), not 8 bits shifted, which is what swscale did; P010 stores the ten bits high in sixteen.

    Why REMOTIX's own code. libswscale went with ffmpeg; libyuv (0.0.1904 on Debian trixie) converts ARGB to 4:2:0 only as BT.601 limited or JPEG full range, which would have changed the product's colours with no error anywhere. About 200 lines and no extra dependency for the installer on seven distributions. x86-64 always has SSE2 (it is in the ABI), so there is no runtime dispatch; other architectures run the same arithmetic in plain C with identical bytes. GCC 14 at -O2 did not vectorise the plain C (13.7 ms at 3840×2160 against 13.1 for swscale, 30 Sep 2026).

    !
    The 1088-row scaling found by refutation (22 Aug 2026). leaving the VPP regions NULL means “the whole surface”, and the destination surface is aligned (1920×1088 on iHD for 1080p): the VPP then scaled 1080 rows to 1088. The colour statistics of the two streams matched within 0.17 levels while the drag bench read 0 marks out of 903 against 870 of 870 on the other path — a slightly blurred, slightly stretched desktop with no log line. Both regions are now the canvas, and the source is the canvas size.
    i
    Radeon VPP. the Radeon's VPP loses on chroma (phase 18 bench: −1 to −6 dB of PSNR from memory, and on zero copy with both the old and the new code); with Vulkan on AMD the shader does the conversion instead.

    7.7 · Writing the bitstream headers

    Since phase 18 REMOTIX writes H.264 and HEVC headers itself. scrittore_bit.c knows no codec: it knows bits, Exp-Golomb and the 00 00 03 rule. Which fields to write, and in which order, is in vadiretta.c, with the standard's clause beside each line. It is the mirror of the reader LettoreBit that codificatore.c has had since 12 Aug 2026 to read back what was produced.

    A field that does not fit sets traboccato (overflowed) and whoever closes the NAL sees it: a truncated header looks like a header. The NAL header itself receives no emulation bytes, as in ffmpeg's cbs_h2645.

    The cropping window rewrite (D-023)

    Measured 27 Sep 2026 on the Radeon RX 6800 (Mesa radeonsi 25.0.7): HEVC at 2544×1344 produced a stream declaring 2560×1344 — the card codes the multiple of its 64-pixel block and does not write the conformance window. The byte check rightly refused a stream whose size differs from the canvas, Chrome chose HEVC, Chrome's canvases are never multiples of 64: a session black forever. cornice_al_suo_posto() (“the window in its place”) decides on the first SPS of each encoder context: if the stream is larger than the canvas by less than 64 pixels on each side and by even amounts, the window is written. riscrivi_sps_con_cornice() re-reads the SPS up to the cropping flag, rewrites the head identical, sets the flag with the four offsets (in chroma units, i.e. half pixels for 4:2:0, added to any that existed), copies the tail bit by bit to the stop bit, and puts the NAL back with its emulation bytes. This is legal because nothing after the window depends on its position. Only keyframes carry an SPS, so only they are touched; any other mismatch remains an error. Measured: the 2560 stream cropped to 2544 decoded against the original at PSNR 50 dB.

    7.8 · Bytes, levels and the confession

    Decision D1 of phase 2: pure Annex-B and no description. Every keyframe carries its parameter sets in front (H.264: SPS, PPS, IDR; HEVC: VPS, SPS, PPS, IDR), so a client that attaches late decodes from the first key it sees. Chromium decides the stream form from the presence of the description, not from the hev1/hvc1 prefix (measured 12 Aug 2026).

    Before any byte leaves, forma_va_bene() checks it, because a decoder fed the wrong shape does not complain: it paints black, or paints at the old size, three links further down.

    • the frame starts with a start code (not a length prefix);
    • a keyframe has its parameter sets before the IDR;
    • the SPS is read with the bit reader (leggi_sps_h264(), leggi_sps_hevc()), and the depth and the displayed size in the bytes must equal what was requested; the size coded and the size displayed are kept apart (larghezza_codificata vs larghezza_flusso, coded width vs stream width: on radeonsi 1080p is coded as 1088 and cropped).
    • a frame larger than 16 MiB is never sent (7.10 “Frame ceiling and quality steps”).

    The confession. codificatore_confessione() returns what the encoder actually did, from two independent witnesses: the context (component opened, path, vendor, entry point verified, size limits, rate-control mask and mode read back, working point, maximum rate, VBV in bits and milliseconds) and the bytes (depth, profile, level, tier, sizes, chroma format, stringa_codec). If they disagree, the component disobeyed: ha_obbedito (obeyed) becomes false and nothing is sent. The reason is history: libsvtav1 printed «Error parsing option» on an unknown option and exited 0; v1 had a CBR nobody asked for that only the bandwidth bill revealed (lesson R31).

    The level is imposed, then verified. RCP/1 says the server must not emit a level above the client's video.livello; the browser does not enforce it (Chrome accepted L30 on a level 3.0 stream and painted, 12 Aug 2026), so the check is the server's (decision D4). On 23 Aug 2026 a 3840×2160 H.264 stream came out at level 5.2 against a declared 5.1, because nobody had told the encoder. Now livello_imposto() translates the ceiling into the codec's alphabet, the encoder writes it, and the child logs the level read from the bytes in decimal next to the client's (livello_in_decimi()). The declared cost: H.264 5.1 allows MaxMBPS 983,040, i.e. about 30 frames/s at 3840×2160, and the encoder keeps running at 60, so the stream declares a level whose rate limit it exceeds — which is exactly what the client asked for by declaring 5.1 at 4K; halving the rate would change what the user sees and is not done here. The largest canvas, 4096×2304, is the MaxFS of levels 5.1/5.2.

    A change of negotiated depth, level ceiling or capture channel order (BGRx ↔ RGBx) between two clients of the same session rebuilds the encoder, because these are fixed at opening; the next frame is a key.

    7.9 · Keyframes on demand

    The GOP is infinite (chiavi_ogni = 0): periodic keyframes are bandwidth spent on an insurance the protocol already buys, and on a bad line keys sent by the clock are the spiral RCP/1 forbids. A keyframe is produced exactly when one is owed.

    A keyframe on a still desktop has nothing to encode, because the compositor sends nothing: the child wakes the stream so a frame arrives (6.5 “PipeWire negotiation, resize and wake-up”). With GOP infinite the request path must exist: without anyone calling codificatore_chiedi_chiave(), a client that lost one delta would keep a broken screen forever. How the page decides to ask is in ch. 9 “The browser page”.

    7.10 · Frame ceiling and quality steps

    RCP/1 forbids a video frame larger than 16 MiB: it must be re-encoded at lower quality and logged, never sent. TETTO_FOTOGRAMMA is 16 × 1024 × 1024 bytes.

    The step was 6 until 22 Aug 2026: at 7680×4320 on nearly incompressible content QP 38 gave 16.654 MiB (8 times out of 8 over, by 4 %) while QP 44 gave 11.056 MiB; a wider step costs a fraction of one more attempt (91–108 ms each on the GPU at 8K). At the user's canvas (2560×1080) the largest of 404 real keys was 21,433 bytes, 0.13 % of the ceiling: the defect is real and far from urgent. Every quality change closes and reopens the context, and the next frame is a key.

    Two server-wide switches change what the user sees and are therefore off by default (invariant I6): --qualita-risale (codificatore_qualita_risale(), climbing back up the quality ladder) and --tetto-banda-mbit N (codificatore_tetto_banda(), QVBR on VA-API / VBR on Vulkan with maximum rate = 80 % of the declared floor, working point = 75 % of the maximum rate — never equal, or the Intel driver deduces CBR — and a 40 ms VBV). Their numbers, measurements and the third witness (the bytes per 10 s window) are described in ch. 8 “Quality, degradation and budget”.

    7.11 · Resizing the encoder

    codificatore_ridimensiona() reopens the encoder at the new size; the first frame after is a true key. The size it receives has already been checked by rcp_misura_ammessa(): at least 320×240, at most 4096×2304, even sides; a larger request is reduced (the side that overflows goes to the maximum, the other stays), a smaller one is refused.

    The 4096-pixel width is the user's decision of 1 Oct 2026 (“4096 max width is fine; it is more than 4K”): H.264 on the Intel GPU stops there (32–4096 per side), and Firefox receives only H.264. Before, the legal canvas reached 7680×4320 and wider H.264 canvases had nowhere to go. The driver's own maximum is still read at every opening (misura_massima_l/misura_massima_a, maximum width/height), because another card may declare less.

    Encoding at a size that is not a multiple of the block: H.264 writes the cropping window itself (16-pixel macroblocks); HEVC relies on the driver, and where the driver does not write it, on D-023 (7.7 “Writing the bitstream headers”). With Vulkan on the Radeon the capture slabs stay at the maximum canvas across resizes (6.7 “Slabs: zero copy on labwc”).

    7.12 · Removing ffmpeg and the CPU path

    Phase 18 (closed 30 Sep 2026) removed ffmpeg; phase 19 (closed 3 Oct 2026) removed the CPU encoders. Both were accepted only on measured equivalence.

    The reason was licensing: REMOTIX must have no GPL dependency, and the distributions' libavcodec is GPL. The product binary no longer links libavcodec, libavutil or libswscale (verified with ldd and nm -D: 0 av_/sws_ symbols).

    The last number is part of why phase 19 removed the CPU path altogether (the user, 1 Oct 2026: “no CPU without a GPU; today even VMs can have hardware acceleration”). Without a capable GPU the installer's preflight refuses the machine with the reason, and a server that starts anyway offers no codec. A VM with a passed-through or virtual GPU works; a VM without one does not.

    i
    Radeon anomaly A3. on the Radeon RX 6800 (VCN 3.0, radeonsi 25.0.7) one frame in about 50 takes ~31 ms instead of 8.7: groups of exactly five slow frames every 12–40 s, p99 30.9 ms, identical with libavcodec and with libva direct (30 Sep 2026, KDE and GNOME 4K). It is inside the driver's encode call, outside REMOTIX's scope by the user's decision, and documented for the Mesa developers in fasi/16-a3-radeon-vcn.md. Since phase 19 the Radeon encodes through Vulkan; whether the anomaly persists there is not settled yet.

    7.13 · Encoder timings and constants

    Every encoded frame carries its costs separately, so that a drop in frame rate can be attributed. They are logged for the first frame and summarised afterwards; performance figures with their hardware are in ch. 18 “Performance and capacity”.

    +
    Diagnosis. the log area of the encoder is video; the line that starts with aperto: (opened) names the codec, depth, component, node, vendor and (on VA-API) the entry point actually in force, and the line before it says which path was taken and whether it was asked by name or by capability. remotix --prova-codifica with --codifica vulkan or --codifica vaapi reproduces one path in isolation; the comparison benches are banchi/18-scheda/18-confronto.sh and banchi/19-vulkan/19-confronto.sh, and the shader is rebuilt with banchi/19-vulkan/19-shader.sh.
    Chapter 8

    Quality, degradation and budget

    8.1 · The quality contract

    REMOTIX does not chase a bitrate or a quality score. It follows a short contract written by the user in SPECIFICHE.md §3 and §8 and in DECISIONI.md §2–§4: what may be spent when there is not enough, in which order, and what must never be spent. Every mechanism of this chapter exists to keep one line of that contract, and each one says so in the log.

    i
    Goals, not promises. since 30 September 2026 the thresholds of SPECIFICHE.md §3 are design goals, not measured promises: the user removed the performance tests from the acceptance criteria as too hardware-dependent. Parameters the product really uses (floor, session cap, clocks) are configuration and hold as written.

    The floor was 20 Mbit/s on the morning of 23 August 2026 and became 30 the same night (§3.1-sexies). Phase 9 was calibrated on 20, and its numbers were left as measured; the encoder's bandwidth cap still derives its three numbers from the value passed on the command line, so the operator chooses which floor it represents (8.3 “Encoder rate control”). The user then moved the target of the phase: bandwidth is a premise, the real challenge is a line that loses, reorders and jitters (§3.1-ter). Most of the mechanisms below react to queues, not to Mbit/s.

    8.2 · Where quality is decided

    Quality is not decided in one place. The encoder lives in the per-user child process, the budget and the admission in the parent's main loop, the line-facing regulators in the parent's WebTransport layer, and the last word — what reaches the screen — in the page. Each piece decides only on what it can measure locally.

    Two of these live in the child, which is a separate program started with execve and a freshly composed environment: they cannot travel as environment variables. figli_fase9() (the phase 9 settings for the children) stores them and the child's command line carries --qualita-risale and --tetto-banda-mbit (and the audio-silence switch) when it is built. Every switch writes its value in force at startup, on and off: “switched off” and “never had to act” must not look the same in the log.

    i
    One way per switch. each cure has exactly one way to be switched off. The old enabling names --ritmo-adattivo and --linea-morta no longer exist: typing them prints an explanation and exits with status 2. The temporary environment bridge for the queue threshold was removed on 23 August 2026 when the option arrived: two ways to set the same value are two numbers that can diverge.

    8.3 · Encoder rate control

    By default the encoder runs at a constant QP of 26 (QP_HARDWARE in src/figlio.c, mode CODIFICATORE_QUALITA_QP), with no bitrate, no buffer and no rate controller. With --tetto-banda-mbit N it switches to QVBR, a rate controller with a ceiling in which the QP still acts as the quality factor.
