    Constant QP is the direct translation of I1 and of “never coarsen”: the quantiser is fixed, so the image of a quiet desktop never gets worse, and the bandwidth is simply what comes out. Measured on the test machine on 23 August 2026 (2560×1080, EncSliceLP on the Intel UHD 770, QP 26, 30 s per point), the real desktop of the user moving at full screen cost 0.204 Mbit/s; a film with grain at full screen cost 58.7 Mbit/s. (The phase 9 document later found that this series had been taken with the test client negotiating HEVC; re-measured in H.264 the same night, the hard case still asked 44.6 Mbit/s.) A cap that bit on ordinary content would repeat the mistake that cost v1 a whole phase, so the cap is for the hard case only, and it is off until the user judges it.

    Under VBR the QP is silently ignored, which would turn the quality ladder and the quality rise into no-ops: a component that ignores an option without saying so is precisely the failure this file exists to avoid. The three numbers of the cap are derived from the floor given on the command line, never written by hand (tetto_filo() (wire), tetto_punto() (working point), tetto_serbatoio_bit() (buffer in bits)):

    The mode is asked for by name (modo_bitrate_voluto(), the wanted bitrate mode) and checked against the mask the driver declares: on VA-API the declared rate-control bits are read with vaGetConfigAttributes and printed in clear, and a mode the driver does not declare makes the encoder fail loudly instead of falling back to a mode nobody chose. tetto_in_tre_numeri() (the cap in three numbers) refuses a working point not below the wire and a non-positive buffer, and serbatoio_entro_i_50_ms() (buffer within 50 ms) refuses a buffer longer than 50 ms. On Vulkan Video, which has no QVBR, the cap becomes VBR with the requested QP as the floor of the controller (apri_scheda_vulkan(), which opens the Vulkan encoder); without the cap the card must declare CQP.

    !
    Which floor. the cap applies only to hardware encoding — since phase 19 there is no other kind — and the value passed is a floor, not a ceiling. The code comments and the phase 9 measurements use 20 Mbit/s; the declared product floor is 30 (DECISIONI.md §3.1-sexies). Whoever switches the cap on chooses which one to pass.

    Not settled yet: the cap and the quality rise are off by default and await the user's judgement on the real desktop; max_frame_size, which QVBR would accept, is deliberately not used — a second lever on the same quantity would give two measurements under one label.

    8.4 · The 16 MiB frame cap and the quality ladder

    RCP.md §6.2 forbids a video frame larger than 16 MiB: the sender must re-encode it at a lower quality and log it, never send it. That rule is the only thing that moves the QP of a running encoder.

    When a frame comes out of the card above TETTO_FOTOGRAMMA (the frame ceiling, 16 777 216 bytes), comprimi_comune() (the shared compression path) logs it, records the step on which the cap bit (qualita_fallita), and abbassa_qualita() (lower the quality) raises the QP by CRF_PASSO (the step) = 9, capped at 51. Changing quality closes and reopens the card context (cambia_qualita(), change the quality), so the next frame is always a keyframe. The ladder from the default is therefore 26 → 35 → 44 → 51.

    The step was 6 until 22 August 2026, and it was one step short: at 7680×4320 with almost incompressible content a keyframe was 16.654 MiB at QP 38 (104 % of the cap, eight times out of eight) and 11.056 MiB at QP 44. Each attempt costs 91–108 ms in hardware at 8K, so a wider step is cheaper than an extra attempt. The limit was later lowered to 4096×2304 (see 9.7 “Canvas and view”), and at the user's own canvas the largest of 404 real keyframes was 21 433 bytes, 0.13 % of the cap: the ladder is a safety net for exceptional frames, not a working mechanism. The encoder side of the same mechanism is in 7.10 “Frame ceiling and quality steps”.

    Every descent is declared in the log (area video) with the frame size and its percentage of the cap. A percentage of 100 or less would be a descent out of prudence, which I1 forbids, and the line would prove it on its own.

    i
    A dead branch, fixed. until 23 August 2026 the delta branch was dead code: the counter read prossimo_chiave (next frame is a key) inside the loop, and every reopen set it, so a delta always walked the whole ladder while the startup line claimed it stopped after three attempts. The frame's kind is now decided once, before the first descent (chiave_chiesta, key requested).

    8.5 · Quality recovery after the cap

    Before phase 9 the QP was a ratchet: four writes, all downwards. One exceptional frame left the session at the bottom of the ladder for hours, with a quiet desktop permanently coarse and no log line saying why. --qualita-risale adds the way back; it is off by default (invariant I6: what changes what the user sees stays behind a switch until the user has looked).

    risali_qualita() (raise the quality) runs at the entry of the next frame, never with a packet in hand (closing the context frees its bytes). It climbs one step at a time and never above the quality the caller requested. A relapse right after a climb doubles the wait (risalito_da_poco, recently raised). The two defences against flapping are the eighth-of-the-cap margin — a scene sitting at 95 % of the cap never produces a calm frame — and the doubling, which halves the reopen rate at every round. If the context does not reopen at the new value, it falls back to the old one: climbing is optional, and a cure that kills the session when it fails is worse than the defect.

    Not settled yet: the three numbers are declared sufficient, not right; the phase 9 bench criteria (more than 3 reopens per minute, or a lower frame rate with the cure than without) would condemn them.

    8.6 · The video queue threshold

    Each video frame travels on its own unidirectional QUIC stream. When a newer frame is produced while an older delta still has bytes in our send queue, RCP.md §5.1 allows (it does not require) a RESET_STREAM of the old one. video_sgombra() (clear the video queue) decides when to use that permission.

    Until 23 August 2026 every older delta was abandoned at once. On the test machine, with a 3-second dip to 10 Mbit/s and a 1920×1080 scene, abandonments and keyframes went one to one, even on the wide line: each abandon opened a gap, each gap asked for a keyframe, and the abandoning itself was manufacturing keyframes. Since 24 August a delta is abandoned only if the video queue cannot drain within WT_SGOMBRA_SOGLIA_MS = 100 ms:

    The decision of video_sgombra()
    wait_ms = video_queue_bytes * smoothed_rtt / cwnd       (from ngtcp2)
        = video_queue_bytes / 2500                      (fallback: no rtt/cwnd yet, 20 Mbit/s)
wait <= threshold            -> keep every delta (counted, one log line per state change)
wait >  threshold            -> abandon the live deltas still in our queue
wait >  threshold, a KEY in queue -> keep the deltas behind it (22 Sep 2026)

    Only bytes still in our own queue are considered; what has already been handed to ngtcp2 is not taken back (nothing would be saved). The last rule was added on 22 September 2026 after a user test with a 4K video on KDE: a ~300 KB keyframe in the queue pushed the wait above the threshold on its own, abandoning the deltas behind it did not shorten it, but opened a gap, which requested another large keyframe — abandons climbed by one per keyframe, 7 → 13 in 6 s, and then the dead line fired. Behind a keyframe the deltas are kept, and braking production is left to the rate regulator.

    The price, measured 23–24 August 2026 (bench 09-b79, together with the rate regulator): up to +160 ms of drift on a bad line, zero on a healthy one (39.85 / 40.19 / 39.63 frames/s in the three arms, no keyframes in any of them). --sgombra-soglia-ms 0 restores the old behaviour byte for byte.

    8.7 · The rate regulator

    The rate regulator is the only mechanism that lowers the frame rate, and it does so on a local fact: arretrato (backlog), the number of live, non-key deltas that still have bytes in our send queue, read when a new frame arrives and before video_sgombra().

    ritmo_frena() (rate brake) returns “do not send” when arretrato reaches WT_RITMO_POSTI (rate slots) = 2: one frame of overlap is allowed, two left behind are not. Nothing comes from outside — no loss rate, no reorder, no client silence can distort it — and there is no state to climb back: the quantity is re-read at every frame, so the episode ends by itself when the queue empties. Keyframes never pass through it; they have their own pacing (8.8 “Keyframe request pacing”).

    Measured in the phase 9 paired comparison: keyframes dropped from 51.7–88.1 % of frames to 0.0–5.6 %, and the delivered rate rose 1.7–2.8× on the degraded profiles (DECISIONI.md §3.1-septies). The price is the same +160 ms shared with the threshold.

    !
    Congestion control. the congestion algorithm was never chosen: src/trasporto.c calls ngtcp2_settings_default() and keeps ngtcp2's default (CUBIC). On Wi-Fi a loss-based algorithm reads radio loss as congestion and halves the window, which manufactures exactly the backlog this regulator measures (4.11 “Congestion and the send queue”). Not settled yet: a different algorithm is to be tried as a separate experiment.

    Not settled yet: WT_RITMO_POSTI = 2 is to be calibrated; the falsifiable prediction is zero descents at 20 Mbit/s with a moving scene. The proper fix of the cost (stop encoding instead of dropping after encoding) needs the decision to reach the child, and is a second step.

    8.8 · Keyframe request pacing

    A keyframe is about ten times a delta. Asking for one at every sign of trouble is the spiral that RCP.md §5.2 names: during a burst of losses the requests multiply and every keyframe worsens the condition that caused it. Both ends pace their requests.

    chiave_intervallo_ms() first looks at a fact: if the previous keyframe still has bytes in our queue, the answer is the 2-second ceiling. Otherwise it computes, from ngtcp2's own cwnd and smoothed RTT, how long a keyframe of the last size needs to leave, adds 20 %, and never goes below 150 ms or above 2 s. Every change of the interval by 100 ms or more is logged with the bandwidth it was derived from.

    Where there is bandwidth the cure declares itself inert (la banda misurata basta: resta il fondo di 150 ms, “the measured bandwidth is enough: the 150 ms floor remains”, 100 times out of 101 at 15 Mbit/s). On a narrow line the image stays broken longer after a loss — that is the price, and it is visible — and in exchange the audio, whose datagrams found cwnd_left = 0 behind keyframes asked faster than they could leave, gets through.

    8.9 · The dead line

    The fifth cure is of another kind: it does not decide how well the desktop is seen but whether the connection still exists. The user decided on 23 August 2026 that a line losing in bursts is not a slow line but a broken one: the wire drops and the user signs in again by hand.

    linea_morta_giudica() (judge the dead line) evaluates both from two monotonic local counters (video bytes handed to ngtcp2, frames offered by the child) and from ngtcp2's received-packet counter; time enters only as the distance between two samples. When either fires, linea_morta_scatta() (fire the dead line) writes one line starting with linea-morta that carries every number of the decision (causa=, stallo_ms=, silenzio_ms=, prove=, cwnd=, ritmo_giu= …), and the transport, the only owner of the QUIC connection, closes it. With the dead line on, the transport's PINGs move from 10 s to half the silence threshold (5 s), or “the client does not answer” and “we never asked” would look the same.

    The stall threshold sits 5.0× above the longest empty second of raffica-1 (burst 1, a line that holds, 23.94 frames/s) and 2.9× below the 14.26 s freeze of raffica-forte (strong burst, a line that serves nobody); on casa-cattiva (bad home line), the worst line that holds for ten minutes, the stall never exceeded 500 ms — a margin above 10× (measured 23–24 Aug 2026, test machine, netem profiles). It is the most expensive cure: a wrong threshold would throw out someone who is working, so whoever touches WT_LM_STALLO_MS must measure those two margins again.

    !
    Loss is not a cause. DECISIONI.md §3.1-quater also lists “copious loss within 1–2 s” as a cause. The code does not: the loss fraction was refuted by its own bench on 23 August 2026 — casa-cattiva declared 512‰ and held for ten minutes, raffica-forte declared 123‰ and did not. On a reordering line pkt_lost/pkt_sent measures reordering, not loss. The fraction stays in the log line as permille=, a witness rather than a judge, and --linea-morta-permille no longer exists.

    On the page the closed transport takes the session back to the login form with the sentence that the connection was interrupted and the password must be typed again (9.13 “End of session in the page”). At 10 % loss the cures do not save the experience — the user called it “stuck” — and declaring the line dead is the only honest answer (§3.1-septies). The transport side — PINGs, QUIC idle timeout, the closing itself — is in 4.10 “Keep-alive, silence and the dead line”.

    8.10 · Ghost eviction and audio silence

    Two of the five phase 9 cures change nothing the user sees, and were switched on together with the others on 24 August 2026.

    The eviction removes a false sentence rather than adding one: the old refusal claimed the user was “connected from another device” when it was usually their own dead session. The audio side is described in ch. 11 “Audio and clipboard”.

    8.11 · The composition budget

    Until 25 August 2026 the server accepted everyone and starved everyone together: on the saturated scene the eleventh user entered with negati 0 (refused: 0) and the first session fell from 39.60 to 0.96 frames/s (−97.6 %). src/budget.c is the cure: it computes, before a desktop is started, whether the machine can afford one more.

    The neck is upstream of REMOTIX: when the machine gives way, rcs0 is saturated by gnome-shell at 99.5 % while remotix sits at 0.00 %, and the video engine drops from 48.7 % to 0.4 % because it has nothing left to encode. Switching off a single scene among eight sessions brought the rate back from 1.6 to 33.4 frames/s, reversibly. At the cliff the Mpixel/s coincide within 0.6 % across canvas sizes while frames/s differ by 74.9 %: the budget can only count composition, and it counts it in composed pixels per second.

    The admission rule of budget.c (peggiore = worst case, consegnato = delivered)
    fits(inside, new)  <=>  sum of demand(inside) + peggiore(new)  <=  C * 1.01
                         AND  no tenant's median delay > 22.9 ms

demand(t)   = peggiore(t)                           if t never delivered, or has no delay sample
            = max(consegnato(t), F * peggiore(t))   otherwise
peggiore(t) = canvas_width * canvas_height * 39.54 / 1e6    Mpixel/s

    The accumulator. deposita_fotogramma() (deposit a frame) in src/main.c already received every frame of every child with width, height and capture instant, so no new channel between processes was needed: budget_deposita() is called there, before the frame is broadcast and without any “is someone watching” guard. That is deliberate: a session whose client has left keeps encoding until its seat expires (a ghost), and costs the GPU as much as the others. The delay is capture → parent, an upper bound of the compositor's hold time, prudent in the right direction.

    The reserve. Eight idle sessions admitted at 0.01 % each woke up within 19 ms and asked for 8 × 14.4 = 115 % of the engine, plus the holder: 130 % of an engine that has 100. The worker lost 95.9 % of its rate and its delay went ×78 (9.7 → 756 ms). The phase 9 regulator cannot help — it drops frames already composed and encoded — so the reserve is the only defence: an idle tenant does not cost zero, it costs F times its worst case.

    Unknown is not zero. A tenant that has not yet delivered a full 2-second window, or has no delay sample, is counted at its worst case; its canvas is that of its last frame or, if none, the stage canvas, the largest any session can get. The newcomer is counted at the minimum of the stage canvas and its video.misura_massima (wt_misura_massima_di(), the maximum size declared by that user's client), because the real canvas is only decided at SESSIONE, later. A missing monotonic clock gives BUDGET_NON_SO (“I don't know”), which admits and logs: a budget that refused for having failed to measure would make the user pay for our fault.

    !
    Off, and not self-tuning. the budget is off by default (--budget-mpixel-s 0) and never calibrates itself. Before the machine has given way once, the highest capacity read is a lower bound, not a ceiling. Whoever types --budget-mpixel-s N declares that N Mpixel/s of composition were measured at saturation on that machine. Passing the encoder's number instead would admit about 22 sessions where six fit.
    i
    Not settled yet. the delay gate never decided alone in the phase 10 runs (the pixel sum always did), and the compositor's buffer count, which would give the second half of the delay meter, lives in the child and does not cross the process boundary: only the measured delay is used.

    8.12 · Admission: the session cap and the budget

    A refusal decided after the desktop has started is not a refusal: it is a login followed by an eviction. Measured in phase 10: a user who was never admitted had 42 processes and a gnome-shell. Since 25 August 2026 both limits are checked in consegna_verdetto() (deliver the verdict) before figli_assicura_da() (ensure the user's child) starts the child.

    The two refusals are deliberately different (fasi/10-multi-tenant-e-il-budget.md §8.1 D5): two different facts may not share an outcome. Neither is checked on a resume — a user whose stage already exists is already inside both counts, and refusing their reattach would be a false no on capacity they are spending anyway. The refusal is sent after trasporto_verdetto() (hand the verdict to the transport), through wt_congeda_utente() (dismiss every connection of the user): that order resets the failed-password counter of the address, and the client never sees AMMESSO, only the farewell. The body of the CONGEDO carries the figures (demand, declared capacity, the newcomer's worst case) for the log; the page shows its own phrase and does not print the body (RCP.md §7.1).

    The page phrase for 0x06 promises only what is true at the gate. An earlier version suggested shrinking the window; at the gate the only canvas number is video.misura_massima, the decoder's ceiling, so a smaller window got exactly the same refusal.

    --tetto-sessioni N sizes the four tables that count a user — the attached seats in src/rcp.c, the children in src/figlio.c, the presence table in src/main.c, the stages in src/webtransport.c — which used to be five hand-written copies (16, 16, 16, 16 and an 8). MAX_IN_VOLO (maximum in flight) in src/aiutante.c stays separate on purpose: it counts PAM verifications in flight, not sessions. The count of refusals, negati, is written even with the budget off, because reading zero there is the fact that proves the product behaves as before.

    8.13 · Capacity measured in phase 10

    How many sessions fit depends on the hardware and on the scene, and is not promised. The phase 10 numbers below were measured on one machine — Intel Core i5-13500T with the integrated Intel UHD 770 (renderD128), 31 GB, 1920×1080 H.264, GNOME — on 24–25 August 2026.

    At the sixth step the budget counted 496 Mpx/s while the machine delivered 478.7: the demand is an upper bound of what is delivered, and that margin is what makes the refusal fall on the seventh session, before the cliff, instead of the eighth, inside it. The control runs: budget off again → 26 violations and no 0x06; ten idle sessions with the budget on → zero refused; budget set to 40 Mpx/s, below one 1080p session → the first user refused, zero processes started.

    The phase 20 campaigns, on all four desktops and both cards, are in ch. 18 “Performance and capacity”.

    +
    Calibrating. measure your own machine before switching the budget on: run the saturated scene with the budget off, find the step where the rate collapses, and pass the composed Mpixel/s of the last healthy step. BUDGET_RITMO_MAX_FOT_S (39.54) is also a property of the test machine; on very different hardware it has to be re-measured and recompiled.

    8.14 · Configuring quality and capacity

    On Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora and openSUSE the packaged unit reads /usr/share/remotix/remotix.conf and then /etc/remotix/remotix.conf.d/*.conf; any extra server option goes into the REMOTIX_OPZIONI variable of a drop-in file there.

    Switching on the budget on a deb or rpm system
    # /etc/remotix/remotix.conf.d/capacity.conf
REMOTIX_OPZIONI=--budget-mpixel-s 480 --riserva 0.5 --tetto-sessioni 8

    The Arch unit has no EnvironmentFile and no REMOTIX_OPZIONI: options are added by overriding ExecStart with systemctl edit remotix. After a restart, check the startup lines (ch. 13 “Logging and diagnostics”): each cure states whether it is on and with which number, and the budget prints its three values with the option names.

    • Not settled yet: the cap and the quality rise wait for the user's judgement on the real desktop.
    • Not settled yet: a second, network budget next to the GPU one (ten sessions × the floor on the server's uplink) was named in phase 9 and never written.
    • Not settled yet: the ban per address, shared by tenants behind one NAT, was deferred to a security chapter (DECISIONI.md §4.6-octies).
    Chapter 9

    The browser page

    9.1 · How the page is served

    The whole client is one file, src/pagina.html: the login page, the RCP/1 client, video decoding and drawing, audio, clipboard, keyboard, pointer and touch. Nothing is installed on the user's device and nothing else is downloaded: the page is the product's only client.

    Cross-origin isolation is a product requirement, not a bench detail (SPECIFICHE.md §11.5): without it Firefox and Safari round the page's timers to 1 ms, on a latency cap of 50 ms, and shared memory does not exist. With require-corp every sub-resource would have to declare its own policy; the simplest cure is to have none, which is why everything is inline. The isolation is inherited by the optional video worker, born from a Blob (measured 13 Aug 2026: crossOriginIsolated true inside the worker, timer grain 0.005 ms).

    pagina_apri() (open the page server) refuses to start if any marker is missing, or if data-bannato=" or data-restano-ms=" occur more than once (a bench that greps the first occurrence would read the wrong one). The fingerprint is the only server text that enters a JavaScript string, and it is base64 written by REMOTIX; the ban sentence never enters the script. The TLS side, the certificates and the ban are described in 4.7 “The page server”, 4.6 “serverCertificateHashes and the fingerprint” and ch. 14 “Security model”.

    9.2 · Structure of pagina.html

    The file is about 13 000 lines, most of them comments that carry the reason and the measurement behind each rule. The code is organised in blocks, and several input blocks are “anchors” owned by different authors, each writing only inside its own markers.

    The page defines one main global, window.REMOTIX, an object to be read by benches and diagnostics (schermo the screen, sondaggio the probe results, tratti the latency stretches, giro the round trip, video, dichiarazioni the declarations, registro the log, scorciatoie the shortcuts…): nothing in it changes what the page does. The input anchors meet through REMOTIX_INPUT (the input stream, set after SESSIONE), REMOTIX_CLASSICO, REMOTIX_PUNTATORE and REMOTIX_SCORCIATOIE.

    i
    Bench switches, not settings. the switches exist so that a comparison changes one variable inside the same page; they are not per-browser or per-compositor options, and the product has one behaviour without them. The fragment form (#…) never reaches the server, so it works on a page served by any static server.

    9.3 · The connection sequence

    The login form has two fields and a button — #utente, #parola, #vai — plus #esito for the outcome, #avviso for the ban and #dichiarazione for what the page declares about codecs and video. The ids are stable: the functional suite finds elements by id, not by text.

    1. Submit. The button is disabled, the outcome cleared; collega() runs. Whatever happens, the password field is emptied at the end: it is never kept, and never logged.
    2. WebTransport present? If not, the page says so and stops.
    3. Fingerprint. impronta() fetches /impronta before every attempt, because a tab left open for two weeks holds the fingerprint of a certificate already rotated. If the fetch is rejected by the network (TypeError: nobody listens), the page says at once that the server does not answer and does not open WebTransport — before this rule (D-009) Firefox waited the 30 s of its QUIC handshake. Any other failure falls back to the fingerprint served with the page, and says so.
    4. WebTransport to https://<host>/rcp/1 with allowPooling: false and serverCertificateHashes: the browser checks the fingerprint, not a certificate chain — the only mechanism browsers offer to a server without a domain (RCP.md §4.1-bis).
    5. Listen first. Video streams, audio datagrams and clipboard streams are listened to before the handshake ends: a server that opened one before SESSIONE violates RCP §2.5, and the violation is only visible to someone already listening.
    6. CIAO (hello) with the capabilities (9.4 “Capabilities declared by the page”), after waiting for the codec probes. ECCOMI (here I am): a version other than 1 is refused with VERSIONE_INCOMPATIBILE before the password leaves.
    7. CREDENZIALI (credentials). RESPINTO (rejected) shows the reason and stops (a second attempt needs a new connection); a CONGEDO (goodbye) shows its reason and stops; AMMESSO (admitted) continues.
    8. ATTACCA (attach) carries the canvas to ask for (tela_da_chiedere()), the view (misura_vista()) and the keyboard layout (disposizione()). SESSIONE says new or resumed, the granted canvas and the desktop name. A granted canvas different from the requested one is declared to the user (RCP §4.5 allows it).
    9. After SESSIONE: the single input stream is opened, the video is negotiated with the decoder, the first-frame watch starts, the control channel is read in a loop (ascolta_controllo()), and ADATTA_TELA (fit the canvas) is sent once for the window size.

    The keyboard layout is guessed from navigator.language (en → us, except en-GB → gb and en-IE → ie; about thirty languages whose XKB name equals the ISO code pass through, a few are mapped, such as sv → se and da → dk; the rest falls back to us); a page cannot know the physical keyboard, and choosing it is described in 10.11 “Keyboard layout negotiation”. The input stream coalesces pointer moves: when the writer's desiredSize is at or below zero, a PUNTATORE (pointer move) is held aside and replaced by the next one, and any key or button pushes it out first — measured from DeX on 14 Aug 2026, median round trip 135 ms but worst 2161 ms, a queue rather than a slow network. Keys and buttons are never dropped.

    Some user-facing texts of the page — the reason sentences, the declarations, the logout dialog — are still in Italian, while the login page is in English; DECISIONI.md §10.32 lists their translation as pending work.

    9.4 · Capabilities declared by the page

    The CIAO capabilities say what this browser can do, measured where possible. An empty value is a protocol error (RCP §4.3), so a capability with nothing to say is omitted, and the omission is logged.

    Declaring something the browser cannot do does not give an error; it gives a black canvas or silence, because the server must choose within the intersection following the client's order. Declaring opus on an engine that cannot decode it once made the server send fifty datagrams a second into a continue — and the PCM fallback, which exists to be Opus's positive control, never came into play.

    9.5 · Choosing the codec on the pixel

    The codec is not chosen by asking the browser's APIs. It is chosen by decoding a real keyframe and reading the pixels back.

    Measured on 12 August 2026 on Firefox 140 ESR, for all seven HEVC strings: navigator.mediaCapabilities.decodingInfo() said supported, smooth and power-efficient; canPlayType() said “probably”; VideoDecoder.isConfigSupported() said false; and no pixel arrived. Three witnesses, two of them false and agreeing with each other. The page never calls the first two. isConfigSupported is used as a filter only — when it says no the pixel never arrives, when it says yes it proves nothing (Chrome accepts a level-3.0 declaration on a 5.1 stream and paints anyway).

    The preference is PREFERENZA = ["hevc", "h264"]: HEVC where it paints, H.264 as the universal fallback; the server makes the final choice within the intersection. AV1 left the product in August 2026 (decided by the user on 17 August, removed from the page on 20 August; DECISIONI.md §1.13-ter): Firefox for Android had neither HEVC nor AV1, H.264 is the only codec in hardware at both ends, and Firefox's AV1 decoder painted rectangular blocks where Chrome and dav1d were clean on the same bytes. Its RCP number, 2, stays reserved forever (CODEC_RCP): reusing it would make an old client paint garbage without an error. The H.264 string is avc1.640033 (High, level 5.1), the same the server now derives from the SPS; the earlier avc1.640032 (5.0) cannot reach 3840×2160.

    If no codec reaches the pixel, video.codec is omitted and the server answers NIENTE_IN_COMUNE (nothing in common); the page writes its own explanation first, because only the page knows which probe failed and why. Whether decoding happens in hardware is not observable from JavaScript, and the page never claims it.

    9.6 · Measuring the decoder ceiling

    video.misura_massima is the largest frame the browser's decoder can bring to the pixel. It is not the screen size: a phone's decoder has limits its screen does not declare, and a desktop screen can be smaller than what its browser decodes.

    Until 13 August 2026 the page put screen.width × devicePixelRatio in this field. On a screen 1010 pixels tall the server granted a 1794×1010 canvas while the stage captured 1920×1080, refused to send frames of the wrong size, and the user saw nothing — even in full screen, since screen.height does not change with F11. The test pages had hand-written 3840×2160 and never showed it.

    If a codec paints at 64×48 but not even at 320×240, the page declares 320×240 and tells the user the image may not arrive at all. The cost of the ladder is logged on every load (sondaggio.misura.ms).

    9.7 · Canvas and view

    Two sizes must never be confused. The canvas (tela in the code) is the remote desktop's size: it belongs to the session, is fixed at attach and reattach, and is what the frames carry. The view (vista) is how much the page has to draw in: it belongs to the connection and changes with the window.

    Since 15 August 2026 (DECISIONI.md §5.0-sexies) the canvas takes the size of the client's window. Scale 1 makes coordinate conversion the identity, removes the black bands and the interpolated text, and the request at attach restarts the capture stream, which makes Mutter deliver a frame at once instead of after 4.4 s of waiting on a still scene. Since 17 August (§5.1-bis) the canvas never changes while the session lives: resizing the window only rescales the image. Resizing an output could not be done on KWin ≤ 6.7.4 and, where it works, it rearranges the user's windows; the user did not want a product that behaves differently depending on the compositor. A new size is taken by reconnecting.

    The maximum 4096×2304 dates from 1 October 2026 (the user: 4096 maximum width is fine): H.264 on the Intel card stops at 4096 per side and Firefox on Linux receives only H.264. A larger window gets the maximum on the side that overflows (5120×2880 → 4096×2304, 5120×1440 → 4096×1440), shown at scale 1 with bands. The limits are protocol constants (RCP_TELA_L_MASSIMA and its siblings in src/rcp.h); the server applies the same rule in rcp_misura_ammessa() (size allowed).

    html { overflow-y: scroll } keeps the vertical scrollbar always present, so turning the canvas on never changes clientWidth. The canvas has tabindex="-1", without which its focus() calls do nothing and the keyboard stays in the password field.

    i
    Not settled yet. a change of devicePixelRatio with the window still (page zoom, a window dragged to a screen with another scale) is not handled: the emulated test delivered no event at all, and a cure needs a measurement with real zoom. The VISTA (view) message is never sent after a resize either: no server component reads it in RCP/1.

    9.8 · Asking for the canvas with ADATTA_TELA

    The canvas is requested once per session, at attach, with ADATTA_TELA. The server answers with TELA (canvas): adopted, or refused with a reason.

    The control channel and the video streams are independent QUIC streams, so a frame at the new size can arrive before the TELA that announces it. While an ADATTA_TELA is unanswered (attese_tela, the pending canvas requests, > 0), a frame at an unannounced size is held (trattieni(), hold) and judged again when the answer arrives. With no request in flight, such a frame is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO at once — the condition is a request in flight, not a number of frames (finding P21, 13 Aug 2026, which replaced an earlier limit of eight frames). The page compares a new request with the size it is going to, not the one in force, so a window moved and moved back before the answer is not left at the wrong size.

    9.9 · Receiving video frames

    Each video frame arrives on its own unidirectional stream, opened by the server in frame order. avvia_video() reads the incoming streams and leggi_uno_stream() collects each one.

    The 28-byte video header (RCP.md §6.2), big-endian, read by Schermo.leggi_intestazione() (read the header)
    offset  size  field
 0      u16   tipo      type: 0x0301 keyframe, 0x0302 delta
 2      u16   codec     1 hevc, 3 h264 (2 reserved: av1)
 4      u32   larghezza width
 8      u32   altezza   height
12      u32   numero    frame number, 0 reserved, wraps to 1
16      u64   istante   instant: server monotonic clock, microseconds
24      u32   input     last input id applied when captured (0 = none)
28      ...   Annex B data

    The reader of these 28 bytes is written from the protocol table, not copied from the bench's reader: two independent implementations of the same bytes are part of the referee, and a disagreement is a gift. Schermo.consegna() (deliver) then applies the rules in a fixed order:

    1. type must be key or delta; codec must be the negotiated one; otherwise ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO;
    2. the input field closes an input round trip (9.12 “Measurements made by the page”);
    3. number 0 is a protocol error;
    4. order before size: a number not after the last delivered one (mod 2³²) is dropped without looking at its size — otherwise the keyframe that closes a tolerance window, overtaking older frames, would close the session;
    5. size: the canvas in force or a tolerated one; an unannounced size is held if an ADATTA_TELA is pending, a size that was in force and no longer is closes the session;
    6. a jump in numbers is a hole: one RICHIEDI_CHIAVE (request a keyframe) with the last delivered number, repeated at most once a second while the hole stays open (Schermo.buco()); the last good image stays on screen, deltas are not even given to the decoder until a keyframe arrives (RCP §5.2) — a delta referencing a missing frame does not error, it just decays;
    7. a frame whose size differs from the decoder's configuration is decoded only if it is a keyframe at the canvas in force (then the decoder is reconfigured); otherwise it is dropped and treated as a hole;
    8. decode, with the server's istante as timestamp.

    9.10 · Decoding with WebCodecs

    Decoding uses one VideoDecoder per session, configured with the string the probe saw paint, the frame size and optimizeForLatency: true. Painting happens inside the decoder's output callback, not on requestAnimationFrame: an extra animation frame would add up to one display interval to a budget worth two and a half.

    Schermo.riconfigura() (reconfigure) creates the decoder lazily and recreates it if an error closed it: after an error a VideoDecoder is closed and every configure() throws, which once made a session unrecoverable in silence. A decoder error is treated as a hole and asks for a keyframe.

    The decoder-queue skip. Measured 14 Aug 2026 (bench 04-b30, scene at 58 draws/s): the server sent 39.6 frames/s, the page drew 34.7, nobody dropped the excess, and the delay between decode() and the callback grew by ~108 ms every second — 4 650 ms after 43 s, with every frame counter green. The cause was a 34 ms drawImage of the 2D path. The cure skips the drawing, never the decoding, so the delta chain is intact and no key is needed. Since 26 Sep 2026 the rule is weighted by the measured drawing cost:

    Schermo.dipingi(): when a decoded frame is not drawn
    skip this frame  if  decodeQueueSize > 2  and  decodeQueueSize * costo_disegno() > 16 ms
costo_disegno()   = drawing cost: median time the callback holds the main thread
                    (+ median transfer-to-glass on the bitmaprenderer path)

    With a 34 ms drawing cost the rule fires at the old threshold; with WebGL2 at 0.26 ms it practically never fires, because skipping a 0.26 ms draw gains nothing — when the decoder itself is behind, the cure is the server's rate regulator. Every skipped frame is counted (saltati_coda, skipped by the queue): a rate that falls without a count would violate I1.

    The counters close, within a session: consegnati = usciti + inside the decoder and usciti = saltati_coda + dipinti + tardive + in_bmp + bmp_falliti. They were added on 23 Sep 2026 after a Firefox session showed 8 952 delivered and 6 929 drawn, with 2 007 frames that no counter named.

    9.11 · Drawing paths: WebGL2, bitmaprenderer, 2D canvas

    The decoded VideoFrame reaches the screen by one of three paths, chosen once when Schermo is built: a canvas takes only one context, so the choice cannot change during a session.

    The blocks. In August 2026 the user saw rectangular blocks of 64×192 pixels in still areas. They were hunted suspect by suspect, with a measurement each: the capture was clean, the encoder was clean (0 damaged superblocks out of 600 through ffmpeg), VideoFrame.copyTo was clean, and getImageData after the draw found 0 wrong pixels out of 180 000 — while a phone photo of the same canvas showed the rectangles. The pixels entered the 2D canvas correctly and broke on the way to the screen, in a stretch no API can read: getImageData reads the backing store, not what the compositor shows. Firefox and Chrome behaved alike, and a <video> on the same GPU was clean. The bitmaprenderer context has no 2D backing store, and the user's verdict on it was “NO ARTEFACTS!”. A second, overlapping defect on Firefox was its AV1 decoder, cured by the move to H.264.

    WebGL2. The stress campaign of phase 16 (anomaly A1) found that on Firefox the bitmaprenderer path reads every frame back from the GPU synchronously — about 34 ms at 4K — and the page skipped 11–62 % of frames. WebGL2's texImage2D has a fast path in Firefox (DMA-BUF and a GPU blit, YUV→RGB without read-back) when level 0, offset 0, RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE, no unpack skip, default colour space and visible rectangle equal to the coded one. Measured 26 Sep 2026 on Firefox at 4K: drawing 34 ms → 0.26 ms, skipped frames 60 % → 12 % (the rest was the old skip rule, then weighted by the drawing cost); the user, with a 4K video and a 30 000-fish WebGL aquarium: “the image is perfect, 45 fps steady, no stutter”, and no blocks. The multiple-of-16 canvas keeps the visible rectangle equal to the coded one; the log says once whether the fast path is possible.

    On every path the buffer is set to the frame size only when it changes (writing canvas.width clears it), explicitly: Chrome, unlike Firefox, does not resize a bitmaprenderer canvas on transfer, and a 16×16 buffer stretched by CSS once sent every click to the top-left corner. The pointer is never painted on the canvas; it is a CSS cursor or a separate element (10.4 “Mouse and pointer in the classic layout”).

    i
    A stale label. when Schermo is built on the WebGL2 path, it writes a log line describing that path as a candidate “requested with ?tela=gl”, “not the default”; the context-loss lines likewise advise reloading without ?tela=gl. Those texts predate 26 September and are stale. REMOTIX.tratti().strada reports webgl2-a-richiesta (WebGL2 on request) for the same reason.

    9.12 · Measurements made by the page

    The page measures its own share of the latency and exposes it, so that benches read the path really in use instead of a copy of it.

    REMOTIX.giro (round trip) is the full input round trip: each input message records when it left, and the input field of a later frame closes it. It is a lower bound — it stops when the frame arrives, not when it is drawn. SCENA (scene) samples the age of the image at every pointer move, which distinguishes “the desktop is frozen” from “the hand moved over the wallpaper and nothing changed”. voff_ms() (glass time minus the frame's server instant) is the video half of the audio/video distance; with the audio's aoff_ms(), the unknown clock offset cancels out (ch. 11 “Audio and clipboard”).

    Lines passed to nota() that contain MISURA (measurement), MARCA or ⛔ are also sent to the server with fetch("/diario?…") and appear in its log as 📄 la pagina di <address> dice: PAGINA … (the page of <address> says): with the desktop at full screen the page's own log is unreachable. The first lines identify the browser (user agent, screen, ratio, WebCodecs), the system (userAgentData on Chromium, navigator.oscpu on Firefox, each value labelled with its source) and what the engine offers without WebCodecs.

    +
    Reading the page. open the page with ?registro to see the log under the desktop, or call REMOTIX.registro(true) from the console; REMOTIX.tratti() and REMOTIX.schermo.conti can be read at any time.

    9.13 · End of session in the page

    A session ends for one of four reasons — a CONGEDO from the server, the transport closing without one, the page closing it, or the tab going away — and in each case the page must say what it knows and go back to a usable login form.

    torna_al_modulo() undoes everything the session turned on: the audio context is closed, Schermo.chiudi() closes the decoder and bumps the epoch (frames still in flight from before the farewell would otherwise put the desktop dress back on), the data-schermo dress is removed, pointer lock and full screen are released, the canvas returns to 16×16, the logout dialog is hidden, and focus goes to the user name. The rule written on it: whoever switches a state on must know how to switch it off.

    The first-frame watch. After SESSIONE the page says at once that the desktop is on its way — after a logout or a reboot the graphical session is born from scratch, measured 9 s and ~32 s — and after ATTESA_PRIMO_FOTOGRAMMA_S (first-frame wait) = 6 s without a frame it explains with numbers: if the granted canvas differs from the requested one, that is the likely cause; otherwise the server log has it.

    Logging out. The page keeps no key combination for itself since 17 August 2026: every combination reaches the remote desktop, and the user leaves from the desktop's own menu, which REMOTIX keeps available (ch. 12 “The four desktops”). TERMINA_SESSIONE (end the session) remains in the protocol and the confirmation dialog remains in the page, but no gesture opens it today.

    9.14 · The optional paths: video worker and MSE

    Two other ways of drawing exist in the file and are off: they are kept because they are measurable, and because each documents a decision.

    Whether to delete them is a cleanup decision for the end of the project (DECISIONI.md §7.16).

    9.15 · Browsers supported and untested

    The technical minimum is WebTransport and WebCodecs. The list below is the user's declaration of 22 August 2026 (DECISIONI.md §7.20), on the live product, plus what has never been tried.

    The rule behind the list: a page runs on three engines written by three teams who do not know REMOTIX — Blink, Gecko, WebKit — and testing on at least two of them gives back part of the external referee lost with native clients. Where two agree and the third does not, the defect names itself.

    !
    DeX and the pointer. on Samsung DeX, Chrome delivers mouse moves with no button pressed only around a click — the known noVNC issue #1727, also seen in KasmVNC #222 and in the native moonlight-android #573; it is not a REMOTIX defect. The page copes in two ways: since the canvas equals the window every event carries its own position, so pointing and clicking hit correctly even without hover; and since 3 October 2026 the first click on the canvas captures the pointer where hover does not arrive (DECISIONI.md §10.29). Details are in 10.4 “Mouse and pointer in the classic layout”.
    • Not settled yet: Safari on macOS and iOS has never been opened against REMOTIX.
    • Not settled yet: Firefox on Windows has never been opened against REMOTIX.
    • Not settled yet: Android's coming desktop mode, which may change the pointer behaviour; the capture rule looks at behaviour, not at the system, so it should adapt by itself.
    Chapter 10

    Input

    10.1 · Input at a glance

    Input travels the opposite way to video: from the browser page to the desktop of the remote session. The page turns mouse, keyboard and fingers into five RCP messages on a single unidirectional stream; the parent process validates them and passes them to the per-user child; the child injects them into the compositor through libei (GNOME and KDE) or through the Wayland virtual keyboard and pointer protocols (labwc, that is XFCE and LXQt).

    10.2 · The input messages

    Input uses five message types on the input channel, all big-endian, defined in RCP §7.3 and decoded by rcp_ricevi_input() (receive input). The client opens exactly one unidirectional stream for them, after SESSIONE (session), and keeps it open; a second input stream is a protocol error.

    Every message starts with the same two fields: u32 id and u64 istante (instant, a timestamp). The id grows by at least one on every message of the channel, whatever its type, and never takes the value 0, which means “no input”. It is the number that comes back in the input field of every video frame header (RCP §6.2): the child sets that field to the last id injected before the capture, not the last received, so a message refused by the compositor or a letter the layout cannot produce never claims an effect that the frame does not show. The istante is the client's monotonic clock in microseconds; no rule consumes it, it is kept for diagnosis.

    Codes are those of evdev (the kernel header linux/input-event-codes.h) because libei and the Wayland virtual devices both speak evdev: any other convention would add a translation table that fails silently. Coordinates outside the canvas close the session with ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO, except during the one-second grace after a TELA(ADATTATA) reply (canvas adapted), where they are saturated (RCP §7.1); the page saturates them anyway, three times over, because a closed session for a rounding error is the worst possible answer.

    Two control-channel messages belong to input as well: the keyboard layout declared in ATTACCA (attach, RCP §4.5) and DISPOSIZIONE (layout, 0x0009), which changes it while the session is open (10.11 “Keyboard layout negotiation”).

    i
    Clock grain. the page writes istante as Math.round(ms) * 1000 (cl_istante_us(), tocco_istante_us()), that is whole milliseconds. RCP §7.3 was corrected on 14 Aug 2026 to say that the client should write the real microseconds it has (5 µs grain on an isolated page in Chrome 151); the page code still rounds.

    10.3 · Classic and touch layouts in the page

    The page has two input layouts and chooses between them by itself, from what the device has and what the user is using, never from the user-agent string: DeX is Android with a real mouse, a laptop is Linux with a touch screen.

    A change of any media query discards the last observation and the context decides again: pick up the mouse and the page goes classic, touch the screen and it goes back to touch. The layout in force is written in body[data-disposizione] so that benches read it from the document. Leaving the touch layout resets the pinch zoom (with the mouse there is no panning, and part of the desktop would be unreachable: measured on DeX on 14 Aug 2026) and releases the button held by a tap-and-a-half; leaving the classic layout releases every key and button it pressed.

    Both layouts send through the same interface, window.REMOTIX_INPUT (prossimo_id(), next id; manda(), send), created right after SESSIONE together with the input stream, with a single writer so that messages leave in the order the user produced them. If the stream cannot be opened the session continues view-only, and the page says so. When the stream is congested (desiredSize at or below zero) a PUNTATORE is not queued: it is held aside and replaced by the next one, and the held position is always flushed before any key or button, so a click never travels with an old position. Measured from DeX on 14 Aug 2026: median input-to-frame loop 135 ms but worst case 2161 ms, which was a queue of stale pointer moves in front of a keystroke.

    10.4 · Mouse and pointer in the classic layout

    In the classic layout (cl_* functions, for “classic”, in pagina.html) the mouse is the primary path, including on DeX, which is the main Android use.

    One visible pointer. The page has three pointer modes (REMOTIX_PUNTATORE.modo()): sistema (system; the default since 14 Aug 2026), where the browser's own cursor takes the remote cursor shape through a CSS cursor: url(...) x y, default rule, the way Xpra does; disegnata (drawn), where the browser cursor is hidden and the page draws its arrow; and due (two), both arrows overlaid, kept for comparison. In the touch layout the drawn arrow stays, because a finger has no cursor to restyle. A zero-by-zero shape (RCP §5.5) means “hidden” and is applied in both modes. The cursor shape itself comes from the capture (ch. 6 “Screen capture per compositor”).

    Pointer Lock only where hover is missing. The lock is requested at the first click (the gesture it requires) only if, before that click, no move with buttons up arrived, or the last one is CL_SALTO_PX (jump threshold) = 8 px or more from the click point. On a computer the last move falls on the click and the lock never fires; on DeX moves with buttons up arrive only around clicks, and with the lock the borders of windows can be grabbed (user test, S23, Android 16, Chrome 154, 3 Oct 2026). The lock asks for unadjustedMovement (the client applies acceleration, CL_GUADAGNO, the gain, = 1.0); the first movement after the lock is dropped if longer than 100 CSS px (Chrome reports the jump of the system cursor); pushing 160 CSS px beyond an edge releases the lock, so that the DeX bar and the browser tabs stay reachable, while a pointer resting on the edge still triggers GNOME's hot corner.

    !
    A limit that is not ours. on Samsung devices (DeX included) Chrome does not deliver mouse moves with buttons up (noVNC #1727, open since 2022; the same on moonlight-android #573, a native app). Pointing, clicking and dragging land correctly; what is missing is the preview: the resize arrow on window borders, buttons lighting up, tooltips. The automatic Pointer Lock above reduces it.
    i
    Documents behind the code. SPECIFICHE.md §7.4 and a comment in cl_su_mousedown() still say that the lock is only manual through REMOTIX.input_classico.aggancia(). The code requests it automatically (cl_hover_manca(), “hover missing”) and REMOTIX.input_classico exposes no such function.

    10.5 · Wheel and scrolling

    The wheel has one sign convention on the wire and three on the way out; the sign is inverted exactly twice, once in the page and once in the server, and nowhere else.

    The sign was measured on 10 Aug 2026 on Mutter (libmutter 48.7, libei 1.3.901, Firefox 140): ei_device_scroll_discrete(0, +120) scrolled the page 114 px towards its end. Hence the server inversion. The horizontal axis of the touch gesture mirrors the vertical one and has not been judged. The wheel event also carries a position, and the page sends it first, for the same reason as a click.

    10.6 · Keyboard: letters and positions

    The keyboard sends letters when the user writes text and positions when the user gives a command. cl_comando() (is it a command?) decides: a key is a command when Ctrl, Meta or Alt (without AltGr) is down.

    The table CL_POSIZIONE maps KeyboardEvent.code to evdev by hand from the kernel table; positions are physical, so KeyZ is the key where Z sits on a US board, which writes Y on a German one. That is exactly why shortcuts travel as positions.

    Modifier resynchronisation. Because Shift alone is not sent, the page sends it at the moment a position key arrives while getModifierState("Shift") (or AltGr) is true but the page has not pressed it. Since 24 Sep 2026 this happens for every position key, not only for commands: before, Shift+← arrived as a bare arrow and did not select text on any of the four desktops. Conversely, before a LETTERA the page releases the Shift or AltGr it holds, because the server presses and releases its own Shift to produce the letter and on labwc that release would leave the page and the server disagreeing.

    Ctrl+V is the one command the page does not cancel. Calling preventDefault() on it would stop the browser paste, and with it the paste event that is the only free way to read the local clipboard on Firefox; the canvas is not editable, so the browser paste writes nowhere. When the clipboard is on, the V is also held back until the page has read the local clipboard and announced it, at most INCOLLA_TRATTIENI_MS (paste hold time) = 400 ms, with every key typed meanwhile queued behind it (11.11 “Clipboard in the browser”).

    Release on focus loss. On blur, on visibilitychange to hidden and on pagehide the page releases every key and button it pressed (cl_rilascia_tutto(), release all). The Keyboard Lock switches itself off precisely when the page loses focus, which is when a modifier is likely to be held; the session does not detach in that case, so the server-side release at detach would not help.

    i
    Privacy of keystrokes. by decision of 26 Sep 2026 (DECISIONI.md §9.2) the log never contains what the user types: neither characters nor key codes. Lines say “a character” or “key pressed”; codes are written only for modifiers and mouse buttons (on the server, registro_tasto_dicibile() in registro.c: whether a key code may be named in the log). It applies to unproducible characters too: the log says that one occurred, not which.

    10.7 · Shortcuts the browser keeps

    Some combinations never reach the page, and some reach it while the browser also runs its own command. The page declares them per engine and per screen state instead of pretending they work.

    The catalogue SC_CATALOGO holds, per engine family (blink, blink-app for an installed app, gecko) and per screen state (finestra window, intero full screen, intero+lock full screen with Keyboard Lock, F11), what is lost; it was measured on 14 Aug 2026 on GNOME/Wayland by injecting from a real keyboard path (org.gnome.Mutter.RemoteDesktop), with Chrome 151 and Firefox 140 ESR. Safari, Chrome on Android/DeX and Firefox 151 or later are listed as not tested (SC_NON_PROVATI), and an untested engine is never deduced from the others.

    On-screen buttons. SC_BOTTONI (buttons) lists five combinations that no browser lets through; only Ctrl+Alt+Del is active (user decision, 14 Aug 2026), because without it a locked session cannot be entered at all. It is sent as positions 29, 56, 111 down and up in reverse. Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Alt+F4 and Super are present but off: switching one on is attivo: true (active).

    10.8 · Touch gestures

    The touch layout turns the phone screen into a trackpad: the finger pushes a pointer drawn by the page, and clicks happen where the pointer is, not where the finger lands.

    The thresholds are a declared starting point, judged by using them. Four design points are not thresholds, and each came from a failing bench run (04-b28-gesti.py, gestures, 14 Aug 2026):

    • Tap-and-a-half and double click are the same gesture. At the second contact the two have produced the same events, so the button is pressed at contact and released at lift: a quick lift is the second click of a double click, a drag is a drag. Waiting to decide would delay every double click.
    • Two fingers make a two-finger gesture if they are down together for at least one sample. Two non-overlapping taps are two one-finger taps, so a badly timed right click comes out as a left double click; the only cure would delay every click by 300 ms, above the 50 ms budget.
    • A tap is short if every contact is short, not the whole gesture: three fingers never land and lift together.
    • When the set of fingers changes, the two-finger reference is rebuilt and nothing is decided in that sample: three fingers lifting one by one move the centre by tens of pixels without any movement, which used to be read as a wheel.

    Wheel and pinch are both “two moving fingers”: the page compares the change of distance with the movement of the centre, takes the larger once, and keeps that decision for the whole gesture. The pointer is moved on every touch sample, without coalescing and without requestAnimationFrame (which never ran on the Xvfb bench). Times come from event.timeStamp when plausible (within 5 s of performance.now()), otherwise from the handler time, declared.

    10.9 · The on-screen keyboard on a phone

    With the phone in hand the system keyboard opens only on request (DECISIONI.md §10.28, 2 Oct 2026), through a small ⌨ button at the top right that exists only in the touch layout.

    1. Why. The hidden paste field is always focused, and on Android a focused text field opens the keyboard, which covered half the desktop for 60 % of a test and typed nothing (measured on an S23+ with Chrome 154).
    2. The field. In the touch layout it carries inputmode="none" and virtualkeyboardpolicy="manual" (and no autocapitalisation or autocorrection); in the classic layout none of these attributes is present, so paste and keys are unchanged.
    3. The button. tastiera_commuta() (toggle keyboard) switches inputmode to text, re-focuses the field inside the user's touch, and calls navigator.virtualKeyboard.show() where it exists. The button never takes focus. It sits at the top because the open keyboard covers the bottom.
    4. What is typed. tastiera_su_input() compares the field with what was already sent: the common prefix stays, every vanished character becomes Backspace (position 14), every new one a LETTERA; newline and tab become Enter and Tab positions. Autocorrection works by rewriting the word. Outside composition the field is emptied.
    5. Real keys (Enter and Backspace on an empty field, a Bluetooth keyboard without a mouse) are handled in tastiera_su_keydown(); if code is empty, as can happen on Android, the key name is used.
    6. Closing. The button again, or Android's back gesture, recognised when the visual viewport grows back above 85 % of the window height.

    10.10 · From a letter to key positions

    tastiera.c (keyboard) solves the reverse problem of a keyboard: given a character, which keys must be pressed on the session's layout to make the compositor produce it. It works on the keymap the session itself handed over, compiled with xkbcommon.

    input_lettera() (input a letter) presses the modifiers first and the key last, releases in reverse order, and if a press fails halfway it releases what it already pressed. It returns 0 when sent, 1 when the character is not producible (the log line is written by tastiera_posizioni_per(), positions for a character, which knows the layout name), −1 on a fault; values outside the Unicode scalar range are protocol errors, not “unproducible”. xkbcommon's own log is redirected so that a layout that does not compile says why, and the layout name always includes what the compiled keymap calls itself (“it [Italian]”), so a silent fallback would read “it [English (US)]”.

    10.11 · Keyboard layout negotiation

    The layout is negotiated at every attach, like the canvas, for two reasons: to make characters reachable and to make shortcut positions match. The client proposes, the server asks the session, and the session's real keymap is always the one in force.

    1. The page proposes a layout in ATTACCA from navigator.language (disposizione(), layout): en becomes us (or gb/ie by region), sv → se, da → dk, cs → cz, el → gr, he → il, ja → jp, ko → kr, uk → ua, thirty languages whose XKB name equals the ISO code pass unchanged, everything else becomes us. Until 10 Aug 2026 the page sent en, which is not an XKB name, and the server rightly refused the session of every English-language browser.
    2. The server checks the form (disposizione_ben_formata(), well-formed layout): at most 64 characters in all, a name of [A-Za-z0-9_-] optionally followed by a non-empty variant of the same characters in parentheses. Dots, slashes and commas are refused because the string ends up in XKB's include machinery, which opens files by name. A bad form is ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO.
    3. The server checks existence by compiling it with xkbcommon (gancio_disposizione_esiste(), the layout-exists hook, → tastiera_apri_per()). At attach an unknown layout is SESSIONE_NON_SERVIBILE (session cannot be served); the fixed list of twenty layouts of phase 1 is only a declared fallback when the hook is missing. Until 16 Aug 2026 that list refused hu, tr, gr and ua, which were installed.
    4. The child asks the session (input_disposizione()), after releasing everything pressed, unless the current keymap already does the same thing as the requested layout (compared key by key, tastiera_e_questa(), “is the keyboard this one”): a needless change costs Mutter the destruction of the keyboard device.
    5. The keymap confirms. The compositor recreates the keyboard device with the new keymap; leggi_keymap() reads it, fingerprints it (size plus hash, since Mutter names every keymap (unnamed)) and writes KEYMAP CAMBIATA (keymap changed). If the session layout differs from the requested one, tastiera.c writes RIPIEGO DICHIARATO (declared fallback) and uses the session's.

    While the session is open, DISPOSIZIONE (0x0009) changes the layout: a well-formed unknown layout does not close the session (the previous keyboard still works, and “never detach” applies); the same layout as the current one asks nothing; there is no reply on the wire. The page does not send this message today.

    i
    Not settled yet: a page cannot know the physical layout of the keyboard in front of it; navigator.language is a hint. Letting the user choose is the real cure and has not been decided.

    10.12 · Injection through libei

    On GNOME and KDE the child is a libei sender on a socket that the compositor hands over: ConnectToEIS on the Mutter RemoteDesktop session (asked before Start, see mutter_apri()) or connectToEIS on org.kde.KWin.EIS.RemoteDesktop with the capability mask 7 (keyboard, pointer, touch) and a token.

    !
    The handshake that must not be interrupted. until 25 Aug 2026 input_chiudi() called ei_disconnect() and ei_unref() unconditionally, and a channel opened 33 ms earlier killed the child with SIGSEGV before the first frame. In libei 1.3.901, a context whose handshake was requested but not answered has a NULL connection that ei_disconnect() dereferences, and ei_unref() calls it first. The cure (D4): EI_EVENT_CONNECT marks the handshake; without it the context is abandoned (its descriptors closed, the memory lost, the count kept in input_abbandoni(), the abandonment count), and input_gira() (the input loop step) checks with a zero-timeout poll() whether the compositor hung up before dispatching a context whose handshake is incomplete.

    10.13 · Pressed keys: counting, releasing, healing

    Input keeps a ledger of everything pressed (RCP §11), because a modifier or a button left down in a session that outlives its client makes the desktop unusable, and nobody connects the two.

    Why orphans exist. Measured on 16 and 21 Aug 2026 with a Wayland test client inside the session: hold BTN_LEFT, let Mutter recreate the absolute pointer (canvas change, or simply a capture wake-up on a still desktop), then release. The release never arrives, and from then on no click arrives at all, while the keyboard keeps working. The chain is in Mutter: remove_viewport_devices removes the device without drop_device(); the new device silently swallows a release it never saw pressed; and the seat counts presses across devices, so it stays at one forever. A press-release on the new device makes the count go 1 → 2 → 1. Only the drop of the EIS client resets it, and it is the ei_disconnect() message, not the closing of the descriptor, that triggers it (both verified with injected faults). Releasing before a resize and cure A close the doors that REMOTIX controls; cure C repairs the doors it does not control (monitors-changed, keymap changes, and whatever GNOME adds: meta_eis_viewport_notify_changed() is new in GNOME 48.5).

    Keyboard devices are not recreated by geometry changes (measured: zero keyboard swaps out of fifteen pointer swaps) but they are by keymap changes, which is why every layout change starts with input_rilascia_tutto().

    10.14 · Virtual keyboard and pointer on labwc

    labwc has no libei. wlr_input.c creates our own virtual keyboard (zwp_virtual_keyboard_manager_v1) and pointer (zwlr_virtual_pointer_manager_v1) on the user's Wayland socket; input.c keeps the same contract on top of it, branching at the top of every public function, so the GNOME and KDE paths are untouched.

    Measured on 21 Sep 2026 on the laptop, with a private headless labwc 0.8.3 (the Trixie version) and the test client 06-b33-testimone.c (the “witness”), not on the test server nor in a full XFCE session: Shift arrives as a modifier before the letter; CapsLock pressed three times locks once; +120 from the client is one notch up and two halves of 60 are one notch; absolute positions are exact and saturated; a double press with one release gives one pair; switching to de puts Z on key 21; closing with Ctrl and left button down releases both.

    !
    Shortcuts belong to labwc. labwc applies its own keybindings to virtual keys too. Measured on 21 Sep 2026 (laptop, headless labwc): Alt+F4 from our channel closes the test client's window, which sees Alt and never F4. It is the desktop's behaviour, and on XFCE what the user expects.

    Bringing windows back inside. On labwc a shrinking output leaves large windows partly outside the right and bottom edges. After every resize the child calls input_riporta_dentro() (bring back inside), which releases everything and types the unused shortcut SESSIONE_LABWC_TASTO (the labwc session key, W-C-A-S-F12, i.e. Super+Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12) that REMOTIX writes into labwc's configuration, then puts the pointer back where the user had it. On GNOME and KDE the function does nothing, because the compositor already does it. The shortcut itself is described in 12.8 “Output size on labwc”.

    10.15 · Input decisions

    The main decisions of the input subsystem, with the reason that made each one.

    Chapter 11

    Audio and clipboard

    11.1 · Audio at a glance

    The session's sound is the mix of every application in it: REMOTIX creates a virtual sink in the session's PipeWire, captures its monitor, encodes 48 kHz stereo blocks and sends one per QUIC datagram. The page decodes Opus with its own WebAssembly decoder and schedules each block at the time the server stamped on it.

    i
    Volume and microphone. the session volume belongs to the session and is set to maximum at every connection (invariant I5); RCP carries no volume. Microphone input (client to session) is foreseen by SPECIFICHE.md §10 as not urgent and RCP/1 defines no format for it. Not settled yet: the microphone.

    11.2 · The audio format and its datagram

    The audio format is fixed, not negotiated (RCP §5.3): two implementations choosing two sample rates would produce noise that looks like a network fault. Only the codec is negotiated.

    PCM is 5 ms and not 20 ms because a QUIC datagram cannot be fragmented: 20 ms of PCM would be 3852 bytes. The largest datagram measured on 17 Aug 2026 (07-b40, wired LAN) was 1024 bytes on Chrome 151, and on Firefox 140 1024 bytes at ready growing to 1214 after 800 ms: PCM fits by 52 bytes. The little-endian byte order of PCM is the only exception to network order in RCP, declared because it is payload, not a protocol field. A datagram shorter than 12 bytes or with another type is discarded and counted, never a reason to close the connection: a datagram is unreliable by definition.

    Negotiation. audio.codec is a capability that both sides declare in CIAO (hello) / ECCOMI (here I am); pcm is mandatory on both sides as the always-available base and positive control of Opus. The page declares opus,pcm only if its WebAssembly decoder loads, or, failing that, if AudioDecoder supports Opus; otherwise only pcm: declaring opus would oblige the server to choose it and nothing would be heard. The server picks inside the intersection following the client's order and logs the choice; the child then opens the encoder for that codec (audio_regola_figlio(), set the child's audio) and never falls back to PCM by itself, which would produce noise instead of an error.

    Audio goes before video. In every write pass of the transport the pending datagrams enter the packet before stream bytes, so on a congestion window of two or three packets audio takes the place of video (SPECIFICHE.md §10.1). A late audio block is useless, a late frame is still a frame. The price is bounded by construction: the datagram queue holds WT_DGRAM_MAX = 8.

    11.3 · The session sink and its capture

    A server has no sound card, and a headless session has no sink at all: measured in v1 on 5 Aug 2026, wpctl status showed zero devices, zero sinks, zero sources with PipeWire, pipewire-pulse and WirePlumber all running. suono_apri() (open sound) therefore creates one.

    The volume measurement that justified monitor.channel-volumes (8 Aug 2026, a 440 Hz tone at 25.9 % of full scale read on the monitor): with the sink at 100 %, 25 % and 0 %, the capture read 25.39 %, 25.39 %, 25.39 % without the property, and 25.39 %, 0.40 %, 0.00 % with it, which is exactly the cubic volume curve. suono_volume_massimo() (maximum volume) sets channel volumes to 1.0 and mute off at creation, at every connection and at every start of the capture, because whoever restores saved levels does so when the node appears and wins the race at creation.

    11.4 · From samples to datagrams

    Between PipeWire's real-time thread and the child's loop sits a lock-free single-producer, single-consumer ring of one second (AUDIO_ANELLO_FOTOGRAMMI (ring frames) = 48 000 frames, 192 000 bytes): the producer moves only the head, the consumer only the tail.

    !
    Real-time priority is declared, not assumed. PipeWire collects samples on its real-time thread only if it gets SCHED_FIFO. dichiara_priorita_audio() (declare audio priority) checks the threads of the audio path and logs whether they are FIFO/RR. Measured on 21 Aug 2026: on a kernel with CONFIG_RT_GROUP_SCHED and cgroup v2, SCHED_FIFO is refused to any process outside the root cgroup, so the LimitRTPRIO of the service is inert, and audio crackles when the desktop works. An independent pw-record on the same monitor hears the same crackles: the fault is born in the session's audio graph, not in the transport.

    11.5 · The Opus encoder

    audio.c encodes with libopus directly since 30 Sep 2026: ffmpeg left the product for licence reasons (DECISIONI.md §10.22, §10.25), and libavcodec was only a wrapper around the same libopus.so.0. The parameters are the ones that wrapper used, and the packets were verified identical byte for byte (18-a1-opus-senza-ffmpeg.c, libopus 1.5.2).

    One block in, one packet out. Measured on 17 Aug 2026 (07-b44): 1000 blocks in, 1000 packets out, no delay. opus_encode() is synchronous, so istante always belongs to the block that leaves. The encoder has a look-ahead of 312 samples (6.5 ms), read with OPUS_GET_LOOKAHEAD and written in the log at open; the decoder removes it, so it cancels end to end, but anyone using these timestamps for audio/video sync must know about it.

    Digital silence is not sent. A block whose samples are all exactly zero produces no datagram: the receiver places blocks at their absolute istante, so a gap is silence, which is what the block contained. Measured on 24 Aug 2026 (09-b84): on a still desktop with Opus, 50 datagrams per second of 3 bytes cost 589 kbit/s of padded packets and shared the congestion window with video. On by default since 24 Aug 2026 (user decision); the only switch is the server option --niente-audio-silenzio (no audio silence), which the parent copies into the child's command line, and which also applies to the test tone of --audio-prova (audio test) opened in the parent.

    11.6 · Playing audio in the page

    The page has its own Opus decoder: libopus 1.5.2 compiled to WebAssembly, decode only, embedded in pagina.html as base64 (D-006, decided 25 Sep 2026). AudioDecoder remains only as a declared fallback where WebAssembly is missing; PCM needs no decoder.

    Why. Firefox with a video playing in the session had short repeated sound gaps (0.1–0.4 s) and Chrome did not. Measured on 25 Sep 2026, 60 s on LXQt and KDE: Firefox with video 3–5 re-anchors, Firefox without video 0, Chrome 0, Firefox with video in PCM 0. The only difference was Firefox's AudioDecoder, which under video load returns blocks late and in bunches. A decoder that answers in the same call has no queue. The user rejected a Firefox-only branch: the same path runs on every browser. It runs on the main thread, because a block costs about 0.1 ms and the AudioContext lives there anyway.

    Scheduling. The page never waits for audio: a block that arrives late is dropped. Each block is an AudioBufferSourceNode started at base + istante, where the anchor base maps the server clock onto the AudioContext clock and is set at the first block to give a cushion of AUDIO_CUSCINO_MS (cushion) = 250 ms. Because playback time depends on the block's own timestamp and not on how many blocks arrived, a lost datagram no longer shortens the cushion for ever: before this cure (measured 21 Aug 2026 on a real Windows session) 61 lost blocks in 3½ minutes walked the queue from 419 down to 79 ms and produced three audible gaps.

    A new AudioContext and a fresh decoder are created at each collega(), and the old ones are closed first: Chrome refuses a seventh context per document, and the exception used to stop datagram reading for the rest of the session. aoff_ms() (playback time of a sample minus its server timestamp, plus outputLatency) is the audio half of the audio/video distance metric; it is updated only by blocks that actually played and expires after 600 ms without sound.

    11.7 · Clipboard at a glance

    The clipboard carries plain text only, in both directions (DECISIONI.md §5-ter.1, decided by the user on 9 Aug 2026 and confirmed on the 17th). Text covers almost every use, costs a few bytes and has no format negotiation; images would open the question of formats and of who pays the bandwidth when an 8 MB screenshot is copied on a link that is struggling.

    The protocol announces and pulls instead of pushing: whoever copies a whole document sends it to nobody until somebody pastes. The direction used most is device to session, and it is the harder one, because on the device side the clipboard belongs to the browser.

    11.8 · The clipboard messages and their limits

    Three messages on the clipboard channel (RCP §7.4), each transfer on its own unidirectional stream (high byte 0x02), so several transfers can be alive together.

    The Ctrl+V race. When the user pastes in the remote desktop with Ctrl+V, the keys and the announcement of the freshly copied local text travel on different streams, and the remote application may ask before the announcement arrives. Xpra delays every keystroke by 100 ms; for REMOTIX that is twice the latency budget, paid on every key. Two cheaper cures instead: the server queues a paste request while the client has announced nothing yet (rcp_appunti_chiedi(), up to A_STREAM_MAX = 8 requests, one APPUNTI_CHIEDI for the whole batch), and the page holds back the V of Ctrl+V until its own announcement has left (11.11 “Clipboard in the browser”).

    Always answer the compositor. A paste request from the session that is left unanswered leaves the pasting application waiting for ever, and the user sees a frozen desktop. The child, which owns the session, keeps up to APPUNTI_IN_VOLO (in flight) = 8 requests in flight and answers “nothing” after APPUNTI_ATTESA_MS (clipboard wait) = 4000 ms, or at once when no client can serve it. The parent may have no client attached, the client may vanish mid-transfer, and the parent itself may die: the debt towards the compositor stays where the session is.

    11.9 · Clipboard on GNOME

    On GNOME the clipboard belongs to Mutter (MetaSelection); the RemoteDesktop session only owns the door to it (EnableClipboard). appunti.c (clipboard) uses that door on the session that mutter.c already opened.

    • The text types, in this order and nowhere else: text/plain;charset=utf-8, UTF8_STRING, text/plain (TIPI_TESTO, text types).
    • The text is read in the module, on the clipboard thread, because the announcement needs its length; the limit and UTF-8 validity are checked there, where the text is still whole; the last text copied in the session is remembered (appunti_ultimo_testo(), last text), so that a client that reconnects finds it (invariant I4).
    • The clipboard is enabled with empty options, so Mutter immediately reports who owns the selection; and at every attach the child reads the current selection with appunti_leggi_adesso() (read now) before offering anything, because Mutter does not tell a new session who owns it and the clipboard would be lost.
