    • GDBus delivers signals to the context of the subscribing thread, and no REMOTIX thread runs a GLib loop: the module runs a private context on its own thread. Its callbacks may write to the socket towards the parent (a SOCK_SEQPACKET send is atomic) but must never touch libei.
    • Mutter's X11 bridge is unconditional in both directions, so xclip works without a REMOTIX session: the clipboard benches have an external referee.

    11.10 · Clipboard on KDE and labwc

    On KDE Plasma and on labwc (XFCE and LXQt) the same module, appunti_kde.c, speaks the wlroots data-control protocol on the user's Wayland socket: appunti_apri_kde() and appunti_apri_wlroots() differ only in the compositor name used in log lines. The child chooses with sessione_su_wlroots() first, then KDE, then GNOME.

    i
    Clipboard managers. the LXQt test box excludes qlipper, which dirties the clipboard; on the user's machine a clipboard manager can still interfere.

    11.11 · Clipboard in the browser

    In the browser the clipboard is not REMOTIX's: the page gets it only under conditions that differ on every engine. The rule of SPECIFICHE.md §9 applies to the letter: what cannot be done is declared, never faked.

    1. The hidden V. On every Ctrl+V with the clipboard on, the V is held (incolla_trattieni(), paste hold) until the page has read the local clipboard and, if it changed, its announcement has left; at most INCOLLA_TRATTIENI_MS = 400 ms. Any key typed meanwhile, Ctrl's release included, queues behind it, or the desktop would receive a plain v. Only this key waits.
    2. Why the server queue is not enough. After a copy made in the remote desktop the clipboard belongs to the remote application, the remote paste does not ask the server, and the first paste gave the remote text (user test, 2 Oct 2026). And when the client had already announced A, a new copy of B was served as A because B's announcement was still on its way (measured, F-014D 7 of 8).
    3. Echoes. The page remembers the last text read or written (ultimo_letto, last read) and does not announce it again, unless the remote desktop was the last owner: then identical text is announced anyway, or the next paste would give the remote text.
    4. Size. Over 1 000 000 bytes the page does not announce and says so; an incoming announcement over the limit is a protocol error.

    Every step of the clipboard in the page also goes to the server's diary (/diario, the page's log route), because with the desktop full screen the page log cannot be read, and the silence of “no announcement arrived” had six possible causes in the page (measured on Firefox, 17 Aug 2026: the cause was the page's own preventDefault() on Ctrl+V). With the phone in hand the paste field must not open the system keyboard (10.9 “The on-screen keyboard on a phone”). Safari is not tested.

    11.12 · Audio and clipboard decisions

    The decisions of audio and clipboard, with the reason that made each one.

    Chapter 12

    The four desktops

    12.1 · Desktops at a glance

    REMOTIX serves four Wayland desktops, which belong to three compositor families. Capture, input and clipboard talk to the compositor; birth, logout and settings talk to the desktop. XFCE and LXQt share labwc and therefore almost everything except the session.

    One desktop per machine (DECISIONI.md §0.6, 20 Sep 2026; §4.6-duodetricies): REMOTIX looks for the desktop that is installed, it does not arbitrate between desktops that coexist, and the --compositore (compositor) option of v1 is not coming back. Machines with several desktops are out of scope; when two are found the choice is made and declared “ambiguous”. Only Wayland sessions are served; X11 applications run through XWayland.

    The four desktops were added one per phase (12 KDE, 13 XFCE, 14 LXQt) under the user's rule “add the new desktop without breaking what already works”: every desktop branch is placed in front of the GNOME code, which stays textually unchanged and is skipped with a return or goto.

    12.2 · Recognising the desktop

    riconosci_desktop() (recognise the desktop) decides once per process, from the programs in PATH, and keeps the reason in words for the server's start line (sessione_desktop_spiega(), “explain”).

    • The XFCE marker is xfce4-session, not labwc: labwc is the family's compositor, shared with LXQt, and remains a precondition.
    • Until phase 12 a machine with neither GNOME nor KDE was declared GNOME by fallback; on an XFCE box the failure surfaced as “another drop-in wins over mine” and “Mutter does not expose RemoteDesktop”, two innocents accused (measured 20 Sep 2026). The fallback was removed: NESSUNO is honesty, not a desktop.
    • SessioneDesktop travels as a uint32_t between parent and child, so new values go at the end: GNOME 0, KDE 1, XFCE 2, none 3, LXQt 4.
    • Capture, input, clipboard and stage rebuild ask sessione_su_wlroots() (XFCE or LXQt), not “is it XFCE”: with five comparisons against XFCE, LXQt would have fallen silently into the GNOME/KDE branch.

    12.3 · The environment of a session

    The environment of the session is composed, not inherited (componi_ambiente(), “compose the environment”): whatever the starter carries ends up in the user's systemd manager and in D-Bus activation, where it outlives the compositor. A stray LC_ALL=C from an SSH shell once stopped every application from opening.

    The render node. wlroots is given the first /dev/dri/renderD* that can actually be opened (the numbers swap between boots, and on the test machine the second node is a card excluded on purpose), and REMOTIX first checks with GBM that a 256×256 XRGB8888 buffer can be created on it. If not, WLR_RENDERER=pixman is set and declared: otherwise wlroots would fall back to software in silence, or the canvas would be black.

    Starting. avvia() (start) runs setsid --fork sh -c with the composed environment and the user's home as working directory, with the session's output appended to ~/.local/state/remotix/sessione.log (the session log, under $XDG_STATE_HOME; a directory and file that must belong to the user and not be writable by others, opened with O_NOFOLLOW), or to $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/remotix-sessione.log as a declared fallback. Because of setsid --fork the session lives outside the server's unit: measured on 29 Sep 2026, stopping the unit or killing the parent or the child kills no desktop on any of the four, and a reattach finds the same compositor and windows. The child does not wait for the birth: sessione_fai_nascere() (bring the session to life) starts it only from a dead session and returns at once (at most one request a minute); the child's retry loop (1 s doubling to 30 s) finds the session on a later round. The 40 s wait ATTESA_AVVIO_MS belongs to the blocking sessione_assicura(), which the product no longer calls. The life cycle is in ch. 3 “Startup and life cycle”.

    12.4 · GNOME sessions

    GNOME is started through the distribution's own session, with a systemd drop-in that makes gnome-shell headless and without monitors: the only monitor is the virtual one that the capture creates with RecordVirtual, and that is where GNOME puts its top bar and dock.

    1. Which session (D8, sessione_gnome()): among wayland-sessions/*.desktop entries that run gnome-session with an installed .session file, take the only one if there is just one, otherwise prefer the one named after the distribution (ID of os-release, e.g. ubuntu), then gnome, then the first alphabetically, as GDM does; if none, gnome as a declared fallback. The Exec line is used as the command, DesktopNames as XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP.
    2. Which shell unit (unita_shell(), “shell unit”): up to GNOME 49 org.gnome.Shell@wayland.service; from GNOME 50 the template org.gnome.Shell@.service with --mode=%i, whose instance is the one that gnome-session@<session>.target requires (@user for gnome, @ubuntu on Ubuntu 26.04). Chosen from what is installed, not from a version number.
    3. The drop-in zz-remotix-monitor.conf in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/systemd/user.control/<unit>.d/ replaces ExecStart with gnome-shell --headless --no-x11 (plus --mode=%i for the template), then daemon-reload. No root needed, gone at reboot, and named zz- so that it applies after any system drop-in. It is written in the instance directory, never the template's, which would also apply to GDM's shell.
    4. The check: REMOTIX re-reads the ExecStart in force; if it lacks the expected arguments, or still contains --virtual-monitor (an old drop-in in /etc/systemd/user), birth is refused and declared: the session would have its own monitor, the capture would add a second, and the user would watch an empty screen.
    5. The previous session must be over: both gnome-session-manager@<session>.service and gnome-session-restart-dbus.service inactive. A session started while GNOME restarts the session bus dies without writing anything (measured 16 Aug 2026).

    The session dconf (D-015, sessione_dconf_prepara(), “prepare”). The child writes $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/remotix/dconf/profilo (the profile) with an in-memory database service-db:shm/remotix on top and the user's databases below, read-only, and sets DCONF_PROFILE before any GSettings call; the session gets the same variable. Everything the remote session writes goes to memory and never to the user's settings, so nothing has to be restored after a crash. The database is emptied at each new birth. Prices, declared: what the user changes from the remote desktop (wallpaper, a shortcut) is lost when the session is reborn; a mandatory profile in /run/dconf/user/<uid> wins over the variable, and then the cure cannot apply and is declared.

    The user decided on 25 Sep 2026 that the user's settings are not touched except those about lock screen, reboot, suspend and standby, which are dangerous for other users of the machine; those are written to the user's dconf writer (gnome_metti_utente(), “put in the user”) and then read back through the session profile, as the shell will read them. Every schema is looked up first: g_settings_new() on a missing schema aborts the process. sessione_inibisci() (inhibit) asks org.gnome.SessionManager.Inhibit with flags SUSPEND | IDLE (4 | 8 = 12; never LOGOUT), and the cookie is never released: it lives as long as the session.

    12.5 · KDE Plasma sessions

    Plasma is started with startplasma-wayland, which starts KWin as the user unit plasma-kwin_wayland.service; REMOTIX overrides its ExecStart the same way as GNOME's shell.

    The KWin drop-in (zz-remotix-monitor.conf), here for a 1920×1080 canvas
    [Service]
ExecStart=
ExecStart=/usr/bin/kwin_wayland_wrapper --xwayland --virtual --width 1920 --height 1080 --no-lockscreen

    Alive means org.kde.KWin owns its name on the session bus; the previous session is over when both plasma-kwin_wayland.service and plasma-workspace.target are inactive. sessione_impostazioni() writes nothing else for Plasma: the desktop lock is off from the command line (--no-lockscreen).

    12.6 · XFCE sessions on labwc

    XFCE on Wayland has no compositor of its own: it runs on labwc. There is no systemd unit to override, so scrivi_dropin() (write the drop-in) has nothing to do and REMOTIX starts the compositor itself.

    The XFCE command line for a 1920×1080 canvas, simplified (the inner script is built by primario_misurato(), “sized primary client”)
    exec labwc -m --session "sh -c 'u=$(wlr-randr | sed -n 1s/ .*//p);
    wlr-randr --output $u --custom-mode 1920x1080; exec xfce4-session'"
    !
    A successful write is not an applied setting. xfconf-query exits with 0 even when the daemon refused and restored the old value: the API is asynchronous and the local cache answers first. Every key REMOTIX writes (xfconf_metti(), “set in xfconf”) is therefore read back, and only a read-back value counts as applied.

    Alive means org.xfce.SessionManager owns its name on the user bus (labwc is started without dbus-run-session). The previous session is over when no labwc process of the user is left, read from /proc (processi_miei(), “my processes”): asked about a unit that does not exist, systemd would answer inactive, and the guard would vanish instead of failing.

    12.7 · LXQt sessions on labwc

    Debian Trixie packages no launcher for LXQt on Wayland (no lxqt-wayland-session, no startlxqtwayland). REMOTIX writes the line itself, modelled on the upstream launcher 0.1.1 (labwc branch), with one deliberate difference: the labwc configuration directory is ours.

    The LXQt command line, simplified
    exec labwc -C "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/remotix/labwc-lxqt" -S "sh -c '...wlr-randr as for XFCE...; exec lxqt-session'"

    Alive means org.lxqt.session owns its name on the user bus; the name appears in the constructor, before the modules, so a lxqt-session dying at start would be read as a user log-out (not measured). Log-out is org.lxqt.session.logout on /LXQtSession, sent without waiting for a reply (it is declared no-reply), then SIGTERM to labwc if the session is still there.

    i
    The LXQt package set. the test box for LXQt installs lxqt-core qt6-wayland lxqt-menu-data lxqt-powermanagement plus kf6-breeze-icon-theme qt6-svg-plugins (without them the panel has no icons and no menu button) and wlr-randr, and excludes lxqt-branding-debian, qlipper, swayidle, swaylock, wlopm and kanshi. On a normal machine apt pulls the recommended icon packages.

    12.8 · Output size on labwc

    On labwc the output size is not part of the birth: the headless output is born 1280×720, hard-wired (measured 20 Sep 2026), and no protocol creates one of a chosen size. REMOTIX resizes it as a Wayland client, twice.

    Bringing windows back inside (D-007, measured 25 Sep 2026). When the output shrinks, labwc moves a floating window only if its centre leaves the screen; on the right and bottom edges large windows stay partly outside. No Wayland protocol lets a client move other clients' windows, and resizing in two steps does not help because labwc restores the pre-change position. The only labwc action that keeps a window inside on the right and bottom is the move-to-cursor placement; with the pointer warped to the window centre it means “move it as little as possible”. REMOTIX therefore writes into labwc's configuration a keybinding nobody uses, W-C-A-S-F12, whose actions do it in four flat passes (labwc 0.8.3 does not nest ForEach), and the child types it after each resize (10.14 “Virtual keyboard and pointer on labwc”).

    • Full-screen windows have no query of their own: labwc does not change the decoration of a full-screen window and does not shade it, so only windows that did change are moved.
    • Moves use the border only, never the title bar, or the window would drop by half a bar at every pass.
    • All passes run inside one labwc action, so no frame shows the temporary border.
    • Prices, declared and rare: a window the user had set to border-only comes back without border; a shaded one comes back unshaded. The pointer is put back where the user had it.
    • labwc 0.8.3 marks MoveToCursor deprecated; the configuration uses AutoPlace policy="cursor", which calls the same function.

    12.9 · What is removed from the session menus

    Nobody may shut down, reboot, suspend or hibernate the server, the person sitting in front of it included (DECISIONI.md §4.7, user decision of 15 Aug 2026): shutting down is the one gesture that takes away every session at once, and whoever does it from a desktop menu cannot see who is connected. Inside the remote desktop the user has a single gesture that ends something: log-out.

    The menu work is cosmetic on top of three system-wide belts, which the package ships inert under /usr/share/remotix/cinture/ (the belts), where nothing reads them; since DECISIONI.md §10.36 the installer no longer puts them in force, so the “refused by polkit” entries above hold only where the administrator has installed them. They are: a polkit rule (remotix-niente-spegnimento.rules, “no power-off”, shipped as 50-remotix-niente-spegnimento.rules) that says no to every power action of logind, including the *-multiple-sessions and *-ignore-inhibit variants that v1 had missed; the logind keys of remotix-tasti.conf (“keys”: HandlePowerKey, suspend, hibernate, reboot and lid switch, with their long-press variants, all ignore), because a physical key does not go through polkit; and the [Sleep] section of remotix-niente-sospensione.conf (“no suspend”). Root keeps CAP_SYS_BOOT and can still run systemctl poweroff (measured 15 Aug 2026: CanPowerOff is no for a user and yes for root); attached clients are told with the farewell reason SERVER_IN_CHIUSURA (server closing). Details in 14.10 “The power belts, shipped inert”.

    i
    What is left visible. in lxqt-leave, reached from fancymenu's fixed Leave button when the user's own panel configuration wins, shut down, reboot and suspend are grey and “Lock screen” is clickable but inert. On XFCE the separate “Log Out” window keeps grey entries. Both are declared residues.

    12.10 · Ending a session and tidying up

    sessione_termina() (end the session) ends the graphical session when the product must (for instance when the same user logs in locally, invariant I2: the local session wins, and two graphical sessions on one XDG_RUNTIME_DIR would make the local one fail). It asks first and insists afterwards.

    After each step REMOTIX waits up to ATTESA_USCITA_MS (exit wait) = 10 s, checking every 500 ms that the session is not alive and its units are inactive (not merely “not active”: deactivating is a trap), then runs systemctl --user reset-failed. An application with unsaved changes may inhibit a polite log-out and show a dialog that nobody in an unattended session will close; that is why the second step exists.

    Tidying up after a session. Once the session is dead, never while it lives:

    • sessione_sgombera_scope() (clear the scope) closes what is left of the user's processes in REMOTIX's own session-N.scope — SIGTERM, then SIGKILL to whatever is still there after 2 s — declared in the log.
    • sessione_sgombera_gestore() (clear the manager) gives the user's systemd manager back as it was — after a session ends, and also at the next birth for what a crash left: it removes our drop-ins (the KWin and xfconfd.service ones, and the shell instance ones found in the directory), reloads, restores with UnsetAndSetEnvironment the values that sessione_fotografa_gestore() (photograph the manager) recorded at birth for the variables REMOTIX sets (VARIABILI_NOSTRE, “our variables”), and restarts xfconfd.service if it had our directory. Without a photograph only values carrying the remotix mark are removed, declared. If the child never comes back, the next child does it: the root server does not talk to a user manager.
    • Everything else REMOTIX wrote for the session lives under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/remotix and is rewritten at every birth; the exceptions in the user's home are the GNOME and XFCE power and lock keys and LXQt's power and lock files, all of them in the categories the user allowed on 25 Sep 2026.

    12.11 · Where the desktops branch

    Every place where the four desktops differ, in one table: the list to walk when a fifth desktop is added (the procedure is in ch. 19 “Extending REMOTIX”).

    i
    Status of the desktops. SPECIFICHE.md §11.2 still lists XFCE and LXQt as “studied, not yet served”; the code serves both since phases 13 and 14 (September 2026). Cinnamon was studied on 9 Aug 2026 and is not served: upstream it has neither RecordVirtual, nor libei, nor a clipboard path.
    Chapter 13

    Logging and diagnostics

    13.1 · The log module

    Every line the server writes goes through one module, src/registro.c (≈300 lines). There is no scattered printf: the four writing functions are macros over four _in functions that add __FILE__ and __LINE__, and all of them end in a single static function, riga() (line).

    The reason is written at the top of registro.h: a log spread over twenty fprintf(stderr, …) has neither a timestamp nor an area, and those two are what make a line readable to whoever hunts a defect six hours later. The second reason is a security check: the review item B13.2 asks that the password appear in no log, and only a single funnel makes «it is not there» verifiable instead of a hope (13.7 “What never enters the log”).

    The log is the main diagnostic instrument of the project (LEZIONI.md §2.7): most defects of REMOTIX were found by reading it, and several design rules below exist because the log once lied under load — which is exactly when it is needed.

    i
    Outside the funnel. a few places do not use the module and write straight to stderr: autenticazione.c (PAM authentication; it is also compiled into a test host, banchi/01-b3-rcp-innesta.py, which has no registro), the child between fork and exec (diventa_ed_esegui(), «become and execute», lines prefixed figlio:), the usage text of aiuto() (help), and the refusals of the command line in main() (a removed option, a missing --nome, a wrong --codifica). These lines have no timestamp and never reach the journal through --journal.

    13.2 · Anatomy of a log line

    A line is HH:MM:SS.mmm area [identity] body: local wall-clock time with milliseconds, the area left-aligned in seven columns, the identity in brackets only when there is one, then the body.

    Three log lines as the server writes them (bodies are in Italian, as the code writes them: «ready», «PAM answered (request 3): admitted, and the loop never stopped», «FIRST CONNECTION: anna is not in the card groups»)
    08:41:07.312 avvio   ⭐ pronto: https://server.lan:7447  —  la sessione WebTransport vive su /rcp/1 (RCP.md §2.2)
08:41:19.884 rcp     [anna] PAM ha risposto (pratica 3): ammesso  ⭐ e il filo non si e' mai fermato (DECISIONI.md §1.10)
08:41:21.040 figlio  [anna] ⭐ PRIMA CONNESSIONE: «anna» non e' nei gruppi della scheda (render,video) …

    The body follows a convention used across the whole code: a body that starts with ⛔ is a fault, with ⚠ a declared fallback or a warning, ⭐ marks a notable fact (a decision in force, a cure that fired). Only the mark at the head of the body counts: many normal lines quote a ⛔ in the middle, and the journal output reads only the head (13.6 “The systemd journal output”).

    The time is CLOCK_REALTIME in local time for the human reader; every interval the code measures uses registro_ora_ms(), which is CLOCK_MONOTONIC. The two are never mixed: the ban file, which must survive a restart, converts monotonic deadlines to epoch seconds when it is written (salva_ban() in rcp.c).

    13.3 · Log areas

    The area is the second column of every line and the REMOTIX_AREA field in the journal. It exists to read the log by column when transport, protocol and session speak at the same time.

    i
    Note. the area is padded to seven characters (%-7s); sessione and tastiera are longer and simply push the body one or two columns to the right. Tools that parse the log split on whitespace, not on column positions.

    13.4 · Whose line it is

    With ten tenants on one machine a line that does not say whose it is sends the reader to look at somebody else's desktop. The identity in brackets is the user name, and it reaches the line by two roads because the processes are of two kinds.

    The measurement that led here (review item R10-A4, 25 Aug 2026, fasi/10-multi-tenant-e-il-budget.md §6.7): with four real GNOME sessions (57,121 lines in 90 s of steady state) only 4.2 % of the diagnostic lines said who was speaking, and the three largest families (fotogramma-spedito, ciclo-cattura, audio-blocchi: frame sent, capture cycle, audio blocks) 0.0 %. With one scene in four switched off, the log showed that a series had stopped but named the session 0 times in 4, and a reader guessing the name was wrong 96 times in 100.

    The identity is composed in one place only, riga(): callers pass the bare name, never a ready-made [name], because two places writing the bracket would write it differently. It is a copy in a static buffer, not a pointer, since callers often pass an argv element; and it does not cross exec, which is why the child sets it again from its own command line.

    !
    A claimed name is not an authenticated name. lines of rcp in the parent carry the user name the client claimed in CREDENZIALI (credentials; rcp_utente()), also before PAM has answered. A line of a refused attempt therefore names a user who may not exist; read the outcome line, not the bracket, to know who got in.

    13.5 · Where the log lines go

    The log has no file of its own: the server writes to its standard error, and whoever starts it decides where that goes. The child inherits descriptors 0, 1 and 2 across exec on purpose, so parent and child lines land in the same stream and can be read in order.

    The session log used to be /tmp/remotix-sessione-<uid>.log: a predictable name in a shared directory. Another user could create it first, and with fs.protected_regular (on by default on Debian, Fedora and Arch) the shell's exec >> on a foreign file failed and the desktop did not start; if the name was a symlink, REMOTIX wrote where it pointed. Since phase 17, registro_sessione_percorso() (the session log path, in sessione.c) creates the directory with mode 0700 and checks that it is a real directory owned by the user and not writable by group or others, and opens the file with O_NOFOLLOW at 0600, verifying it is a regular file owned by the user.

    13.6 · The systemd journal output

    With --journal every event line also goes to the systemd journal, with fields that can be filtered (DECISIONI.md §9.1, phase 16 §12, commit 62753e7). The line on stderr does not change and is not switched off: the journal is added, never substituted.

    The child, after pam_open_session, lives in the scope of the user's logind session, not in the server unit. Its lines are therefore not found by journalctl -u remotix: the right query is by identifier.

    Reading the journal
    journalctl -t remotix -f                         # everything, parent and children
journalctl -t remotix -p warning --since today   # faults and fallbacks only
journalctl -t remotix REMOTIX_INQUILINO=anna     # one tenant
journalctl -t remotix REMOTIX_AREA=budget        # why somebody was refused
journalctl -t remotix -o verbose -n 1            # see every field of the last line

    At startup the parent declares the outcome: either registro anche nel journal di systemd (--journal) … (log also in the systemd journal), or ⚠ --journal chiesto ma il socket non si apre (<errno>): il registro resta SOLO qui (--journal requested but the socket does not open: the log stays ONLY here). The journal is switched on before the first line, so the first line goes there too.

    !
    Every line twice. all three packaged units start the server under systemd, whose default sends the unit's stderr to the journal as well. With --journal every event line of the parent is therefore in the journal twice: once from the output stream (no fields) and once native (with fields). Noted as open in fasi/17-l-installatore.md (§13.1, the items left undone by task T3, point 3): the program should stay quiet on stderr when JOURNAL_STREAM is its stderr. Not settled yet.
    i
    Priority 7. the help text of main.c and the box in registro.h still say «7 for the detail lines». The code never sends detail lines to the journal, so priority 7 never occurs.

    13.7 · What never enters the log

    Three things never enter any log at any level: passwords, what the user types, and the content of the screen. The first is a protocol rule (RCP.md §4.4), the second a decision of phase 16 (25–26 Sep 2026, DECISIONI.md §9.2), the third follows from the first two: the only images the server writes are those of --rilievo, a bench option.

    A sequence of evdev codes 30, 48, 46 is a word: a key code is a character up to the layout. That is why the list of speakable keys is the only question a caller must ask before writing a code, and why its answer lives in one place. rcp.c carries its own copy because it is also compiled without the server's log (banchi/rcp/).

    !
    An open question on the password. the zeroing of the local copy in rcp.c is a plain memset, which an optimising compiler may remove because the buffer is not read afterwards. The known cure is explicit_bzero(); the code asks to inspect the assembly of the running binary first (suspicion R9.20). Not settled yet.

    13.8 · The startup declarations

    At startup the parent writes the value in force of every mechanism that changes what users see or that can close a session — switched on and switched off. A threshold that is off and a threshold that never fired produce the same log; a thirty-minute clock is never verified by waiting thirty minutes. The line is the verification (failure form E1, «written is not in force»).

    While running, the parent adds one line per minute with the guardian's count (guardiano: chiamate=… peggiore_ms=… inquilini=… giri_fermi=… giro_peggiore_ms=…: logind calls, worst call, tenants served, times the parent's loop fell behind, worst gap; constant CONTO_GUARDIANO_MS = 60,000): a cumulative count, written once a minute instead of at every 2-second pass, which would be 43,200 nearly identical lines a day. Every rotation of the session certificate is declared in cert. At shutdown the parent writes how many QUIC connections were alive and whether the farewell 0x0C SERVER_IN_CHIUSURA (server shutting down) left on the wire within 4 s.

    13.9 · Command-line options of the server

    The server is configured only by its command line. Every option is parsed in the single loop of main(); an unknown option prints the usage text (aiuto()) and exits 2.

    The column «lives in» matters because the child is an execve with an environment built from scratch: a setting that the encoder or the audio encoder needs must be repeated on the child's command line, or it silently does not exist there. That cost a day on 16 Aug 2026: --parlantina was not passed, every detail line of the child vanished, and branches were believed «never taken» while they ran. The parent appends to the child's argv only what differs from the default: --parlantina, --journal, --qualita-risale, --tetto-banda-mbit N, --niente-audio-silenzio (negated, the same word the parent received) and --codifica X when it is not scheda.

    The child's command line (written by diventa_ed_esegui(), read by figlio_vive())
    remotix-figlio --figlio-interno <user> <uid> <gid> <width> <height> <serial> <rilievo-dir|-> [optional words]
    i
    Option names. the options are still in Italian. DECISIONI.md §10.35 records that renaming the product's own options is «a job of its own», not yet done.

    13.10 · Environment variables

    REMOTIX reads almost nothing from the environment, on purpose: a cure that can be switched by an option and by a variable has two numbers that can diverge, and the child would not see the variable anyway. The complete list of names that start with REMOTIX_ in src/, installatore/ and packaging/, leaving out the include guards of the headers (REMOTIX_*_H):

    !
    It does not reach the sessions. REMOTIX_VULKAN_CONVERSIONE is read with getenv inside the encoder, but sessions encode in the per-user child, whose environment is composed from scratch by diventa_ed_esegui() (HOME, USER, LOGNAME, PATH, an empty SHELL, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, plus XDG_SESSION_ID from PAM). The variable therefore reaches only the startup probe (a fork of the parent) and remotix --prova-codifica; it never reaches a real session.

    Other variables the code reads are the standard ones of the session it lives in: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, WAYLAND_DISPLAY, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, XDG_CONFIG_DIRS, XDG_DATA_DIRS, XDG_STATE_HOME (through GLib, for the session log), DCONF_PROFILE, LANG, PATH and USER (sessione.c, kwin.c, wlroots.c, wlr_input.c, figlio.c). Variables used only by the test benches are documented with the benches.

    13.11 · Diagnostic instruments

    Besides the log, the product carries a few instruments for diagnosis. None of them is on in the packaged units except --journal: bench options are kept off the shipped command line (review rule R13), and the build refuses to package a binary with the bench function compiled in (BANCO_ACCESO must be 0 in rcp.c).

    1. Read the startup declarations (13.8 “The startup declarations”): most «it does not work» cases are already named there — no codec offered, no PAM service file, KWin permission missing, guardian not connected.
    2. Filter by tenant (REMOTIX_INQUILINO or the bracket) and by area; read budget for refusals, rcp for the handshake, figlio for the birth of the desktop.
    3. For a refused login, distinguish PAM ha RIFIUTATO (PAM REFUSED: a real no) from ⛔ PAM NON HA POTUTO GIUDICARE (PAM COULD NOT JUDGE: a missing /etc/pam.d/remotix or /etc/remotix/utenti-negati): the client receives 0x07 in both cases, the log does not.
    4. For a desktop that is born and shows nothing, look for the line of figlio about the card groups (the groups that own the nodes in /dev/dri) and for sessione.log in the user's home.
    5. Only then switch on --parlantina, for the shortest time that reproduces the defect.
    +
    No silent exits. a session that disappears always leaves a line with the numbers it was closed on: the dead line writes linea-morta (dead line) with its stall or silence values, the clocks write the clock that expired, and the farewell code reaches the page. A disappearance without such a line is a defect of REMOTIX, by definition of invariant I1.
    Chapter 14

    Security model

    14.1 · Two security levels

    REMOTIX has two security levels and deliberately no third (SPECIFICHE.md §4.1, set by the user on 9 Aug 2026): the transport, so that nobody reads or rewrites what passes, and the access, i.e. who may enter the machine. Transport is TLS, always and without alternatives; access is address, port, user name and password, checked by the machine's own PAM.

    Accepted risks, written down rather than hidden: the first connection from each device is open to a man-in-the-middle (there is no domain and no authority; with a web client the attacker does not intercept the page, they rewrite it), which is acceptable for the intended scenario — own server, own network or VPN. Multi-factor authentication is deferred by the user to after project completion (DECISIONI.md §1.7). The desktops' own screen lockers stay off (SPECIFICHE.md §5.4): the only road to a desktop is RCP, and RCP goes through PAM — a reasoning that holds only while the password is the only key.

    14.2 · Certificates and TLS settings of the server

    The server makes its own certificates — two of them, on purpose (RCP.md §4.1-bis, certificati.h, the certificates module). Confusing them passes every bench and makes the browser warning reappear every two weeks, «and nobody would connect the two things».

    A page left open for two weeks holds the fingerprint of a certificate that has since rotated. The page fetches the current one from GET /impronta on the server that served it — a plain HTTPS request, since no RCP channel exists before the session opens.

    0-RTT is off because early data can be replayed, and the client's second RCP message is CREDENZIALI (credentials); the gain would be one round trip on a session that lasts hours. The symptom of 0-RTT left on does not exist — the session opens the same — and libraries offer it by default (ngtcp2's example even sets it to UINT32_MAX), so leaving it alone would be a distraction no functional bench sees. The page's responses carry Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin, Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin, Cache-Control: no-store and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

    !
    No Retry. QUIC address validation with Retry is not done (trasporto.c, the QUIC transport): «the product is used on its own network or VPN; it must be put back before exposing it». Exposing REMOTIX directly to the Internet is outside the declared scenario.

    14.3 · Authentication with PAM

    The server runs one poll loop for every connected user, and a PAM transaction blocks: measured on 11 Aug 2026 (bench B8) at 1.0–2.2 s per attempt, of which PAM itself added +1034 ms on refusals against +84 ms on admissions — the signature of pam_faildelay. With video, that would freeze every connected screen whenever somebody logs in. Since 12 Aug 2026 (DECISIONI.md §1.10) PAM is asked by a helper process.

    One process per transaction was chosen over a thread by the user: PAM is not reliably re-entrant, and its modules — foreign code loaded at runtime, with getpwnam, sockets to nscd, dlopen — share nothing with anybody this way. Ten users logging in together do not queue: they are ten grandchildren. SOCK_SEQPACKET keeps messages delimited by the kernel, so a request cannot arrive in half and two answers cannot merge into «somebody else's answer»; the socketpair has no name in the filesystem.

    Inside the grandchild, rcp_autentica_da() follows sshd: pam_start("remotix", user, …), PAM_RHOST = the client's bare address (no brackets, no port, ::ffff:1.2.3.4 reduced to 1.2.3.4, like sshd with UseDNS no), PAM_TTY = remotix, then pam_authenticate and pam_acct_mgmt: the first says the password is right, only the second says the account is usable (expired or locked accounts pass the first). The conversation answers only PAM_PROMPT_ECHO_OFF with the password and at most 16 prompts. With PAM_RHOST set, pam_faillock records the address, pam_unix logs rhost=…, pam_access has the host and logind marks the session RemoteHost.

    i
    The service file is checked. the server checks at startup that /etc/pam.d/remotix or /usr/lib/pam.d/remotix exists (guarda_il_servizio_pam(), check the PAM service). Without it Linux-PAM falls back to the other service: pam_deny on Fedora and Arch (every right password refused), the common stacks without the root exclusion on Debian. The server does not refuse to start — the page, the ban and the certificates still work — but it writes the fault with the remedy.

    14.4 · The PAM service files

    One file per distribution family, like Cockpit: @include is a Debian modification of Linux-PAM and is an «illegal module type» elsewhere. Since DECISIONI.md §10.18 (D3, 30 Sep 2026) each file is the distribution's own sshd PAM file, line for line, plus one line at the top.

    The one line that is not sshd's: root excluded, as ssh does by default
    auth  requisite  pam_listfile.so item=user sense=deny file=/etc/remotix/utenti-negati onerr=fail

    14.5 · The address ban

    Three failed authentications from the same address within five minutes, and that address is out for twelve hours (DECISIONI.md §1.9, SPECIFICHE.md §4.2, decided 10 Aug 2026). The user name does not count: three different names count three. A successful login resets the count. The ban survives restarts.

    The key is the address without the port, in brackets even for IPv4: [192.168.0.2], [fe80::1]. The first version keyed on 192.168.0.2:44661; with one attempt per connection the port changes every time and the counter was always 1 — code that looked right and did nothing, found only by a bench case that tries seven different names from one address. The key is built in exactly one place, rcp_chiave_indirizzo() (the address key), used by the session, the page server and the unlock command alike: before 10 Aug 2026 a second function made keys without brackets and rcp_bannato("192.168.0.2") (is it banned?) answered «not banned» (B-8).

    !
    The declared price. behind a NAT addresses are shared, so three mistakes by one person close the door to everybody for twelve hours, and the first to trip is whoever types a long password on a phone keyboard. A per-name counter that softened this was removed knowingly. Whether 256 entries are enough against an attacker with more addresses is not measured: the eviction line in the log is where it would show.

    14.6 · The unlock command socket

    The way out for whoever bans themselves from their own phone must ask «the only key that case admits — access to the machine». comando.c (the command module) implements it as a Unix socket, opened with --comando-socket PATH.

    Unlocking an address (the socket path is whatever <code>--comando-socket</code> was given)
    printf 'SBLOCCA 192.168.0.2\n' | nc -U /run/remotix/comando
python3 banchi/01-b8-sblocca.py --socket /run/remotix/comando 192.168.0.2

    The socket is created with umask(0177) around bind so that it is born 0600, then chmod 0600 again: a later chmod alone left a window with whatever the inherited umask allowed. It has no IP address, so it adds no surface reachable from the network. PING answers «somebody answers», not «the right server answers»: with two servers on a machine, the wrong socket replies PONG and NON-BANNATO. No identity verb was added to the protocol; the client asks the kernel instead (SO_PEERCRED).

    !
    Not in the packaged units. the packaged units do not pass --comando-socket (it is listed among the bench options kept off the shipped command line), although the deb and rpm tmpfiles entries create /run/remotix «for the command socket». On an installed system a ban therefore ends only after twelve hours, unless the administrator adds the option through REMOTIX_OPZIONI (deb, rpm). SPECIFICHE.md §4.2 promises the command as a way out. Not settled yet.
    i
    Requested, not confirmed. rcp_sblocca() (unlock) writes the file through salva_ban() (save the bans) without a session, which stays silent on a write failure: the line ⛔ SBLOCCATO (unlocked) therefore says the rewrite was requested, not done.

    14.7 · Isolation between users

    The parent stays root because only root can verify another user's password with PAM and descend to any uid; for every admitted user it creates a child that runs as that user and holds the session bus, the capture and the devices (DECISIONI.md §1.10-bis, 12 Aug 2026). Root does not connect to a user's session bus, which was measured.

    The child is a fork and an exec of the same binary. A fork alone would run as the user while holding the parent's memory: the TLS private key, the ban table and the state of every other session — and /proc/self/mem is readable by the process owner, who would be the user. That would be the worst defect this work could produce. The descent happens before exec, so there is no instant in which the new image runs as root.

    1. The socketpair end goes to descriptor 3, without CLOEXEC: the only thing that must cross exec.
    2. Every other descriptor from 4 up is closed (close_range, or a loop up to 4096 as declared fallback). A child that kept the UDP socket and the TCP listener would hold the port after the server died. 0, 1 and 2 stay: the child logs to the parent's stream.
    3. A PAM session is opened for the user (service remotix, silent conversation) with XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland, XDG_SESSION_CLASS=user, no XDG_SEAT (a session without a seat is headless by construction), PAM_RHOST = the client address (remotix if unknown) and PAM_TTY = remotix; then pam_end without pam_close_session: the logind session belongs to this process and logind reclaims it when it dies. A failure is logged and the child goes on.
    4. On SELinux systems the exec context gets the level of the user's login mapping, as sshd does (livello_selinux_come_sshd(), libselinux opened with dlopen).
    5. setgroups, then setgid, then setuid — never in another order: groups first or the right to change them is lost, gid before uid or the privilege to set it is lost. Exits 31, 32, 33.
    6. getresuid and getresgid are read back: all three uids and all three gids must be the user's, or the child does not start (exits 34–36). A setuid that returns 0 does not prove that the saved uid changed; one left at 0 would be one line away from root.
    7. The environment is composed from scratch, one variable at a time, and only XDG_SESSION_ID is taken from PAM's list. Then execve (exit 37 if it fails). No secret is on the command line: the password died with the PAM grandchild.

    Before any of this, figli_assicura_da() (ensure the user has a child) refuses to create a child for a user whose uid is 0: the child exists in order not to be root, and a root child would have nobody's session bus anyway. (Root is also excluded earlier, by PAM.)

    One child per user, one graphical session per user (SPECIFICHE.md §5.1): a second device of the same user is refused with 0x0F GIA_ATTIVA_REMOTA (or takes the seat by ghost eviction, never across users), and a user who sits at the machine and opens a local session wins over the remote one (0x05 GIA_ATTIVA_LOCALE (already active locally) at attach, 0x04 SESSIONE_LOCALE_PREVALSA (the local session prevailed) for a session already running; logind is polled once every 2 s for all tenants). The session cap and the composition budget keep one user from starving the others (0x0E, 0x06).

    Per-session files live with the user: runtime configuration (systemd user drop-ins, labwc and Qt settings, menu rules) under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, which disappears at reboot, and the session log under ~/.local/state/remotix, created 0700/0600 with O_NOFOLLOW checks. Nothing is written in shared /tmp.

    14.8 · The graphics card groups

    On a normal desktop logind grants access to /dev/dri with an ACL (uaccess) to whoever owns a seat. A remote session has no seat on purpose, so the ACL never comes and only the groups of the card nodes remain. Without them the session is born blind: measured 27 Aug 2026, 0 sessions of 4 without the groups, 17 of 17 with them — and no error says so.

    This is the one wanted exception to «REMOTIX does not modify the system» (DECISIONI.md §7.21 and §10.36: «no packages without authorisation, but users must be able to access»). The annotation file is opened before usermod with O_NOFOLLOW in a root-owned directory that others cannot write, born 0600, one write plus fsync per line, and written only after usermod succeeded: annotating an enrolment that never happened would make the uninstaller remove a group someone else gave.

    i
    Only render? DECISIONI.md §10.36 asks to restrict the groups to render if that does not hurt the four desktops, because video also grants /dev/fb* and webcams; and later a dedicated remotix group. The code still enrols in every group that owns a card node (typically both). Not settled yet.

    14.9 · What REMOTIX does not change

    «The key of everything is that REMOTIX does not modify the systems it is installed on: it says what it needs, and then it is up to the administrator» (the user, 10 Oct 2026, DECISIONI.md §10.36). The installer's check says what is missing without suggesting packages or commands; the plan stops before touching anything if something blocking is missing.

    14.10 · The power belts, shipped inert

    On 15 Aug 2026 the user decided that nobody powers off, reboots, suspends or hibernates the server — not even who sits in front of it — because powering off takes away every session at once and whoever does it does not see who is connected (DECISIONI.md §4.7). Three «belts» implement it. Since §10.12 and §10.36 they are shipped inert in /usr/share/remotix/cinture/ (cinture = belts), where nothing reads them, and the installer no longer applies them.

    What remains in force regardless is session behaviour, not system configuration: inside a REMOTIX session the desktops' menus lose suspend, lock, restart, power-off and switch user, so that the only gesture that ends something is the logout (DECISIONI.md §4.7, §8.2; described with the four desktops). When root does stop the machine, attached clients receive 0x0C SERVER_IN_CHIUSURA (server shutting down).

    !
    The specification is older than the decision. SPECIFICHE.md §11.3 still says power-off and suspend are «taken away from everyone». Since DECISIONI.md §10.36 that holds only inside REMOTIX sessions; the machine itself suspends and powers off as its administrator configured it.

    14.11 · The service unit and SELinux

    The server runs as a systemd system service, as root and outside any user session: PAM must verify anyone's password, and the parent descends to each user's uid for the child. No User= and no ProtectSystem: it opens logind sessions, writes in users' homes and touches /dev/dri.

    !
    The Arch unit differs. the Arch unit reads no EnvironmentFile: the REMOTIX_PORTA that the installer writes to /etc/remotix/remotix.conf.d/porta.conf for a non-default port is not seen there, and the unit lacks --journal. The deb and rpm units are the reference. Not settled yet.

    On SELinux distributions the remotix-selinux sub-package (packaging/rpm/selinux/) confines the server in remotix_t with its own types for the executable, the port (7447 TCP and UDP, declared in CIL because portcon cannot be written in a .te module), /var/lib/remotix and /run/remotix. The domain may authenticate like a login program (auth_login_pgm_domain, the rule of sshd and Cockpit's session), talk to logind, and transition to the users' domains, so desktops are born unconfined_t like an ssh login. Without the module, measured 29 Sep 2026, the child exited with 37 ({ transition } unconfined_service_t → unconfined_t); with it, enforcing, 0 denials on Fedora 44, Alma 10, Tumbleweed and Leap 16. A different port needs semanage port -a -t remotix_port_t -p tcp N (and udp) by the administrator.

    14.12 · Known limits of the security model

    The weaknesses that are known and written in the code, collected in one place for whoever evaluates exposing a REMOTIX server.

    Chapter 15

    The installer

    15.1 · The installer at a glance

    REMOTIX is installed by one program, remotix-install, delivered inside one file, remotix-X.Y.Z-R.run. It examines the machine, says what is missing, shows the exact packages the distribution's package manager would install, asks once, installs, verifies and starts the service. It also uninstalls, and re-checks an installation later. It is a statically linked Go binary (no cgo), with the catalogue of supported platforms compiled in.

    i
    History. the design went through several shapes between 29 Sep and 10 Oct 2026 (signed archive, an install.sh script, answer files, offline bundles, plan/approve/apply, a Gio GUI, an Italian/English interface). Only the current shape is described here; the retired codes in 15.23 “The RX- code catalogue” are the visible trace of the old ones and must never be reused.

    15.2 · Installer source layout

    The installer is one Go module, remotix/installatore (go.mod: Go 1.25, Bubble Tea 1.3.10, lipgloss 1.1.0, godbus 5.2.2). Every dependency is vendored, and the build runs with GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor GOPROXY=off CGO_ENABLED=0: it never touches the network and the result runs on every distribution before any package is installed.

    The engine is the only package with installation logic. The interfaces read the engine's objects and events and collect a single consent; they never choose packages, repositories or rollbacks. In tests the Ambiente (the environment: files, D-Bus, programs) is a fake rooted in a temporary folder (Radice, the root), so the same engine code runs against a fake machine (finti_test.go, finti2_test.go: the fakes).

    15.3 · The installer commands

    Since 10 Oct 2026 the command line has four public commands plus tui (§10.36: from fourteen down to five). Options can come before or after positional arguments (argomenti(), “arguments”, re-parses after each one).

    !
    Doc vs code. §10.36 lists prepare-offline among the five commands; the code has no such command (RX-FUORI-001…005 are retired: “the .run file is already offline”). The .run carries only REMOTIX's own packages: dependencies still come from the machine's repositories.

    The .run wraps these: sudo sh remotix-X.Y.Z-R.run runs install; check and tui are passed through, and version prints the release (17.14 “The .run file format”).

    15.4 · An installation from the .run file

    What happens when the administrator runs the .run. The engine stays on the machine afterwards as the remotix-install package, so status and uninstall work without the .run.

    1. run.sh checks it is root (for install and tui), extracts the payload into /var/tmp/remotix-run.XXXXXX, verifies the payload sha256 written in the header by the release, and runs remotix-install install --bundle <dir>/packages. The folder is removed on exit.
    2. sistemaAperta() (settle the open one): an unfinished operation is rolled back (installation, upgrade) or completed (uninstallation) first; then the command starts again from scratch, with no automatic retry.
    3. Phase 0 TRUST and phase 1 PREFLIGHT (15.10 “Phase 1: the machine profile”), phase 2 COMPATIBILITY (15.12 “Phase 2: compatibility and what is missing”).
    4. PianoInstallazione() (the installation plan, 15.14 “The installation plan”): the REMOTIX files for this distribution are picked from packages/<target>/ (PacchettiDelRun(), the packages of the .run; Bersaglio(), the target), and the package manager simulates the transaction with the desktop dependencies.
    5. The plan is printed: steps with their reversibility, then “What the package manager will do (its own simulation)”, the declared group enrolment, conditions, and what is not done. A BLOCKING item ends here: “REMOTIX is not installed: nothing was touched.”
    6. Proceed? [y/N] is read from stdin; only y or yes proceed. The plan is written to /var/lib/remotix/plans/<id>.json and applied with the consent recorded as “by hand, --approve”, by SUDO_USER (or USER, LOGNAME, the uid).
    7. Motore.Applica() (engine.apply) walks the states (15.5 “Operation states”); at the end the CLI prints the operation and its folder and, for an installation, the router reminder: forward the port TCP and UDP (no UPnP).
    i
    Upgrade. on a machine where a CONFIRMED installation exists the same command is an upgrade: the plan holds only the package step (groups, port and service are already there). If the simulation says every file of the .run is already installed at that version, it prints “REMOTIX X is already installed: nothing to do.” and exits 0.

    15.5 · Operation states

    An operation (installation, upgrade, uninstallation) has an identifier — the UTC time plus 4 random bytes, e.g. 20261010T081500Z-1a2b3c4d (nuovoID(), new ID) — and one state, kept in <state-dir>/<id>/state. Valida() (valid) allows only the transitions of the design; any other is RX-STATO-002, an engine defect. No state is skipped.

    Only one engine runs at a time: Blocca() (lock) takes an exclusive flock on <state-dir>/.serratura (the lock file; RX-STATO-003 if busy); the kernel releases it if the process dies, so a resume never finds an orphan lock. At most one operation is ever open, and Applica() refuses to start next to one (RX-STATO-001).

    i
    Rule. installed is not certified. CONFIRMED_WITH_CONDITIONS on a COMPATIBLE platform is a successful installation, but not a certified combination; and an UNKNOWN check never counts as PASS (15.16 “Verification and the certificate”).

    15.6 · Engine objects and files on disk

    The engine produces and consumes seven JSON objects; all but the execution log (one event per line) carry "format": "remotix-install/3" (Formato in formato.go) and an object field. LeggiJSON() (read JSON) refuses an object of another format; every write goes through ScriviAtomico() (atomic write): temporary name in the same folder, fsync, rename, fsync of the folder — a reader sees the old file or the new one, never half.

    The plan digest (Piano.Digest(), plan digest) is the sha256 of the canonical JSON of the plan without the approval; the approval carries that digest, so a plan changed after it was shown is refused (RX-PIANO-005).

    !
    Known gap. the certificate's product field is always the text “none: engine test plan (T4)” (cert.prodotto_prova), a leftover of the T4 test plan; the installed product version is not written in it.

    15.7 · The write-ahead log and resume

    Every step runs in four beats, and the log records them before the engine moves on: Registro.Scrivi() (log.write) appends one JSON line and calls fsync before returning; a new log also syncs its folder.

    A line cut in half by a crash is removed when the log is reopened and reported as RX-RIPRESA-003: lines are whole or absent, and without its line a thing did not happen. The first INTENT of a step is the one that counts (Registro.Intenzione(), log.intent): re-photographing the machine after an effect would mistake our own change for a PREEXISTING one and never undo it.

    Rolling back (annullaTutte(), undo them all) walks the steps in reverse: a step never started is skipped, a PREEXISTING one is left untouched, one that is already undone is recorded as such, one changed by someone else is left and listed; otherwise ROLLBACK_INTENT, Annulla(), Annullata(). Whatever could not be undone makes the final state PARTIALLY_ROLLED_BACK.

    The engine tests kill the process at named points (PuntoDiProva, the test hook: before/after intent, after effect, after done, during rollback) and resume (ripresa_test.go). In the shipped binary the hook is always nil: no variable or option can turn it on (R13).

    15.8 · Plan steps, reversibility and origin

    A plan step (AzionePiano, plan step) carries its id, type, parameters, a description, and three texts written when the plan is made: how it is done, how it is verified, how it is rolled back. Undo is born with the step. Each type implements Azione (step): Fotografa (snapshot), Fai (do), Controlla (check: COMPLETE, ABSENT, HALF_DONE or FOREIGN), Annulla (undo), Annullata (is it undone?), Vincoli (constraints: its fingerprint elements). Every method is idempotent.

    The promise, as the code implements it: everything REMOTIX did directly is undone; what happened indirectly is declared; what was there before is not touched. azioni_dichiarate.go (declared steps) keeps a mechanism for step types the engine knows but cannot run yet (RX-AZIONE-004, stopping before touching anything); its list is empty today.

    15.9 · The machine fingerprint

    A plan is valid only on the machine it was made on. Before applying, CalcolaImpronta() (compute the fingerprint) recomputes the binding fingerprint and compares its digest with the plan's; a difference blocks with RX-PIANO-001 and writes fingerprint-now.json, and the detail lists what was in the plan and what is there now.

    The digest is the sha256 of the sorted elements, one per line. With the install flow the plan is made and applied seconds apart, so the check catches a machine changed between the question and the answer; it is also why the plan stays in the operation folder as a document of what was done.

    15.10 · Phase 1: the machine profile

    Phase 1 builds the machine profile in read-only mode (R1): no function in preflight.go writes, creates, renames or changes permissions. It reads files, asks systemd, logind and firewalld over D-Bus (properties and queries only), and runs one program, rpm -q on RPM families, recorded in the profile. The proof is installatore/prove/r1-contenitori.sh: a fingerprint of /etc before and after check, in one container per family, must be identical.

    Each fact has a state: DETECTED (seen: “PipeWire is installed”), VERIFIED (actually tested: “the card encoded a frame”) or UNKNOWN (the tool is missing, permission denied, time out). The rule the whole engine follows: a DETECTED fact never makes a PASS, and UNKNOWN is never “fine” — it is the lesson of GNOME 50's false green (fasi/17 §5.1).

    Every call goes through eseguiDavvero() (really run): absolute path, fixed arguments, an environment of three variables (LC_ALL=C, a fixed PATH, DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive), no stdin, a timeout (45 minutes for the package managers), and an annotation path args ⇒ exit in the profile or in the log. A name outside the list returns ErrNonAmmesso (not allowed) without running anything.

    15.11 · Encoding routes and the card verdict

    REMOTIX encodes only on the graphics card (§10.27: “no CPU without a card”), so a machine without a card that can encode is refused before anything is touched. The route is chosen by capability, not by brand: StradeCodifica (encoding routes) lists them in order of preference, and the verdict is “at least one active route has a capable card”.

    Intel is never counted on the Vulkan route: ANV encodes only behind ANV_DEBUG=video-encode, experimental (§10.27). Which route really encoded is known only after installation, from the strada field of remotix --prova-codifica (15.16 “Verification and the certificate”). The minimum Mesa with RADV encoding by default is not measured (Mesa 25.0.7 works, measured 1 Oct 2026 on the test server's Radeon RX 6800).

    !
    Code defect. codiceH264() in preflight.go still raises RX-H264-003 (Fedora) and RX-H264-004 (openSUSE), which codici.go marks as retired by §10.36: where a driver warning was meant, the administrator reads an INFO line with a “(retired…)” text. The verdict above is what blocks; these lines are cosmetic.

    15.12 · Phase 2: compatibility and what is missing

    Phase 2 (Valuta(), assess) judges the machine against the catalogue, desktop by desktop, and collects in one list everything that is missing. An empty list means REMOTIX can be installed.

    1. Reasons that hold for every desktop: an excluded version (RX-COMPAT-001, with the first supported version of that distribution), an immutable system (RX-COMPAT-003), no systemd or OpenSSL below 3.5.0 (RX-COMPAT-007), a platform not in the catalogue (RX-COMPAT-002), a derivative below its minimum, and the card verdict.
    2. Platform repositories REMOTIX itself needs (on Alma: EPEL): each missing one is RX-MANCA-002.
    3. For each supported desktop: the conditions of H.264, the desktop's components that are absent become dependencies (labwc, wlr-randr, breeze6-wallpapers), a scalable font is added when the catalogue marks the desktop serve_carattere (needs a font: XFCE and LXQt, which run under labwc) and fonts.scalable is 0 (the catalogue's carattere_scalabile for the family, e.g. fonts-dejavu-core), limits become C-LIMITE, a 3D need becomes C-HARDWARE (or a refusal with no node), and a version below the minimum is RX-COMPAT-006.
    4. The level: UNSUPPORTED if there is any reason; CERTIFIED only on a matrix platform (not a derivative) whose catalogue entry records a full green run (giro_intero); COMPATIBLE otherwise.
    5. Missing pieces of an installed supported desktop become RX-MANCA-003; no installed supported desktop at all, when one is possible, is RX-MANCA-001 with the minimum versions.
    i
    Current state. every desktop of every platform is COMPATIBLE today, none CERTIFIED: the catalogue's giro_intero is empty everywhere because the full run (T10) on the 26 combinations has not been done with this engine. The matrix platforms are “in the matrix, not yet certified”.

    Desktop dependencies are ordinary dependencies of REMOTIX (user's decision of 10 Oct 2026): they are passed to the same package-manager transaction, shown under “Dependencies of REMOTIX” with “needed by REMOTIX for XFCE”, and if the distribution does not have them the simulation fails and the plan stops with RX-PACCHETTI-005.

    15.13 · The catalogue of platforms

    The catalogue is installatore/catalogo/catalogo.json, embedded in the binary with go:embed (catalogo.go). It is data, so its keys stay Italian and its format is remotix-catalogo/1; its texts (reasons, notes, limits) are English. A new catalogue is a new release with a higher sequenza.

    !
    Code finding. Linux Mint 23 is a compatible derivative in the catalogue, but Bersaglio() maps its os-release to linuxmint23, a folder the .run does not have: the plan stops with RX-MANCA-004. Fedora 43 (outside the matrix) has the same fate. Rocky and RHEL map to alma10, Manjaro and EndeavourOS to arch through ID_LIKE.

    The catalogue's component minimums and the build's disagree on two libraries: libei 1.3 here, 1.1 in src/Makefile, packaging/debian/control and packaging/rpm/remotix.spec; libopus 1.4 here, 1.3 in the Makefile. Not settled yet: which one is the real floor.

    15.14 · The installation plan

    PianoInstallazione() is the whole installation policy in one function. REMOTIX does not modify the system, so the plan has few steps; everything else is said, not done.

    With the steps built, the package manager simulates the transaction (Gestore.Simula(), manager.simulate); its exact list (name, version, architecture, origin, new / upgraded / present) goes into the plan and is printed before the question. If the manager cannot resolve it, the plan carries RX-PACCHETTI-005 with the manager's own words. At execution the package step simulates again in Fotografa and records that result as the resolved set.

    i
    One question. the TUI asks only for the port and the “yes”. Repositories, the firewall, the desktop, guards and drivers are not questions any more: what is missing is said and the installation stops (§10.36).

    Not settled yet: whether the card groups shrink to render only — video also grants /dev/fb* and webcams (§10.36); until it is measured on the four desktops the engine enrols every non-root group it finds on /dev/dri/card* and renderD*.

    15.15 · Package manager adapters

    Each family has an adapter (Gestore, the manager, in gestore.go, chosen by ScegliGestore()): versions, simulate, install, simulate-remove, remove only the named packages, integrity, and the manager's own repair. Files from the .run carry no rpm signature (the .run sha256 vouches for them); packages from the machine's repositories are verified by the manager as usual.

    Removal never uses the managers' autoremove: it would also take orphans that were there before and are not ours. Instead trattenuti() (kept back) simulates removing the NEW packages; those whose removal would drag along something outside our set (an upgraded package, a program installed later) are kept and declared (RX-PACCHETTI-006). The reason is measured: on leap16-kde (30 Sep) zypper rm of a codec library would have removed 53 packages, Plasma included. A Togli() (remove) that would remove anything else stops with RX-PACCHETTI-002.

    !
    Doc vs code. the text az.pacchetti.fa printed as “how it is done” still describes the retired design (“resolved, everything downloaded and verified … installs from the cache, offline”). The code installs through the manager, which downloads dependencies from the machine's repositories.

    15.16 · Verification and the certificate

    Phase 7 re-runs every step's Controlla() and, for an installation, the platform checks of ControlliPiattaforma() (platform checks). It runs after every step, the service start included.

    !
    Doc vs code. §6.0 of fasi/17 designs the checks that do not need the service (7a: the encoding test, PAM) to run before switching it on, and the live ones (7b) after, so that most errors appear while undoing is cheap and nobody is connected; the step texts still say “after the checks with the service stopped (7a)”, and the TUI's plan screen “started after the final check”. In the code start-service is an ordinary step of phase 6, and verifica() (verify) runs all checks afterwards: the encoding test runs with the service already on.

    A required FAIL sends the operation to ROLLING_BACK (RX-AZIONE-003). Conditions from verification and from the compatibility report make the final state CONFIRMED_WITH_CONDITIONS. The certificate, and for an installation installation.json pointing to the operation, are written before the final state: if the process dies in between, the resume finds VERIFIED and writes them again.

    Who can log in is shown at the end (TUI “WHO CAN LOG IN”): any account that can log in by ssh, with its password; root is excluded by /etc/remotix/utenti-negati. The page certificate fingerprint shown is the SHA-256 of /var/lib/remotix/certificati/pagina.pem.

    15.17 · Uninstallation

    Uninstalling is an operation like the others, with its plan, consent, log and resume. PianoDisinstallazione() (the uninstallation plan) reads the plan and log of the operation named by installation.json and walks it backwards.

    1. For each step of the installation that was started and is not PREEXISTING, an undo step: doing it is the original's undo, undoing it is the original's do — a failed uninstallation reinstalls.
    2. Right after the undo of the service, close-sessions: the sessions logind lists with PAM service remotix are terminated; a local or ssh session of the same person stays (§10.16). The administrator warns people beforehand with their own means; there is no extra question. It is IRREVERSIBLE.
    3. For each group enrolment the product recorded at first connection in /var/lib/remotix/gruppi-iscritti.jsonl (format remotix-gruppi/1, written by figlio.c) that the engine did not do itself, a remove-membership step.
    4. Last, remove-user-logs: ~/.local/state/remotix/sessione.log in every home, declared in the plan with the current list.
    5. On CONFIRMED: installation.json is removed; without --purge the operations history stays (for support); with --purge the operations folder, the enrolment file, recorded-versions.json and /var/lib/remotix if empty go too.

    Removing the packages removes the NEW packages of the installation's resolved set, remotix-install included (the running engine keeps its open file). The rollback of a failed installation always purges; an uninstallation purges the configuration only with --purge (like apt purge).

    !
    Code finding. the uninstallation plan is built only from the original installation operation. Packages that an upgrade operation added as NEW (a dependency a later release needs) are in the upgrade's resolved set, not in the installation's, and are not removed by uninstall.

    15.18 · Unfinished operations

    An operation that did not reach a final state is never left as it is and never resumed half way (§10.36: “I don't like the idea of leaving a system half way”). sistemaAperta() runs at the start of install, tui and uninstall.

    If the rollback itself cannot finish, the command stops with RX-STATO-001 and the operation's state. status marks an open operation with “← open: remotix-install install rolls it back”.

    15.19 · Upgrades and post-upgrade

    REMOTIX is upgraded by running the newer .run: install sees the CONFIRMED installation and makes an upgrade plan with the package step only. There is no timer and no update command of ours (D14, §10.23).

    Packages can also change under the engine (an administrator's apt upgrade pulling a dependency, a downgrade with the manager's commands). The package scripts call remotix-install post-upgrade, which records the installed versions of remotix, remotix-install, remotix-selinux in recorded-versions.json. The package step's Controlla() accepts a package at the resolved version, at a newer one (compared with the dpkg or rpmvercmp algorithm of versioni.go), or at the recorded one — so status stays GREEN after a legitimate system update or a rollback with the manager.

    The service restart does not close the desktops: they live outside the unit (KillMode=mixed, desktops started with setsid --fork), and the new server finds them again (T2, measured 10 runs out of 10 on 29 Sep 2026, fasi/17 §5.2).

    15.20 · Phase 0: trust

    Phase 0 answers one question: is the catalogue the right one, and does this engine understand it? After D11 was simplified (§10.21) and the signed archive was dropped (§10.36), there are no keys of our own.

    What remains for the engine: the catalogue must parse and have format remotix-catalogo/1 (RX-TRUST-004), and VersioneMotore (the engine version) must be at least motore_minimo (the minimum engine, RX-TRUST-003). No expiry, no catalogue stored on the machine. RX-TRUST-001, 002 and 005…017 are retired. Honestly: the sha256 is worth what the site that publishes it is worth.

    15.21 · The installer TUI

    The TUI (remotix-install tui, or sudo sh remotix-X.Y.Z-R.run tui) is the “professional” interface of §10.31, for administrators on ssh or the console. It is Bubble Tea and lipgloss, drawn on the mockup the user approved on 10 Oct 2026 (grafica/tui-mockup/index.html): a fixed frame as wide as the terminal (at least 80 columns and 12 lines, else a line says so), four steps Check › Plan › Install › Ready, a body that scrolls inside the frame, the keys at the bottom.

    remotix-install tui --preview 80 — the check screen (sample data, shortened)
    ╭─ REMOTIX 0.1.0 · Installation ────────────── Debian GNU/Linux 13 · GNOME 48 ─╮

│ Desktop           GNOME · Wayland                               ✓ OK         │

╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
    the plan screen (body only, shortened)

    The TUI talks to the engine through interfaccia.Motore (the engine interface), implemented by Sessione (the session) in the same root process: Controlla(porta) (check(port): phases 0-2 and DomandeDaFare(), the questions to ask), Piano(voci) (plan(entries): PianoInstallazione(), written to plans/), Applica(digest, eventi) (apply(digest, events)) — the approval is recorded only if the digest is the one shown — and Ferma() (stop). Events reach the screen as the engine's JSON lines, parsed by righeEventi (event lines). vista.go (the view) turns engine objects into plain words (“Graphics card”, “Sign-in”), grouping steps (the groups of one person = one row) with the real reversibility tag.

    Colours come from the mockup and degrade by themselves to 256 or 16 colours, and to none with NO_COLOR (termenv); bold stays. remotix-install tui --preview N prints every screen at width N with sample data, without root and without touching anything — the way to compare with the mockup and the basis of tui_test.go. Not shown because the engine does not know them: the size of the packages (the simulations do not give it) and automatic suspend as a check row.

    15.22 · Installer messages and texts

    All texts live in catalogues, not in the code: motore/codici.go (message and remedy of each code), motore/testi.go (states, steps, CLI, certificate; looked up with T(key, args…)), interfaccia/testi.go (the TUI). A missing key prints ⟨key⟩ and is found by TestTesti. inglese_test.go fails on any Italian word or accented letter in the strings of the code and of the catalogue.

    i
    Identifiers. the codes keep their Italian area names (RX-MANCA, RX-PIANO, RX-GRUPPI…): they are identifiers, decided in §10.35 not to change. So are the C-… conditions and the catalogue keys.

    15.23 · The RX- code catalogue

    The table is generated from installatore/motore/codici.go when the manual is built; the last column lists the non-test files whose code mentions the code (comments excluded). A code in force with no file is defined but never raised; a retired code with a file is still raised somewhere.

    15.24 · Testing the installer

    The engine's tests run with installatore/costruisci.sh prove: gofmt -l, go vet and go test in the golang:1.25 container, offline. The release refuses to continue on any FAIL or gofmt: line (17.13 “The release command”).

    What the containers cannot prove — real cards, systemd, firewalls, the four package managers on real distributions — is the job of the distribution boxes and VMs of banchi/17-distro/ (ch. 16 “Testing”). Not settled yet, from fasi/17 §6.6.16: the simulation and installation with the .run files on zypper and pacman have never run on a real machine; install to the end on the 26 combinations, the upgrade with a browser connected, and the interrupted install/uninstall are still to be run on the hardware.

    Chapter 16

    Testing

    16.1 · How REMOTIX is tested

    REMOTIX has no unit-test suite in the usual sense: the C server talks to compositors, the GPU, PAM, logind and real browsers, and almost every defect the project has paid for lived in that contact, not inside a pure function. What it has instead is a large body of benches in banchi/ — about 1,800 files kept by git — and three of them grown into permanent machinery: the safety net, the functional suite and the stress campaign.

    Two convictions shape all of it, and both were paid for. First, the bench is the first suspect (REVIEWER.md §1): the project never stalled on a hard problem, it stalled every time on a measurement that did not measure what everyone believed (LEZIONI.md §10). Second, a check that has never been seen red is not a check: every predicate carries, in --certifica, the case that makes it fail, and that case is run, not imagined (CODER.md §3.3-bis).

    i
    Scope. nothing in this chapter is a performance number. Capacity and speed results are tied to the hardware and date they were measured on and belong to ch. 18 “Performance and capacity”.

    16.2 · The bench folder

    The bench folder is a record, not a toolbox: most files were written for one phase, measured once and kept next to their results. The prefix of a file is the number of the phase that wrote it; the folders are the machinery that is still run.

    Historical benches are not maintained: they call helpers, paths and binaries of their time. They are kept because their results are cited by FASI.md and DECISIONI.md, and because a verdict must stay re-readable next to the code that produced it.

    +
    Tip. to find the bench behind a number in a document, search for the bench identifier (B12, C8, F-018, R19…) in banchi/; the file header says what it measures, from where it starts and how it knows it can say red.

    16.3 · Rules every bench follows

    Every bench and every mesh speaks the same small language. The rules are short; each one exists because its absence once produced a wrong verdict that looked right.

    Code 3 is not requeued on purpose: re-running until the wanted number appears is how the project once had to withdraw two conclusions. A single 3 is neutral; a frequent 3 is a bench defect. The functional suite maps the same three judgements onto PASS, FAIL and BLOCKED, and a BLOCKED always carries its reason.

    Isolation. Benches share one test machine, so they count everything they could share: port, ban file, socket, working directory, tree, user, uid and shared-memory name (LEZIONI.md §1.24, §1.26). Two benches on the same port once killed each other silently, and the survivor's probe kept knocking with its credentials until the server banned the machine's own address for twelve hours. Tenants created by benches are named c<n>u<n> (regular expression ^c[0-9]+b?u[0-9]+$), so that cleanup and C19 recognise them and never touch a person's account.

    !
    Why the boxes are locked. the box lock exists because a git push during a suite round once made the hook clean up every bench tenant — including the ones the suite had just created — and the failed logins got the test machine's address banned for 12 hours (29 Sep 2026). After the lock: a 60-minute short round with a push in the middle gave 368 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 BLOCKED.

    16.4 · The boxes of the safety net
