    The safety net runs in four containers, one per desktop, on the test machine itself — not in virtual machines, because a VM takes the real graphics card away, and every number of the project comes from that card (decision D1 of phase 11).

    The four desktop recipes start from debian:13 (Contenitore.xrdp is built on top of a desktop box's image) and boot systemd as PID 1. Three rules keep them honest. R1: one binary, built once, copied into all four — and its libraries taken from where the real server takes them (a box once ran the right binary against a same-named libngtcp2.so.16 of another version, started cleanly and died at the first client with Unreachable). R2: recipes declare exact versions; «the latest available» is a date disguised as a version. R3: alignment is verified by mesh C11 on the running boxes, not trusted from the recipes.

    --privileged was refused on purpose: it would have made everything pass and taught nothing. Removing pam_loginuid from the PAM stack was refused too: it would have tested a PAM chain different from the one shipped. Each recipe also carries a unit that reads the group number of the render node at boot and aligns the render group to it (pinning the host's number would make a box that works here and is silent elsewhere), and STOPSIGNAL SIGRTMIN+3: with systemd as PID 1 the default SIGTERM is ignored and podman stop waited its whole timeout.

    Step 0 (11-passo0.sh) validated the container before anything was built on it: the first process is systemd; logind knows the user and opens a session; linger starts the user manager without a login; a user unit starts inside the session; when the session closes, children really die; /run/user/<uid> exists and belongs to this box; the session bus answers; a compositor announces an output and a real client draws; the card and the hardware encoder are reachable. Measured on 26 Aug 2026: 18 verdicts green out of 18, on all four boxes.

    Adapters keep the list of checks blind to the desktop. Each box carries, at the same path, a short adattatore.<d>.sh (adapter) that answers three questions — what is your name, which package do you come from, how do I start you — for example WLR_BACKENDS=headless for labwc where Mutter wants --headless and KWin --virtual. The boundary is written in phase 11 §3.7: an adapter says how to start and look at a desktop, never how the product behaves; an adapter that starts containing product behaviour is a per-compositor exception in disguise.

    The verbs of 11-accendi.sh (on the test machine, as root)
    bash 11-accendi.sh costruisci gnome     # rebuild the image from the recipe
bash 11-accendi.sh accendi gnome        # throw the box away and start a fresh one
bash 11-accendi.sh prodotto gnome       # copy binary and page in
bash 11-accendi.sh server gnome         # start the product server on the box's port
bash 11-accendi.sh c4 kde --senza-tasto # one mesh, with its injected fault
bash 11-accendi.sh impronta gnome       # the fingerprint (R3)
bash 11-accendi.sh bilancio gnome       # server, tenants, /tmp: what is there now

    16.5 · The meshes C1 to C24

    The checks of the net are called meshes (maglie in the code) and are numbered C1–C24. The columns that matter are the third and the fourth: where it starts from and what it looks at, because those were the two that explained the three failures that created the net.

    Images are judged with three poor checks and no knowledge of what a desktop looks like: a mark with a declared tolerance (compositors apply colour profiles, and H.264 4:2:0 subsamples exactly the chroma); an image that is not degenerate (not all black, not one colour, varied enough); and the expected zone changing when it must. Pixel-by-pixel comparison with a reference rots in a week and was rejected, and so was computer vision: a tolerance and a histogram were enough, and if one day they are not, that decision will come with a measurement. The image judge itself is shared — C8 imports 10-f1-testimone.py rather than keeping a second judge that could diverge in silence.

    The net proved its worth before it was finished. Pointed at the code of 25 Aug 2026 it went red on its own on both acceptance defects — the session born blind and the second user whose browser does not start — and the injected fault exposed three bench defects that would otherwise have passed for product defects. Its full round on 27 Aug 2026 (7,896 s, four boxes) gave 57 green verdicts, 23 injected faults seen out of 25, and no bench red. Its first red from the product was two log lines in src/tastiera.c that did not name their tenant; its most valuable one was the sound reaching the client at one fortieth of its rate on GNOME only — audible and loud, so no eye would have noticed.

    i
    The lesson of C1. for weeks a number — «ten new sessions out of ten are born without a monitor» — governed the order of work. It came from one mesh whose green branch was unreachable. An agent asked to disprove it found that in ten minutes; the true cause was that bench users were not in the video and render groups (17 sessions out of 17 see with the groups, 0 out of 4 without). Rule (LEZIONI.md §1.53): when a red resists for days, first ask whether the test can say green.

    16.6 · When the net runs: the hook

    The net runs by itself: 11-gancio.sh is installed as a git pre-push hook and decides what to run from the paths that changed, not from anyone's good will. A hook that asks «do you want to run the net?» does not run on the day one is in a hurry, and those are the days things break.

    The fast family has a hard ceiling of 180 s: above five minutes a hook starts being switched off, above ten it certainly is. When time runs out meshes are cut, the ceiling is not raised, and the cuts are written at the top of the script with their cost — C8, the most important mesh, is not looked at on every push, and that is declared as the most expensive cut. A mesh that does not fit is skipped and the skip is logged; it is never truncated, because truncation would produce a red that is not the product's.

    Each round appends one line to 11-gancio-registro.jsonl: where it ran, the trigger, the family, every mesh with exit code and seconds, whether a fault was injected and seen. The file is in git with merge=union in .gitattributes, because the two halves write it on two machines and lines are only ever added. A dry run (--secco) writes its line with "secco": true and C12/C13 ignore it — otherwise one dry run would let the net claim to be alive for a week.

    Product meshes C2, C3, C4, C6, C8b, C17 and C20–C23 (C24 runs under the gate of C20) ask the gate whether the desktop has what they need (image, input, clipboard, shape) and, if not, skip with the missing capability in the register. A capability is opened only in the increment in which the mesh that judges it has given green and seen its fault — not when the code exists. The gate never softens a judgement: a mesh that passes runs with the same arguments, thresholds and faults as before. C1, C5, C7, C9, C18 and C19 do not pass through it: they run on every box and say «could not look» on their own.

    Running the hook
    bash banchi/11-scatole/11-gancio.sh decidi                     # what it would do, and why
bash banchi/11-scatole/11-gancio.sh gira --famiglia rete
bash banchi/11-scatole/11-gancio.sh gira --famiglia tutto --scatola gnome
bash banchi/11-scatole/11-gancio.sh remoto                     # decide here, run there, report back
bash banchi/11-scatole/11-gancio.sh installa pre-push
bash banchi/11-scatole/11-gancio.sh registro 10                # the last 10 rounds

    16.7 · What the net does not catch

    The net is written against defects of birth, visibility, basic function and correctness between two users. It is deliberately not a performance net, not a browser-compatibility net and not an endurance test, and the gaps are written so that nobody trusts it too much.

    16.8 · The functional suite

    On 24 Sep 2026 the user tried the product by hand and found six defects the net had not seen: the window edge that cannot be grabbed, Shift+arrow, a stripe in Firefox, the click one pixel off in Chrome, the lock icon of LXQt, «Log Out» that resurrected the LXQt session. The net looks at the pieces (the frame arrives, the key reaches the server); the suite looks at what the user does: select a text, grab an edge, log out.

    The user's decisions of that evening frame it: the suite replaces the full net, leaving under it only a short technical layer (C7, C9, C14, C18, C19); browsers are real, Firefox and Chrome on the server, real windows; the Python client does not certify; every test has its injected fault and lasts less than 10 minutes; and the cycle is round 1 ⇒ defect list ⇒ clean-up ⇒ a complete round 2 with zero defects, with product and tests frozen in between. If round 2 finds a defect, it is fixed and round 2 is redone in full, not just the red test.

    Every test is a script 15-fNNN-<name>.py that declares, as plain text lines, what it looks at: FUNZIONI = (…), and if needed PER_BROWSER = False (runs once, with Firefox), LUNGA = True (runs in parallel with the others of its desktop) and SERVER = "15-g7-server.sh" (needs its own server). The common base suite.py gives them one language: --scatola, --browser (one only), --guasto (after the healthy pass, the pass with the injected fault in the same session), --certifica, --evidenze, --porte-base; 4K by default. Each judged function prints one SUITE {…} line; the exit code is 0 all PASS, 1 a FAIL or a fault not seen, 3 a BLOCKED and no FAIL.

    Groups G7 and G8 start a second server per box, on ports 8611–8614 and 8621–8624, with shortened clocks or with their own ban file, socket and log, so that a ban test never bans the machine for the others. The dead line is simulated on the server with a private nftables table that drops the UDP of the test's port only.

    15-giro.py runs a round on the server: it finds the 15-f*.py and 15-n*.py (negative) tests, runs the four desktops in parallel (one queue each, Firefox then Chrome, distinct debugging ports), kills any test after 10 minutes as BLOCKED, refuses to start if a person (anyone who is not a bench tenant) has a session in a box, and with --strato-tecnico (technical layer) adds C7, C9, C18, C19 per box and C14 at the end. Each desktop has its own headless labwc at 3840×2160 (15-compositori.sh): in a shared compositor Chrome windows covered each other, and a covered Chrome window does not repaint — one screenshot hung for 17 minutes.

    Defects go to difetti.jsonl (the defect list) with a class — A true regression, B one desktop's assumption in common code, C bench defect, D wrong invariant (never as a shortcut) — a state, the measured cause, the commit of the cure and the test that guards it from then on. The report (15-rapporto.py, --testo or --html) is generated from the register, never written by hand: the function × desktop × browser matrix with the last verdict, the defects, and for every FAIL or BLOCKED the reason and its evidence.

    The bench entries were each a green or a red that was not the product's: a pixel judge tried only on the most colourful wallpaper (XFCE's is black), C9 not knowing the new forma log area, cleanup not done between meshes, an empty log slice read as «not read», a shortened clock shorter than XFCE's 4K start, fixed pauses synchronised with the animation they were watching. The product cures of the clean-up — session «resumed» reported correctly, the page saying that the line dropped, the abandonment clock starting at birth, KDE starting empty, the keyboard layout reaching KWin, our own Opus decoder in WebAssembly, user settings left untouched — are described in the chapters of the parts they changed.

    16.9 · Driving real browsers

    Real browsers are driven without WebDriver servers: Firefox through Marionette, the protocol Firefox speaks by itself, and Chrome through the DevTools protocol (CDP). The drivers live in 12-client-veri.py and are imported, never copied, by the suite, the stress actors and the phone bench.

    07-b46-marionette.py is a minimal Marionette client: frames are length:json, commands are [0, id, command, parameters], answers [1, id, error, result]. The bench uses WebDriver:NewSession with acceptInsecureCerts, WebDriver:Navigate, WebDriver:ExecuteScript and its async form, WebDriver:SetWindowRect and WebDriver:TakeScreenshot with an element id (Marionette has no element-screenshot command). Chrome is photographed with Page.captureScreenshot.

    Pixels are read from a photograph taken by the browser, never with getImageData: the canvas may be bitmaprenderer or transferred to a worker, and reading it from the document sees nothing — or, worse, the backing store instead of the screen (LEZIONI.md §1.16). Headless runs are declared as such: without a GPU, decoding and painting are in software, so they judge behaviour, not numbers. Default ports: Marionette 2851, Chrome DevTools 9341, Android DevTools 9342 (through adb forward); --porte-base moves them so that four desktops can run in parallel. The certification proves that a port with no server is red, that a wrong password is red by refusal (consuming one login attempt, which counts for the ban), and that a black canvas is degenerate while a gradient is not.

    !
    Marionette time is not page time. the stress actors originally stamped the time of keys typed in Firefox from the return of the Marionette action chain; a chain held back placed keys after their own echo, and «longest freeze» took the next caret blink (~1.1 s). Since phase 20 the page itself stamps gestures with a capturing keydown/pointerdown/wheel probe, and 16-riclassifica.py recomputes past levels from the page's own round-trip data.

    16.10 · Stress and capacity benches

    Phase 16 asks how much load REMOTIX carries while still working. Clients run on the server itself — the tablet's graphics and Wi-Fi would be the bottleneck — so every result is a lower bound: «N users on this server, which meanwhile also runs the N browsers».

    Each user is an independent actor (16-attore.py): its own process, browser, labwc compositor and clock, no conductor. Odd users drive Firefox, even users Chrome; tenants are c16<NNN>u<N>, created and always removed by the actor, with exactly one login attempt so that a ban is impossible. Actors are programs, not AI agents: an agent would set the rhythm of input by its own thinking time and never repeat itself, while a seed per user makes every climb different inside and identical across campaigns. The four workloads (16-lavori.py) are fixed by the user number.

    A level is GREEN if every session is GREEN, FAIL if one is FAIL; «significant DEGRADED» (more than a quarter of sessions, or one measure past the middle of its band) stops the climb for diagnosis and a repetition under the same conditions. A FAIL starts a bisection between the last good step and the broken one, precise to one user. If 4K fails the whole climb is redone at 3K (3200×1800), then 2K, then Full HD. The delay that classifies is the product's own share: the p95, over the judging window, of the per-second p95 values the child writes for its own work (copy → bytes out, frames of that second only), plus 9 ms, the constructive ceiling of the input leg (the child's 8 ms poll); the child's «capture → bytes out» lines and the page's round trip are recorded, the latter as the experienced delay, but do not classify.

    Resources are sampled once a second by 16-risorse.py (as root, or it declares what it could not read) for three process sets — remotix, sessioni, browser — with PSS memory and per-process GPU engine use from /proc/<pid>/fdinfo. A high resource alone is never a FAIL: classification comes from behaviour, and resources explain it. At every level 16-controllo-corto.py opens one extra session (the 17th at the top step, hence a session ceiling of 17 during the campaign) and runs reduced F-004, F-007, F-003 and F-014.

    Campaigns run unattended overnight as a queue (16-coda.sh the queue, 16-campagna.sh one campaign) inside a systemd-run unit with three settings that are not optional: OOMPolicy=continue (a browser killed for memory is a red step to measure, not the end of the night), TimeoutStopSec=1200 and KillMode=mixed (the queue alone receives the stop and lets the climb clean up). After the machine froze with RAM exhausted at 16 users on 28 Sep 2026, earlyoom was added to the test machine's recipe, preferring browsers as victims. Results are generated by 16-rapporto.py — the final desktop × card matrix, the curves, the bottlenecks.

    For the comparison with xrdp (phase 20) the bench has a twin: 16-attore-rdp.py drives the same four workloads with the same seeds through xfreerdp3 in a private Xvfb per user (16-compositori-rdp.sh), with XTEST for input and XDamage for paint times, against the -xrdp boxes, so that 16-classifica.py reads both with the same thresholds. 14-stress/ is the earlier, tablet-driven night harness of phase 14; its client that never stays still (removed on 10 Oct 2026 with the other benches of closed phases) found that a server heartbeat was postponed by every input message, freezing the screen for minutes under a moving mouse.

    16.11 · The distribution bench

    Phase 17 tests REMOTIX where an administrator would install it: on the official images of each distribution, in virtual machines with real kernels, SELinux, firewalls and boots — and, since VMs have no graphics card, in boxes for everything that needs the encoder.

    On 30 Sep – 1 Oct 2026 the full T10 round passed on 32 machines out of 32 (26 desktop images and 6 ISO installs), the two KDE combinations whose KWin produces no screencast without 3D in a VM being run in boxes with the real card. The requirements behind it are numbered R1–R43 in phase 17 §8: the check touches nothing (fingerprints of /etc before and after, also in prove/r1-contenitori.sh), every known fault is reported with its stable code, uninstalling undoes everything REMOTIX did and nothing else (a user already in video stays there), an update with users connected closes no desktop, SELinux enforcing logs no denial, PAM behaves as sshd on every family, bench markers are absent from the package, an interrupted installation resumes.

    i
    Boxes for all combinations. since phase 19 the installer refuses a machine without a card that encodes, so the daily round must move to the boxes. On 10 Oct 2026 the box recipes for the 26 combinations (one per distribution, with the desktop as argument) were written but none had been built yet (they are built on the test machine, after the xrdp campaign). Not settled yet: the first full round in boxes.

    17-t2/ measured what kills desktops when the service stops (nothing does, 29 Sep 2026); 17-t6/ PAM, SELinux and firewall per family; 17-t7/ updating without closing desktops on the four boxes. 17-t4-motore.sh, 17-t8/ and 17-t9/ test an installer that no longer exists (separate plan and apply, signed archive, answer files) and are kept as history; their headers say so and they are not run — except t8-browser.py, the browser that stays attached during the update, which 17-t10.sh still uses.

    16.12 · Encoder and platform benches

    When an encoder path changes, the old path stays alive as a term of comparison until the new one has been measured against it on the same frames.

    Three small folders complete the picture. rcp/ holds the twin of the RCP module that phase 1 grafted into ngtcp2's example server; the build of the product refuses to compile if the two copies differ, and GEMELLO=nessuno (twin = none) must be declared to build without the comparison. prodotto/ has the smoke test of the server inside the build container (fumo.sh, smoke) and its pages; sonda/ a real-browser probe that collects what the page saw.

    16.13 · Running the benches

    Benches are written and compiled on the laptop; they run on the test machine, where the card, the boxes and the browsers are. The test machine's root filesystem lives in RAM: after a reboot the recipe in the project notes restores packages, keys and boxes, and everything persistent sits under /media/REMOTIX.

    Typical commands
    # from the laptop: the safety net, decided here and run there
$ bash banchi/11-scatole/11-gancio.sh remoto
# from the laptop: copy the suite to the server
$ bash banchi/15-suite/15-porta.sh
# on the server, as the bench user: rebuild the boxes (only when nobody is testing by hand)
$ bash /media/REMOTIX/src/controllo/banchi/15-suite/15-rifai-scatole.sh
$ python3 /media/REMOTIX/src/controllo/banchi/15-suite/15-giro.py --elenco
$ python3 /media/REMOTIX/src/controllo/banchi/15-suite/15-giro.py --giro 3 --strato-tecnico
# one test, with real browsers
$ bash banchi/15-suite/15-una.sh --remoto 15-f001-accesso-e-prima-immagine.py --scatola gnome --browser firefox --guasto
# the report, generated from the register
$ python3 banchi/15-suite/15-rapporto.py --registro banchi/15-suite/registro.jsonl --difetti banchi/15-suite/difetti.jsonl --giro 2 --testo
# a stress climb, without doing anything (the plan)
$ python3 16-salita.py --scatola gnome --campagna prova-4k-gnome --misura 4k --secco
    !
    The boxes are also where people test. rebuilding boxes kills every session inside them, including a person's. The suite refuses to start if anyone who is not a bench tenant is logged in; rebuilding needs the user's go-ahead. And never restart the product server while the user is measuring by hand.
    • Build first, then run: a bench run against a stale binary or page measures the wrong thing; the register records binary and page md5 for this reason.
    • Look at the scene before calling anyone to judge it: a counter is not looking.
    • Close your own manual test users before starting a full round: the net reads the whole log, including lines that are not its own (C9 once went red on a leftover session, class C).
    • Measurements are not run in parallel on the same hardware; development and reading are. A bench must refuse to measure if the machine is not idle, rather than declare the load in a note nobody reads.
    Chapter 17

    Build and release

    17.1 · The build roads

    REMOTIX is never built on the host and never with sudo: every build runs in a podman container as the user, with the source tree mounted inside. There are four roads, and they share images and scripts.

    Why containers: on 14 Aug 2026 the C code could not be built at all — the laptop lacked ngtcp2 and nghttp3, the test machine's live root file system had no compiler, and the container there did not see the source tree. A rootless podman container on the laptop, with the tree mounted and the binary coming out on the host, solved it (the header of src/Contenitore, the Containerfile). The per-target containers came with phase 17 (fasi/17-l-installatore.md §6.2): the binary is not portable between distributions (OpenSSL, libei, PipeWire… differ in version and soname), so each target is compiled inside its own root.

    i
    Disk. everything temporary goes under costruzione-uscita/ (ignored by git) or installatore/.cache/, never /tmp: on the development laptop /tmp is nearly full and ~/.cache links to it.

    17.2 · Declared build dependencies

    The Makefile's header lists every library with the piece of code that needs it, because “which library is this for?” is the question asked the day one is missing (LEZIONI.md §2.5-bis: libraries installed by hand become invisible within a day). Since phase 18 there is no ffmpeg; since phase 19 no software encoder (OpenH264, SVT-AV1).

    make dipendenze checks each module and then compiles a one-line program per header (the ngtcp2, OpenSSL, PAM, VA-DRM, Vulkan headers…). It has three outcomes, and says which: OK, NO (too old, with the version found), and ?? (pkg-config does not know the module — which with a prefix may only mean the .pc is not on the path). The package recipes run it before compiling (override_dh_auto_configure, the PKGBUILD's build()).

    !
    Doc vs code. the catalogue's minimum component table says libei 1.3 and libopus 1.4; the Makefile, packaging/debian/control and remotix.spec say libei 1.1 and opus 1.3. Not settled yet which is the real floor.

    17.3 · The product Makefile

    src/Makefile builds one program, remotix, from 34 C files and 8 Wayland protocols. make (target tutto, “all”) runs impronte (fingerprints) first, then links.

    Each object lists the headers it includes (the “seams” between parts written in parallel): without them make would keep an object compiled against yesterday's contract — a program that links and misbehaves (seen on 14 Aug 2026, when cattura.o was not rebuilt). Every object depends on registro.h since it became a header of macros (25 Sep 2026). main.o deliberately does not depend on the capture and encoder headers: those parts run in the per-user child, never in the root parent. vulkanvideo.o alone gets -Wno-missing-field-initializers (Vulkan structures are filled by name).

    17.4 · The twin-copy check

    rcp.c, rcp.h and autenticazione.c exist twice in the repository — in src/ and in banchi/rcp/ — because they are the same module mounted on two hosts: the product server and the graft into ngtcp2's example server used by the benches. Until 10 Aug 2026 they were identical by luck, not by construction.

    This is why the development container mounts the whole tree, not src/, and why every package recipe copies banchi/rcp/ next to src/. The concrete case it prevents: changing the ban duration in src/rcp.c while the benches keep testing the old copy and stay green.

    17.5 · The development container

    src/Contenitore is the every-day build image, localhost/remotix-costruzione (the REMOTIX build image): Debian 13 with the declared development packages, and nghttp3 1.18.0 and ngtcp2 1.25.0 built from source at fixed tags (shared libraries in /usr/local, unlike the package images). Extra packages (libgbm-dev, libopus-dev, libvulkan-dev) sit in layers of their own at the end, so the ngtcp2 layer stays cached and the image rebuilds in seconds.

    Every-day build
    podman build -t remotix-costruzione -f src/Contenitore src/   # once, about 4 minutes
bash src/costruisci-in-contenitore.sh              # builds src/remotix
bash src/costruisci-in-contenitore.sh dipendenze   # only says what is there
bash src/costruisci-in-contenitore.sh pulisci      # removes the objects
    i
    Gap. libwayland-dev (for wayland-client and wayland-scanner) is not named in src/Contenitore, while every src/costruzione/Contenitore.* and the Debian Build-Depends name it; the image builds today, so it arrives as a dependency of another package. Not settled yet: name it explicitly.

    src/costruisci.sh is the older road, run inside the test machine's container (enter.sh): it looks for ngtcp2/nghttp3 in PREFISSO, NGTCP2, NGHTTP3 (defaults under /srv/src/b2), requires OpenSSL ≥ 3.5, deletes the old binary before building (so “it exists” means “it is new”), and then greps the binary for marker strings, with a positive control that the search tool itself works. Last, if they are missing and it can write them, it installs /etc/pam.d/remotix from src/remotix.pam and /etc/remotix/utenti-negati (the denied users) with root.

    17.6 · Per-distribution build images

    src/costruzione/Contenitore.<target> is one image per target, localhost/remotix-costruzione-<target>, with the distribution's development packages and the same static QUIC libraries for all. The image is the build environment of that target's package.

    src/costruzione/costruisci-tutti.sh [target…] (all eight by default) builds the image, copies src/ and banchi/rcp/ into $CACHE/albero-<target> (a copy of the tree) — eight targets on the same src/ would step on each other's objects — runs make pulisci and make tutto inside the image, and writes in costruzione-uscita/<target>/: the binary, immagine.log (image build), compilazione.log (compilation), versioni.txt (the versions of OpenSSL, opus, libva, libei, pipewire, glib, gcc, ngtcp2, nghttp3), ldd.txt run inside the target, and esito.txt (one-line outcome: compiles yes/no, ldd clean yes/no). ldd is not clean if any library is “not found”, if ngtcp2/nghttp3 are dynamic, if ffmpeg (libav*, libswscale, libx264/5) or a software encoder (openh264, SvtAv1) appears.

    17.7 · Static ngtcp2 and nghttp3

    src/costruzione/quic-statiche.sh (static QUIC) builds nghttp3 v1.18.0 and ngtcp2 v1.25.0 (with -DENABLE_OPENSSL=ON, which produces libngtcp2_crypto_ossl) from their git tags with CMake and Ninja, static only, PIC, libdir fixed to lib, into /usr/local/lib. It fails if any .so of them is there: the linker would prefer it.

    Each recipe then proves the link: debian/rules and the spec refuse to build if pkg-config reports another version than the one declared (Static-Built-Using, Provides: bundled(…)), and write /usr/share/remotix/incorporate.json ({"formato":"remotix-incorporate/1",…}) with the versions actually linked — static libraries leave no version string in the binary. The Arch recipe builds the same two libraries inside build() from the release tarballs, with fixed sha256.

    17.8 · The Debian package

    packaging/debian/ is copied to debian/ in a fresh copy of the tree by src/costruzione/costruisci-deb.sh and built with dpkg-buildpackage -b inside Contenitore.debian13 or .ubuntu2604 (debhelper 13, source format 3.0 native).

    After the build costruisci-deb.sh runs lintian and checks the finished package, not the tree, writing one line per check in controlli.txt (checks):

    Measured 29 Sep 2026 (commit cdefd1f): lintian 0 errors, 0 warnings; R13, R14, R4 green; R23 two identical builds on Debian 13 and Ubuntu 26.04. After apt install on debian13-gnome and ubuntu2604-kde the service was disabled and inactive, nothing listened on 7447, groups were unchanged (fasi/17 §13.2).

    17.9 · The RPM package

    packaging/rpm/remotix.spec is one spec with %if 0%{?fedora}, 0%{?rhel} and 0%{?suse_version} branches, as Cockpit does, built by packaging/rpm/costruisci-rpm.sh in the target's image (fedora44, alma10, tumbleweed, leap16) with rpmbuild -ba and rpmlint.

    The rpm unit starts the binary directly, without /bin/sh -c: under SELinux systemd moves to remotix_t only when it executes remotix_exec_t itself (T6). The Debian unit keeps sh -c 'exec …' to expand REMOTIX_PORTA and REMOTIX_OPZIONI. costruisci-rpm.sh validates remotix-firewalld.xml as XML first: firewalld silently drops a malformed service (a -- inside a comment, measured on Fedora 44, 29 Sep 2026).

    17.10 · The Arch package

    packaging/arch/PKGBUILD is built by packaging/arch/costruisci.sh [commit]: git archive of src/, banchi/rcp/ and packaging/arch/ at that commit, then makepkg as the user in localhost/remotix-costruzione-arch, namcap in a throw-away container, and the R14 blacklist. Unlike .deb and .rpm, uncommitted changes never enter an Arch package.

    !
    Code finding. the Arch unit has no EnvironmentFile for /etc/remotix/remotix.conf.d/*.conf (it sets REMOTIX_PORTA=7447 and REMOTIX_NOME=%H with Environment=) and no --journal, and the package ships neither /usr/share/remotix/remotix.conf nor the remotix.conf.d folder. The installer's port step writes /etc/remotix/remotix.conf.d/porta.conf: on Arch a non-default port is not applied, start-service waits for a port nobody opens, and the installation rolls back.

    17.11 · What the packages install

    The three families install the same pieces in the same places, except where the distribution's conventions differ. The package carries inert pieces only: it never enables or starts the service, never touches groups, firewall or system configuration (DECISIONI.md §10.12, kept by §10.36).

    The KWin permission file is byte-for-byte what the product would check (kwin_verifica_permesso()), so the product finds it right and never writes to /usr. Never in any package (fasi/17 §6.4, R14): test users, bench sudoers, gpu-udev.sh, riavvia-*.sh, provisiona.sh, ld.so.conf.d entries.

    !
    Doc vs code. the package comments (and the Debian remotix.ufw comment) still say the guards, the ufw profile and the firewalld service are “mounted by the engine with consent”. Since §10.36 the engine does none of this: the guards ship switched off and nothing switches them on; the firewall definitions are only names an administrator may use. Not settled yet: whether the guard files stay in the packages.

    17.12 · Building the installer engine

    installatore/costruisci.sh (the installer's build script) builds installatore/uscita/remotix-install (uscita: output) in docker.io/library/golang:1.25: CGO_ENABLED=0, GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor, GOPROXY=off, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, -trimpath -ldflags '-s -w', Go caches in installatore/.cache/. Go is not installed on the laptop and does not need to be.

    Building the engine
    installatore/costruisci.sh            # builds uscita/remotix-install
installatore/costruisci.sh prove      # gofmt -l, go vet ./..., go test -count=1 ./...
installatore/costruisci.sh go ...     # any go command in the same container
RX_VERSIONE=1.0.0 installatore/costruisci.sh   # -X remotix/installatore/motore.VersioneMotore=1.0.0

    Static and without cgo, the engine runs on every distribution before any package is there — Debian's glibc or Alma's. Until 10 Oct 2026 there was a second, cgo build for the Gio GUI on Debian 12's glibc; with the GUI gone (§10.31) vendor/ went from 37 to 14 MB and there is one build.

    packaging/motore/pacchetti-motore.sh (engine packages; called by the release) packages that one binary three times, refusing if the binary's version is not the release's:

    i
    Release prerequisite. the engine's Arch package is built in localhost/remotix-costruzione-arch even when BERSAGLI (the targets) excludes Arch: the image must exist for any release.

    17.13 · The release command

    packaging/rilascio.sh X.Y.Z-R is the one command of a release (for example 0.17.0-7: X.Y.Z is REMOTIX's version, R the package revision of a rebuild). The same version goes to everything: the product packages, the engine and its packages.

    Work files stay in costruzione-uscita/rilascio-X.Y.Z-R/: rilascio.log (the journal of the release), prove-motore.log (the engine tests), the product packages, the engine packages, the payload. The rpm containers leave files owned by another sub-uid, so the folder is removed with podman unshare rm -rf. The final message gives the sha256 to publish next to the file, over HTTPS, and the install command sudo sh remotix-X.Y.Z-R.run.

    17.14 · The .run file format

    The .run is the single installation file of §10.36: a POSIX shell header followed by a tar.gz. It needs only tar, gzip, sha256sum, awk and mktemp on the target.

    1. Find the first line after __PAYLOAD__ with awk; none ⇒ “the file is damaged (no payload): download it again”.
    2. Create /var/tmp/remotix-run.XXXXXX and a trap that removes it on exit, interrupt or termination.
    3. Copy the payload out with tail -n +N and check its sha256 against PAYLOAD_SHA256; a mismatch ⇒ “the file is damaged (sha256 does not match)”. (An empty value — a header not filled by the release — skips the check.)
    4. Extract, delete the archive, run the engine, exit with the engine's code.

    Two sha256 protect the file: the one of the whole .run, published on the site for the administrator, and the one of the payload, inside the header, checked every time. The rpm files inside are not signed: dnf installs them with localpkg_gpgcheck=0 and zypper with --allow-unsigned-rpm (measured 30 Sep on tumbleweed-kde: “Signature verification failed [6-File is unsigned]” otherwise) — only for these files; repository packages stay verified. The runtime side is in the installer chapter (15.4 “An installation from the .run file”).

    i
    Status. tested so far only on the laptop and only in its header: extraction, sha256, refusal of a damaged file, check (fasi/17 §6.6.16). A full install from a released .run on the distributions is still to be run.

    17.15 · Reproducible builds, SBOM and licences

    The goal (R23) is four levels of reproducibility: binary, package, package metadata, and what is published. What the recipes do for it:

    SBOM and third-party licences (R24): every product package carries incorporate.json with the linked ngtcp2/nghttp3 versions, and declares them (Static-Built-Using, Provides: bundled(…)). packaging/archivio/sbom.py (SPDX per package, red if declared and linked differ) and packaging/archivio/licenze.py (THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES with the text of every licence, including the Go modules of vendor/) were written for the signed archive's publishing step, which no longer exists: nothing calls them. Not settled yet: putting the licences back into the .run (an open point of §10.36).

    !
    Doc vs code. the package metadata still say the licence is proprietary (debian/copyright: “License: proprietary”, with a note that the distribution licence is not decided yet; License: LicenseRef-Proprietary in both specs; LicenseRef-REMOTIX in both PKGBUILDs), while DECISIONI.md §10.33 makes REMOTIX free of charge with a draft licence awaiting the user's approval. The package descriptions and summaries are still in Italian, against §10.32 (everything the administrator reads is English).

    17.16 · Version numbers

    One version per release, written in several dialects.

    The catalogue has its own version and sequence (2026.10.10.14) and the minimum engine that understands it; a new catalogue ships only with a new release.

    17.17 · The Opus decoder build

    The browser decodes Opus with a small WebAssembly module, embedded as base64 in src/pagina.html between the OPUS_WASM_INIZIO / OPUS_WASM_FINE (start / end) markers. src/opus-wasm/costruisci.sh (build) rebuilds it reproducibly.

    sh src/opus-wasm/costruisci.sh --verifica (verify) checks that the page carries exactly opus.wasm. The decoder's role in the page is described in ch. 11 “Audio and clipboard”.

    17.18 · Build pitfalls already met

    Problems already met while building, and the cure now in the scripts — so nobody meets them twice.

    Chapter 18

    Performance and capacity

    18.1 · What was measured, and on what

    This chapter answers one question for whoever maintains REMOTIX: how much load does the product carry while still working, on which hardware, and how does that compare with xrdp, the X11 remote desktop server most Linux administrators would otherwise install. Every figure was measured once, on one machine, between 7 and 10 October 2026, and is tied to that hardware and that date.

    !
    Declare the hardware. these are the numbers of this machine, and the Intel card is an integrated one. They are design evidence, not promises: DECISIONI.md §10.26 keeps them out of SPECIFICHE.md, and nothing here should be read as the capacity of a different machine.

    18.2 · The bench, the scene and the classes

    The bench is the stress harness of banchi/16-stress/, described in 16.10 “Stress and capacity benches”. In short: real browsers on the server, one per user, each in its own headless compositor, drive real desktops with input sent through the page; four fixed workloads rotate by user number; every session and every level is classified against frozen thresholds.

    The climb. Steps of 1 → 4 → 8 → 12 → 16 users, 10 minutes each (30 at the last), a repetition of any significant DEGRADED, and a bisection to one user between the last good step and the broken one. At every step one more session (user 99) logs in and runs the short functional check: a level where nobody else can get in is not a healthy level. If 4K breaks, the climb is redone at 3K, then 2K, then Full HD.

    Two numbers per climb, both written by 16-coda.sh in the queue log:

    • true GREEN (ultimo GREEN vero): the highest level where every session is GREEN — the «optimal up to» of the public table;
    • good (buono): the highest level the climb passed, admitting a non-significant DEGRADED (at most one session in four, inside the first half of its band) — the «holds up to».

    A level is FAIL if one session is FAIL, which includes the short check. The thresholds (input → frame delay, frames skipped, longest freeze, video frames painted per second, audible sound, birth time, drops, memory growth) are those of SOGLIE in 16-classifica.py, approved on 25 Sep 2026 and frozen; the table is in 16.10 “Stress and capacity benches”.

    i
    The Firefox freeze, cured. until 10 Oct 2026 the actor rebuilt the time of Firefox's keystrokes from the return of the Marionette chain; a held-back chain moved keys after their own echo and produced false freezes of ~1.1 s (the next cursor blink). The probe the actor injects now stamps every keydown in the page clock, and 16-riclassifica.py re-judges finished climbs from their files. Run on all 32 REMOTIX climbs (every one exited 0), it changed exactly three cells: Intel GNOME 3K 1 → 4, Intel XFCE 3K 4 → 8, Intel XFCE Full HD 1 → 12. The tables below are re-judged. Chrome, which types through CDP with real times, never had the defect, and neither does the xrdp actor (XTEST).

    18.3 · Capacity per card and desktop

    Each cell gives REMOTIX first, in bold, then xrdp; «—» means not even one user. The xrdp figures carry the shared-memory note of 18.5 “REMOTIX against xrdp”.

    • 15 is the bench's ceiling, not the Radeon's. In the seven cells at 15 the 16-user level fails only because the 17th session, the short check, paints nothing within 90 s; the sixteen working users are all GREEN (for example amd-f20-fhd-xfce, level 16 repeated: 16 GREEN, 1 FAIL — the check).
    • Radeon 4K on GNOME and KDE is the driver. RADV 25.0.7 accepts the ULTRA_LOW_LATENCY tuning that src/vulkanvideo.c asks for but does not pass it to the firmware: frames come out in groups, and one user's delay is 51–56 ms against a 50 ms threshold. The Debian backport of Mesa 26.1.6 brings GNOME 4K to 4 users (1 user: 21 ms); the product stays on the driver Debian 13 ships.
    • The public table (fasi/20-le-prestazioni.md §5) is the range over the four desktops:

    18.4 · What limits capacity

    At the first level that is not GREEN, 16-rapporto.py names the busiest resource and the process sets that consume it. The answer is almost never the remotix process.

    This is the physics of DECISIONI.md §4.6-nonies, seen again on all four desktops: on the integrated card the neck is composition, upstream of REMOTIX, and its currency is the composed pixel. That is why the admission budget of src/budget.c (SPECIFICHE.md §5.5; 8.11 “The composition budget”) counts composed Mpixel/s and the delay of those already inside, and refuses a newcomer with BUDGET_PIENO rather than slowing everyone down. The campaigns ran with the budget off on purpose, to find the cliff; the product's default ceiling is 10 sessions (--tetto-sessioni).

    +
    Using the numbers. to switch the budget on for a machine like this one, take the composed Mpixel/s of the last true GREEN level of the desktop and size you serve, and pass it to --budget-mpixel-s as described in 8.14 “Configuring quality and capacity”. On the Radeon the encoder, not composition, is what fills first: the budget then protects a resource it does not count directly, and the ceiling is the simpler lever.

    18.5 · REMOTIX against xrdp

    xrdp ran the same scene, the same steps and the same thresholds, in the same desktop boxes switched to X11 (Contenitore.xrdp), driven by 16-attore-rdp.py: FreeRDP in a private Xvfb per user, XTEST for input, XDamage for paint times. Three things cannot be compared by construction: skipped frames, holes in the video chain and audible sound do not exist on the xrdp side; the delay is compared only as seen by the viewer.

    • Under load REMOTIX is lighter. xrdp spends 1.5 to 4.6 times the server-side cores (the most on GNOME: Mutter on X11, xorgxrdp's capture and RemoteFX all on the CPU) and 1.3 to 1.7 times the memory. REMOTIX moves the work to the card. With a single user xrdp is the cheaper one on XFCE and LXQt (1.9–2.6 % of the machine against 4.3–4.9 %): a FreeRDP client weighs less than a browser. The gap opens with load.
    • Video. xrdp loses about one frame in five or six at every level, alone or loaded: RemoteFX on the processor is the ceiling, not the load. It sits right on the GREEN threshold (0.8 × 30 = 24) and falls below it on GNOME 2K with 4 users (DEGRADED). REMOTIX paints the full 30 with no frame skipped until the break level. (On KDE the page counts 53–58 paints per second: the compositor's repaints, not the film's frames.)
    • Delay with one user is even. Key → image p95: Intel Full HD 36–39 ms REMOTIX against 33–44 xrdp; Intel 4K 53–67 against 33–55, xrdp ahead on XFCE and LXQt; Radeon 2K and Full HD 33–45 against 32–45. The meter favours xrdp: the page's round trip includes decoding and painting in the browser, XDamage on Xvfb does not. REMOTIX's advantage is holding up under load, not one user's response.

    Where xrdp breaks, and the shared-memory wall. Most xrdp failures are not the working users: they are the next session failing to start. xorgxrdp captures each session into a shared-memory area of width × height × 4 bytes (the rdpClientConAllocateSharedMemory lines in journal-scatola.log), and when /dev/shm is full the new session's Xorg dies with Caught signal 7 (Bus error) in rdpCapture (diagnosi-sessione.txt of the short check). The boxes are started by 11-accendi.sh without --shm-size, so they get podman's default of 64 MiB, and the arithmetic matches the climbs step by step:

    On XFCE and LXQt the wall is xrdp's limit; on GNOME and KDE xrdp gives way earlier for reasons of its own (GNOME: delay p95 of 67 ms with 2 users at 2K, 40–42 % of the machine's CPU with 6 at Full HD; KDE: input lost, 3 actions out of 3 without effect with 2 users at 3K, 2K and Full HD, on both cards).

    !
    The 64 MiB wall. this is a difference of architecture, and it is how the project reads it: xorgxrdp needs width × height × 4 bytes of shared memory per session, REMOTIX needs none — frames travel from the card to the encoder as DMA-BUFs, and the few memory buffers it does use (the fallback path of src/wlroots.c, the keymap) come from memfd_create, which does not live in /dev/shm — and in the same boxes, with the same 64 MiB, REMOTIX admitted 16 users. In the user's words (10 Oct 2026): «4K is a limit for everyone … the numbers speak clearly: REMOTIX is more efficient and performs better than xrdp thanks to its newer architecture». Declare it next to every xrdp capacity figure all the same: on an ordinary installation /dev/shm is half the RAM (16 GB here) and the wall is not there, so the xrdp cells for XFCE and LXQt are a lower bound set by the box. The verdict on CPU, memory and video does not depend on it: it was measured on the users who were inside.

    18.6 · Limits of the measurements

    What the numbers above do not say, and why.

    • One machine, and a modest one where it matters: the Intel card is the integrated UHD 770.
    • The clients run on the server. Up to 16 real browsers for REMOTIX (≈ 5 GB of RAM at 11–12 users: the memory that runs out on the Intel at 2K and Full HD), FreeRDP for xrdp (1.8–2.4 cores at 4 users, decoding RemoteFX). REMOTIX's numbers are therefore a lower bound; the network is not measured (everything goes through lo).
    • The bench's ceiling is 16 users plus the check; seven Radeon cells stop at 15 because of the 17th session.
    • The memory guard of the xrdp climbs (the level closes below 3 GiB free) was never reached by xrdp (at most 40 % used). REMOTIX had no such guard; on the Intel it would have fired at the break levels, where the level is already FAIL.
    • Not comparable: skipped frames, video-chain holes and audio exist only on the REMOTIX side; GPU engine readings are empty for xrdp; the delay is compared only as seen by the viewer.
    • The 64 MiB wall cuts xrdp's XFCE and LXQt cells (18.5 “REMOTIX against xrdp”).
    • The driver decides two cells: on the Radeon at 4K, GNOME and KDE stop at RADV 25.0.7, not at REMOTIX.

    18.7 · Repeating the measurements

    A campaign is a queue of climbs that runs unattended on the test machine for one to two days per card. Never run it while someone uses the machine, and never two at once: performance is not measured in parallel.

    Starting and stopping a campaign
    # on the test machine, as nicfio: the two REMOTIX campaigns, Intel then Radeon
sudo systemd-run --unit=r20-campagna --uid=nicfio -E XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 \
     -p TimeoutStopSec=1200 -p KillMode=mixed -p OOMPolicy=continue \
     bash /media/REMOTIX/src/controllo/banchi/16-stress/16-campagna.sh intel-f20 amd-f20

# the same for xrdp: every climb gets --sistema xrdp, and the queue must never be the OOM victim
sudo systemd-run --unit=r20-xrdp --uid=nicfio -E XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 -E REMOTIX_16_SISTEMA=xrdp \
     -p TimeoutStopSec=1200 -p KillMode=mixed -p OOMPolicy=continue -p OOMScoreAdjust=-900 \
     bash /media/REMOTIX/src/controllo/banchi/16-stress/16-campagna.sh intel-x20 amd-x20

# stop between two climbs, or now
touch /media/REMOTIX/misure/fase16/FERMA
sudo systemctl stop r20-campagna

    Results land in /media/REMOTIX/misure/fase16/<label>-<size>-<desktop>/: salita.jsonl (one line per level), and per level classifica.log, risorse.jsonl, the server and box journals and the actors' stato.jsonl. The registers registro.jsonl and registro-xrdp.jsonl in banchi/16-stress/ accumulate every classification; for a repeated level the last one wins.

    i
    Read-only data. the measurement folders are treated as read-only evidence. When an analysis has to write beside the data without touching it, build a shadow tree — a real directory per climb and per level, with symbolic links to every original file — and run 16-riclassifica.py on that: this is how the re-judgement described in 18.2 “The bench, the scene and the classes” was produced on 10 Oct 2026.

    A full matrix costs about 22 hours of machine on the Intel and 28 on the Radeon for REMOTIX, about 11 and 11 for xrdp (it breaks earlier). The phases that produced these figures are fasi/16-stress-e-capacita.md (method and thresholds) and fasi/20-le-prestazioni.md (this campaign, its anomalies and the comparison).

    Chapter 19

    Extending REMOTIX

    19.1 · The increment method

    REMOTIX has been extended three times in the same way: KDE, XFCE and LXQt were each added while the desktops already served had to keep every certified capability. The method that made this work is more important than any single file it touched, and it is the first thing to reuse.

    A red on a desktop already served is a regression until proven otherwise, and it is classified: A true regression · B one desktop's assumption hidden in common code · C bench defect · D wrong invariant (never as a shortcut). Each increment is small enough that a red has one suspect. When the change to common code cannot be separated from the new desktop's code, phase 11 §3.3 asks to split it in three steps — common changes first, proved on the old desktops; then the new desktop's code, which the old ones do not cross; then switching the new box on — and to declare it when the split is impossible, because from then on a red has two suspects.

    i
    The rule that bounds every extension. there are no per-compositor feature switches. What the product offers is asked of all four desktops identically (DECISIONI.md (the decision register) §0.5, §5.1-bis); a function that one desktop cannot give leaves the product instead of living behind a switch — live canvas resizing left on 17 Aug 2026 because KWin 6.3 could not do it. Per-desktop code exists only for how: how a session starts, which protocol captures, which channel injects input.

    19.2 · A new desktop: the product side

    A desktop is not a module of REMOTIX: it is a set of answers spread across the session code, the child process and the capture, input and clipboard paths. Each family of compositors answers differently; inside a family almost everything is shared.

    The product's touch points, in the order an increment meets them:

    1. Recognition — riconosci_desktop() (recognise the desktop) in src/sessione.c, decided once per process and read through sessione_desktop(). It is a search, not an arbitration: one machine, one desktop (DECISIONI.md §0.6). A new desktop gets a new value of SessioneDesktop appended at the end: the value travels as a uint32_t between parent and child, and moving 0 or 1 would break that boundary. Its branch goes after the existing ones so that no machine served today changes behaviour; an ambiguous machine is resolved as before and declared in the log.
    2. Every implicit negation — sessione.c and figlio.c (the per-user child) were written as «if KDE … else GNOME». Adding a value turns every else into «GNOME or the new one» without a compiler warning; phase 13 counted thirteen of them. Each must become explicit, and family predicates exist for the facts that belong to the compositor rather than the session (sessione_su_wlroots(), “is the session on wlroots?”).
    3. The session — environment composed from scratch, one variable at a time (CODER.md §4.5); the start line; how «alive» is read (a name on the bus, the compositor's unit, or neither); the «Log Out» gesture the product recognises; the user-settings rule (only lock, reboot, suspend and standby may be written to the user's settings, everything else lives only in the remote session, DECISIONI.md §8.2); dangerous menu entries hidden; the guard against a second session.
    4. The stage — figlio.c opens Mutter (mutter_apri(), open Mutter), KWin (kwin_apri()) or nothing (on wlroots the source is the capture itself), then calls cattura_avvia() (start the capture) or cattura_avvia_wlr(). A pull-model source entered under the capture interface, not beside it: the 35 call sites in figlio.c did not change.
    5. Input and clipboard — input.c with libei, or wlr_input.c; appunti_apri_kde() or appunti_apri_wlroots() (open the clipboard), both in appunti.c and both handing over to appunti_kde.c.
    6. The name on the wire — main.c maps the desktop to the name sent in SESSIONE (the session message, wt_desktop()); a desktop the product does not recognise is reported as sconosciuto (unknown).
    7. Cursor shape — the real pointer shape reaches the browser on all four desktops: Mutter sends it in the cursor metadata; on KDE and labwc, where the compositor draws the pointer into the image, forma.c (shape) writes an encoded cursor theme whose colours say which shape was asked for, read from the metadata on KDE (cursore.c) and through a 3×3 probe on labwc (wlroots.c); a new desktop must give it too, or the shape leaves the product for everybody.
    !
    Guards that evaporate. phase 13 found that unita_inattiva() (unit inactive), the guard against a second session, asks systemd whether the compositor's unit is stopped — and an unknown unit counts as stopped. On a desktop whose compositor is not a unit, a guard paid for on 16 Aug 2026 would not have failed: it would have vanished. Before reusing a guard, ask what fact it reads, and whether that fact exists on the new desktop.

    19.3 · The worked example: KDE, XFCE, LXQt

    The three additions are the worked example. Each row is an increment that passed all the gates; the surprises column is the part worth reading before the next desktop.

    Two lessons recur. The second desktop asks for what the first did not — a file capability, a group, a permission — and the symptom never resembles the cause; finding it in the box before the phase cost ten minutes instead of a wrong diagnosis. And the first desktop is not the reference: when C5 went red on GNOME only, it was GNOME that behaved differently, and without the other three boxes the number would have been read as «sound works like this».

    19.4 · A new desktop: the benches and the installer

    Most of the work of a new desktop is outside src/. The order below is the one phases 11–14 settled on; each step has a reason that was paid for.

    1. Study first. Answer the fifteen questions of LEZIONI.md (lessons) §3 (how capture is asked without a portal, push or pull, is it behind a permission, can that permission be withdrawn while running, does it draw on the GPU without a monitor, what does resolution cost…) in STUDI.md (studies), and before that ask who in the world already does this on that desktop (§9 step 0: the KDE study missed KRdp because it searched only the repositories already cloned).
    2. Check the environment before the compositor. Session of class user, seat and ACLs, the video/render groups, the card, XDG_* variables read from pam_systemd and never invented (LEZIONI.md §9-bis): on GNOME, four times out of five what failed was the environment.
    3. The box. A Contenitore.&lt;name&gt; (container recipe) from debian:13 with exact versions, the desktop's real packages (not only the compositor), the clipboard tools of the other boxes, the render-group unit and STOPSIGNAL SIGRTMIN+3; extra permissions only for that desktop and each justified by what breaks without it.
    4. The adapter adattatore.&lt;name&gt;.sh — name, package, how to start — and nothing about how the product behaves.
    5. A port in the map of 11-accendi.sh (switch on a box; 8511–8514 are taken, unknown desktops get 8519) and the name in DESKTOP_NOTI (known desktops) of 11-gancio.sh (the pre-push hook). Adding a recipe triggers the desktop-nuovo (new desktop) family on the next push: everything on the new box, regression on the old ones, C14.
    6. Step 0 in the new box: 18 verdicts, all green, before anything else.
    7. A fault of its own. Every new desktop enters with at least one plausible, invented fault that the net must see (phase 11 §3.6): the net is certified against the past, and a new desktop brings its own defects.
    8. The capability gate. A row in capacita_del_desktop (the desktop's capabilities) of 11-capacita-del-prodotto.sh: empty at first, so every product mesh skips with a reason; each capability (immagine image, input, appunti clipboard, forma pointer shape) is opened in the increment in which its mesh is green and its fault was seen.
    9. The «Log Out» gesture of the desktop in the table C20 and C24 share (DESKTOP_E_GESTO, desktop and gesture): it is the desktop's gesture, not a capability of the product.
    10. The suite — the desktop list of 15-giro.py (the suite round), a headless labwc in 15-compositori.sh, and the tests that depend on the desktop's applications (file manager and terminal names, menu photographs, settings that must stay untouched in 15-f031b-impostazioni-intatte.py, settings intact).
    11. Stress — the B and C workloads of 16-lavori.py (the workloads) name the desktop's file manager and terminal; LXQt needed qterminal -e bash and a different delete gesture in pcmanfm-qt.
    12. The installer — the package that marks the desktop on each family (PacchettoDesktop, desktop package), its display name (NomeDesktop, desktop name), the catalogue's desktop entry per platform with the components it needs under labwc, and the 26-combination matrix of the distribution bench.

    19.5 · A new RCP message

    RCP/1 is closed by design: a receiver that does not understand something must close with ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO (protocol error; RCP.md §3), and inside a major version one grows only through capabilities, never by adding fields to existing messages. A new mandatory type is a new major version.

    1. Write it in RCP.md first: number, name, direction, body in the elementary types of §6.0 (big-endian, no alignment, no padding), when it is valid, the answer, what happens to other sessions of the same user. The rule in the code says it plainly: whoever changes a rule changes RCP.md first, or the two separate in silence.
    2. Decide how an old peer reacts. A peer that does not know the type closes the connection. Since page and server ship together this is acceptable for a message only one side sends on an explicit gesture (TERMINA_SESSIONE, 15 Aug 2026); for anything a client must be able to omit, add a capability in CIAO/ECCOMI (here I am; §4.3: names a-z0-9._, unknown names ignored).
    3. If it tolerates anything, add the line to the list of exceptions in §3 in the same moment — the list was found incomplete twice, and a client written from §3 closed exactly the sessions the other sections saved.
    4. Server: the constant in the type enum of src/rcp.c, the exact body length checked before allocating, the state in which it is accepted, the handler, a log line saying what was not understood when it is refused.
    5. The twin: copy the same change into banchi/rcp/. The build compares rcp.c, rcp.h and autenticazione.c byte by byte and refuses to compile if they differ; mesh C10 checks the same on the laptop.
    6. Page: the type in the TIPO (type) table of src/pagina.html (or TIPO_INPUT), the encoder or decoder with DataView in network order, and the page's own handling of the refusal.
    7. Validate against the document, not against the other side: two programs written by the same hand that agree confirm nothing. 01-b4-validatore.py (the B4 wire validator) was written from RCP.md alone and found a contradiction inside the document (the underscore in capability names, §4.3); bench B5, also reading only the document, found a second one two days later (§9 against §2.2).
    8. Tests: the suite function that exercises the gesture, real browsers, and the description in the message tables of this manual (ch. 5 “The RCP/1 protocol”, ch. 21 “Appendix A — Data structures and messages”).
    !
    Compatibility is not a feeling. a field added to an existing message «because it is compatible» is exactly what §9 forbids. The day an old phone stays behind, either the version was written well, or one discovers that the extra field broke it.

    19.6 · A new installer check

    The installer's check is a read-only inspection (phase PREFLIGHT) that builds a profile of facts, and a compatibility step that turns facts into verdicts with stable codes. A new check touches both, and the tests that guard their contracts.

    1. Read a fact in installatore/motore/preflight.go: a small function called from Preflight() that records Rilevato(), Verificato() or Sconosciuto() (detected, verified, unknown) on the profile. It may read files, ask logind, systemd and firewalld over D-Bus (properties and queries only), and nothing else: the only program ever launched is rpm -q on RPM families, from a closed list annotated in the profile. Nothing is written — R1 compares fingerprints of /etc before and after, in a container per family (prove/r1-contenitori.sh, R1 in containers). An unreadable source is UNKNOWN, never an empty value.
    2. A code, if the fact can be a problem: an entry in Codici (codes) of motore/codici.go with the form RX-&lt;AREA&gt;-&lt;NNN&gt;, a severity (INFO, WARNING, BLOCKING), a nature (ACTION_NEEDED, RETRYABLE, RECOVERABLE, ROLLBACK_NEEDED, FATAL), an English text and, when there is one, the remedy. A code never changes meaning and is never reused: a retired code stays with a «retired» text because old registers name it (RX-GPU-001 is an example).
    3. Attach it where it belongs: Con() (“with”) on the profile for a preflight message, or the verdict in compatibilita.go (compatibility; e.g. fonts.scalable = 0 under labwc adds a font package to the dependencies, or a missing item); administrator-facing sentences go through T() and motore/testi.go (texts).
    4. Tests: TestCodici fails if a code used in the sources is missing or malformed; the English tests (inglese_test.go) fail if any text that reaches the administrator looks Italian; preflight_test.go builds fake machines (a Fedora with NVIDIA, a machine without a capable card) and asserts the codes. Run them with installatore/costruisci.sh prove (go vet and go test in the official Go container).
    5. A broken machine on purpose (R2, R29): the check must report the fault with its code and its remedy, and the certification must never say green on a broken machine. UNKNOWN is never PASS (R32).
    6. The manual: the code in ch. 15 “The installer” — this manual's check refuses any RX- code it cannot find in the installer's sources.

    19.7 · A new bench or mesh

    A new bench is cheap to write and expensive to trust. The checklist below is what a reviewer asks before believing its first verdict (REVIEWER.md §1).

    +
    Tip. when a new bench turns green at the first attempt, the right suspicion is not «well done» but «am I re-writing a bench that already exists?». Four clipboard benches once all typed Ctrl+V and none tried the menu's Paste: one bench per entry path, not per function (LEZIONI.md §1.18).
    Chapter 20

    Conventions

    20.1 · Italian inside, English outside

    REMOTIX is written in Italian and speaks English. The project's own language — documents, comments, names in the code, commit messages, reports — is Italian; everything a customer or an administrator reads is English. The line is drawn by what the reader is, not by the file type.

    Why the split: the product is meant for system administrators outside Italy, and one interface is written and tested once; the project's reasoning, on the other hand, lives in a long Italian record that the code cites section by section, and translating names would sever those links. Two consequences for a maintainer: in this manual, Italian names appear only as code (they are the real names in the sources); and administrator-facing texts live in one place per program — installatore/motore/testi.go, installatore/interfaccia/testi.go, the page's own strings — so that another language can be added later without hunting for them.

    i
    The desktops keep their language. REMOTIX does not translate or touch the desktops. Users see their programs and their desktop in the machine's language; only REMOTIX's own text is English (§10.35).

    A detail of style in C and shell sources: accented letters are written with an apostrophe in comments and messages (e', puo', perche'). Inside ${…:?…} and inside double-quoted shell strings an apostrophe is not style but a hazard — see 20.6 “Rules for code and scripts”.

    20.2 · Evidence marks

    Every statement of fact in the project carries a mark that says how much it is worth. The marks are used everywhere — documents, comments, commit messages, bench headers — and they are the first thing to read in any sentence.

    A decision resting on a [?] is a decision taken halfway (LEZIONI.md §2.3-quater); the difference between «the user said yes» and «a consequence I drew» is exactly what the marks keep. When a measurement contradicts a document, the document is updated at the same moment, with the date and the source: a reference that ages in silence is worse than no reference.

    • Numbers come with their hardware and date. The project's numbers come from one test machine with an integrated Intel GPU and, for some campaigns, an AMD Radeon RX 6800; a number without its machine is not citable. A number measured under load comes with the load (LEZIONI.md §1.26).
    • Historical measurements are flagged. When ffmpeg left the product (phase 18) the measurements it invalidated were removed, and the documents that keep older numbers carry a banner saying they are historical, measured on the machine of that time.
    • External code is marked in documents with ⟨v1⟩, ⟨mutter⟩, ⟨kwin⟩ and similar, so that mesh C16 knows a cited path lives outside the repository.
    • No line coordinates into our own code (src/&lt;file&gt;.c:&lt;line&gt;) in documents: a coordinate right today is wrong next week and cannot be told apart. Cite the file and the name, which move with the code. Mesh C16 enforces it on every push that touches documents.

    20.3 · The decision register

    DECISIONI.md does not explain and does not persuade: it records. A decision taken aloud and not written is one nobody remembers in two weeks, and the first doubt reopens it from scratch.

    Each entry says what, when, why and with what certainty, usually with the user's own words. Newer sections supersede older ones; a superseded entry is not deleted but marked with ⛔ and superata da §x (superseded by §x), so that its reasoning stays readable and nobody revives it by accident (for example §10.15, a bilingual installer, superseded by §10.35). Before proposing an alternative, check that it was not already rejected — Flatpak and AppImage (§10.11), live canvas resizing (§5.1-bis), a graphical installer window (§10.31) and per-compositor targets (§0.5) all were, with reasons.

    • Decisions live in DECISIONI.md, once. Phase documents, README.md and this manual refer to them; they do not copy them. Eleven registers are eleven places to search, and sooner or later two contradict each other.
    • The «later» has its own place: MASTERPLAN.md lists work for when the product is finished. Every entry must say what it costs never to do it; an entry whose «never» costs nothing is deleted. Anything that must happen before the end goes into a phase, not there.
    • Open questions are §7 of DECISIONI.md: holes in the thinking, not work items.

    20.4 · The documents of the project

    The project keeps few, large documents, read in a fixed order. Agents' reports are not kept: in August 2026 ninety-four report files were removed by the user's decision, and what mattered in them had been moved into the documents below.

    A phase document is opened at the start and filled as the work goes; written at the end it would be an account, in which measurements are remembered rather than recorded. Its skeleton is fixed by PIANO.md §0.2:

    The skeleton of a phase document: the headings as written in Italian, with their meaning on the right
    # Fase N — <titolo>                 Phase N — <title>
Aperta il <data> · Chiusa il <data>   Opened on <date> · Closed on <date>
## Che cosa deve produrre        What it must produce: one line, and what the user sees and judges
## Il banco                      The bench: written BEFORE developing, with its positive control
## Che cosa è stato sviluppato   What was developed: files, lines, what they are for
## Le misure                     The measurements: what · expected · measured · date, the scene next to every number
## ⛔ Che cosa NON ha funzionato  What did NOT work: dead ends, with the reason, embarrassing ones included
## Le decisioni prodotte         The decisions produced: links to DECISIONI.md, never copies
## Che cosa resta [?]            What remains [?]: what the phase leaves open, declared
## Il giudizio dell'utente       The user's verdict: the real sentence, with the date

    Four rules of the plan go with it: decisions once, in DECISIONI.md; «what did not work» is filled even when it looks bad — the seven dead ends of v1 in LEZIONI.md §8 exist only because failures were written; a phase closes on a measurement judged by the user, not on a complete document (invariant I8); and the bench is certified before it is believed. And one consequence worth more than the rules: if you cannot write the bench at the start, you have not understood the phase yet.

    20.5 · Writer and reviewer

    Work is done by two kinds of agent with opposite jobs, under rules written in CODER.md and REVIEWER.md. Every rule on one side has its check on the other; a rule without a check is unverified, a check without a rule is checking something nobody asked for.

    The reviewer finds contradictions, not truths: every verdict has the form «this contradicts X», never «this is right», and a green review is declared as «found nothing», not as approval. A finding has a fixed shape — where, what it contradicts, how it is demonstrated (a concrete input, not a hypothesis), and a mark: [R] confirmed by an existing rule, corrected; [?] a suspicion, handed to the writer to measure; [M] only if actually run. The reviewer does not measure, does not rewrite and does not supplement what the code omits. The writer does not ask the reviewer to measure, and does not rewrite code on a [?] before measuring it.

    Review weighs more here than in a usual project because dropping RDP removed the external arbiter: mstsc used to complain for free when the specification was misread, and two programs written by the same hand that agree confirm nothing. Three things replace it, none sufficient alone: RCP.md (the written arbiter), the wire validator (the mechanical one) and adversarial review (the only one that can notice that client and server share the same misunderstanding). In practice reviewers are sent to disprove: the mandate «try to prove me wrong» found the unreachable green branch of C1 in ten minutes after it had governed the order of work for weeks.

    20.6 · Rules for code and scripts

    The numbers are set by the user and the technique serves them (CODER.md §1): minimum 480p at 25 fps with 24-bit colour, a guarantee of service; desired 4K at 60 fps with 10 bits per channel; and, since 9 Aug 2026, a ceiling of 50 ms and a target of 40 ms from input received to frame sent, counting only the part that is ours. Upwards the desired filters choices; downwards the minimum binds them; and delay weighs more than frames.

    Comments carry the why next to the how, and the source of the why: a section of RCP.md or DECISIONI.md, a lesson, a measurement with its date. The sources are long because of this, and deliberately so: the record of what was tried and failed sits next to the line it protects.

    The script trap of 25 Aug 2026 (CODER.md §4-bis)
    U=${1:?serve l'utente}            # ⛔ the apostrophe OPENS a quotation…
PROFILO=${2:?serve il profilo}    # …and this line ends up INSIDE the string

    (serve l'utente means “the user is needed”, serve il profilo “the profile is needed”.) The apostrophe swallowed four lines up to the next ', which sat in a comment; PROFILO= never ran, and the script died much later on an unrelated line — and bash -n passed, because the syntax was valid. Hence two rules for scripts: no apostrophes inside ${…:?…} or double-quoted strings, and a syntax check is not a test: a new script is run at least once and one looks at what it produced, not at its exit code. Benches call a program by its absolute path, without nested sh -c layers: a command nested three times lost its quotes, ran nothing and returned 0 (LEZIONI.md §1.46).

    20.7 · Before every commit

    Every commit leaves the project built, checked and documented. The list is short because most of it runs by itself; what does not run by itself is the part that is forgotten.

    1. The product builds: make in src/ (inside the build container — see ch. 17 “Build and release”). The build first compares the twin RCP files with banchi/rcp/ and stops if they differ; GEMELLO=nessuno (twin = none) builds without the comparison only when declared.
    2. The installer's tests, if installatore/ (the installer) changed: installatore/costruisci.sh prove (gofmt, go vet and go test: state machine, register, resume, codes, English texts).
    3. The documents are updated in the same commit as the change they describe: the phase document (a measurement with its date and scene), DECISIONI.md if something was decided, the chapter of this manual that describes the behaviour.
    4. The manual, if docs/sources/ changed: python3 docs/sources/build.py --controlla, then python3 docs/sources/build.py to regenerate the published page in docs/. The check fails on cited files, functions, REMOTIX_* variables or RX- codes that do not exist, on undocumented REMOTIX_* variables read by the product, on broken internal links, and on Italian left in the text or in figure labels.
    5. Push: the pre-push hook (11-gancio.sh, the hook script) picks the family from the paths that changed — Markdown documents only run C16 in under a second; banchi/ (the benches) runs the net's own checks, plus C14 (about 800 s) when the box recipes or the port map change; src/ runs the fast family under its 180 s ceiling; a new box recipe runs everything on the new desktop — and appends its line to the hook's register (11-gancio-registro.jsonl), which is committed like any file.
    6. Before closing a phase, by name: --famiglia tutto (the “all” family) or the functional suite, which no path can infer.

    Commit messages are Italian, and apart from merges and the very first commits they start with an emoji that says what kind of change it is, and cite the section of the document they implement (for example «📋 DECISIONI §10.35: …»). This is a practice of the history, not a written rule.

    !
    Do not disturb the test machine. the test machine is shared with long measurement campaigns and with the user's own manual tests. Never restart the product server, rebuild a box or run a heavy family there while a campaign or a person is using it; the box lock and the suite's «is a person logged in?» guard exist because it happened. Credentials for it are read from a file outside the repository and never committed.
    Chapter 21

    Appendix A — Data structures and messages

    21.1 · The main C structures

    This appendix collects the central data structures of the server, with the file that defines them and where they are covered. They are the contracts that run through REMOTIX. Structures private to one file are listed only when a maintainer will meet them while following a frame, an input or a farewell; the chapters named in the last column describe them in depth.

    21.2 · Index of RCP/1 messages

    All RCP/1 message types in one table, by number. Bodies use the elementary types of 5.4 “RCP: elementary types and framing”; the length column is the body length without the 6 framing bytes.

    Field names are those of RCP.md: versione version, utente user, parola password, tela canvas, vista view, larghezza/altezza width/height, disposizione keyboard layout, stato state, motivo reason, dettaglio detail (for the log), attivo_x/attivo_y hotspot, ultimo_numero last decoded frame number, esito outcome, colore colour, ritardo_ms delay, istante timestamp in microseconds, codice code, premuto pressed, asse_x/asse_y axis, carattere Unicode character, trasferimento transfer id, lunghezza length.

    i
    Defined but unused by the page. the page never sends VISTA, DISPOSIZIONE or BANCO_MARCA today; the server serves all three. ADATTA_TELA is sent once per attach, and repeated once after a NON_ORA refusal.

    21.3 · Sub-codes carried in RCP bodies

    The small enumerations that travel inside message bodies.

    21.4 · Stream, datagram and IPC layouts

    Every layout a maintainer can meet on the wire, from the outside in. All RCP integers are big-endian; the WebTransport prefixes are QUIC variable-length integers.

    WebTransport framing around RCP
    Server-opened unidirectional stream (video, clipboard)
  varint 0x54 (40 54) · varint session id · RCP payload
Client-opened unidirectional stream (input, clipboard)
  varint 0x54 (40 54) · varint session id · RCP payload
Client-opened bidirectional stream (control)
  varint 0x41 (40 41) · varint session id · RCP payload
HTTP datagram (audio)
  varint quarter stream id of the session · RCP audio datagram
    RCP payloads
    RCP framed message (control, input, clipboard)
 0      2        6
 │ tipo │ length │ body (length bytes; 6 + length <= 1 MiB)
 │ u16  │ u32    │

RCP video frame (unframed, ends with FIN; RESET_STREAM = incomplete)
