 0      2      4      8      12     16      24     28
 │ tipo │codec │width │height│numero│istante│input │ access unit …
 │ u16  │ u16  │ u32  │ u32  │ u32  │ u64   │ u32  │

RCP audio datagram
 0      2      4        12
 │ tipo │codec │istante │ one Opus packet, or 960 bytes of PCM
 │ u16  │ u16  │ u64    │

    In the RCP payloads, tipo is the message type, numero the frame number, istante a timestamp in microseconds and input the id of the last input injected before the capture (0 if none).

    The closing capsule
    CLOSE_WEBTRANSPORT_SESSION, as REMOTIX writes it on the CONNECT stream
  00        HTTP/3 frame type DATA
  07        frame length
  68 43     capsule type 0x2843 (2-byte varint)
  04        capsule length
  00 00 00 mm   u32 application error code = RCP reason
    The parent–child envelope
    Parent <-> child (SOCK_SEQPACKET, native struct layout, figlio.c)
  struct testa
   ├── u8[4]  magia            'F','I','G','1'
   ├── u16    tipo             MSG_*
   ├── u16    versione         FIGLIO_VERSIONE = 1
   ├── u64    matricola        the child's serial number
   ├── u32    uid_dichiarato   who the sender believes the child is
   └── u32    byte             body bytes after this header
  body: one struct corpo_* ; frames, cursors and clipboard text travel in
        pieces of at most PEZZO_MAX = 32768 bytes
    PAM helper and unlock command
    Parent -> helper   struct richiesta { u64 pratica; char utente[257]; char parola[1025]; char rhost[64]; }
Helper -> parent   struct risposta  { u64 pratica; u8 esito; }      esito 1 and only 1 = admitted
Unlock socket      one text line:  SBLOCCA <address>  ->  TOLTO <address> | NON-BANNATO <address>
                                   PING               ->  PONG
                                   anything else      ->  NON-CAPITO <line>

    In the helper messages, pratica is the ticket number that pairs answer and request, utente the user, parola the password, rhost the client address for PAM_RHOST and esito the outcome. On the unlock socket, SBLOCCA means unlock, TOLTO lifted, NON-BANNATO not banned and NON-CAPITO not understood.

    The recording format of the benches (RCPREG magic 0x00 0x03) is in 5.23 “Testing against the specification”.

    21.5 · Protocol and transport constants

    The protocol and transport constants a maintainer is most likely to look for, with their value and home. Each lives in one place; where a number was once copied by hand into several files, the copies diverged.

    Chapter 22

    Appendix B — File map

    22.1 · The project's files

    Every product file with its line count, recounted each time the manual is generated: the server, the page, the installer and its interface, the packaging of each family and the sources of this manual. The files kept out are the installer's vendored modules, the protocol headers generated at build time and binary images. If a file is missing from the map, or the map lists a file that no longer exists, generation stops — and so does build.py --controlla. The role of each file is taken from its own header comment; for C modules the .h carries the why and the .c the how.

    22.2 · The bench files by folder

    banchi/ holds about 1,800 files and is described by folder, not file by file. The prefix of a file at the root is the number of the phase that wrote it; the folders with a name are either evidence kept next to a result or machinery that is still run. How to run them is in 16.13 “Running the benches”.

    Chapter 23

    Appendix C — Known issues

    23.1 · Open defects in the product

    Defects found while this manual was written (10 October 2026), by reading the code against the documents. Each one was checked in the source. They are recorded here so that a maintainer meets them before a user does; a defect leaves this table in the commit that cures it.

    23.2 · Stale texts in the code

    Comments and log lines in the code that no longer describe what the code does. None changes behaviour, but each one misleads the next reader.

    i
    Documents. the project documents (SPECIFICHE.md, RCP.md, DECISIONI.md, the phase documents) carry their own list of stale passages, found in the same pass; they are corrected there, not here.
    Chapter 24

    Glossary

    24.1 · Italian names in the code

    The code and the documents of REMOTIX are written in Italian, and many names a maintainer meets are Italian words used as terms. They are listed here as they are spelled in the sources, with their English meaning and the section that explains them.

    aiutante
    Helper. The PAM helper process: a dispatcher started once at boot that forks one short-lived grandchild per password check, so that PAM, which can take seconds, never blocks the server's single loop (aiutante.c). See 2.4 “The PAM helper process”.
    anello
    Link. One link of the chain a phase builds — capture, encoding, wire, decoding, input. A module's header says which link of which phase it is, and each link has its own bench.
    appunti
    Clipboard. Plain text only, in both directions, announced first and pulled on demand (appunti.c on GNOME, appunti_kde.c on KDE and labwc). See 11.7 “Clipboard at a glance”.
    attore
    Actor. One simulated user of the stress benches: its own process, browser, labwc and clock, no conductor (16-attore.py). See 16.10 “Stress and capacity benches”.
    banco, banchi
    Bench, benches. A test or a measurement, with its scene, its verdict and its results kept next to it, in banchi/. BANCO_ACCESO is the build switch of the bench functions, 0 in the product. See 16.2 “The bench folder”.
    budget
    The optional composition budget: an admission check in megapixels per second, off by default (--budget-mpixel-s). See 8.11 “The composition budget”.
    cattura
    Capture. Reading the pixels of the session's virtual output from the compositor: a PipeWire node on GNOME and KDE, screencopy on labwc (cattura.c, wlroots.c). See 6.1 “Capture at a glance”.
    certifica
    Certify. In a bench, --certifica runs the pure judges on synthetic inputs that must give red and inputs that must stay green; in the installer, the platform certification after installing (certifica.go). See 16.3 “Rules every bench follows”, 15.16 “Verification and the certificate”.
    chiave
    Key, that is keyframe. RICHIEDI_CHIAVE asks for one; the child keeps a debt (debito_chiave) until it has produced it. See 7.9 “Keyframes on demand”.
    cinture
    Belts. The three system settings that forbid power-off, reboot and suspend: a polkit rule, logind key settings and sleep settings. The packages ship them inert in /usr/share/remotix/cinture/. See 14.10 “The power belts, shipped inert”.
    codificatore
    Encoder. The front of video encoding: picks Vulkan Video or VA-API by capability, checks the bytes, owes keyframes, enforces the 16 MiB ceiling (codificatore.c). See 7.1 “Encoding at a glance”.
    confessione
    Confession. What the encoder declares it really produced, read back from the bytes: codec string, depth, a promotion from 8 to 10 bits, the route used (CodificatoreConfessione). See 7.8 “Bytes, levels and the confession”.
    CONGEDO
    Farewell. The RCP message that closes a session, always with a reason code; the reason is repeated in the WebTransport close code. See 5.18 “RCP: the farewell”, 5.19 “Disconnect reasons”.
    copia zero
    Zero copy (COPIA_ZERO). The frame never leaves the GPU between compositor and encoder; the default. See 6.8 “Zero copy and the memory fallback”.
    cucitura
    Seam. A header that joins two pieces and is owned by the coordinator, not by either piece: input.h, appunti.h, cursore.h, tastiera.h. The defects of phase 3 lived between pieces each correct on its own.
    cursore, forma
    Cursor, shape. The pointer is drawn by the page; only its shape travels (CURSORE_FORMA). Where the compositor does not send it, an encoded theme of 1×1 coloured images and a dictionary recover it. See 6.9 “The cursor channel”, 6.10 “The encoded cursor theme”.
    diario
    Diary. The page's /diario endpoint: the page writes its own lines into the server log. See 4.7 “The page server”.
    disposizione
    Layout (keyboard). Proposed by the page in ATTACCA; the session's real keymap is always the one in force. See 10.11 “Keyboard layout negotiation”.
    figlio
    Child. One process per admitted user, running as that user: it opens the logind session, starts the desktop and holds the stage. In ps it is remotix-figlio --figlio-interno. See 2.5 “The per-user child process”.
    gancio
    Hook. 11-gancio.sh, the git pre-push hook that runs the safety net chosen by the paths that changed. See 16.6 “When the net runs: the hook”.
    gemello
    Twin. The copy of rcp.c, rcp.h and autenticazione.c in banchi/rcp/; make refuses to build if the two differ (GEMELLO names the folder). See 17.4 “The twin-copy check”.
    impronta
    Fingerprint. Four different things: the SHA-256 of the session certificate the page fetches from /impronta; the installer's machine fingerprint that binds a plan; the impronte target of the Makefile (the twin check); the folder fingerprint of test R1. See 4.6 “serverCertificateHashes and the fingerprint”, 15.9 “The machine fingerprint”.
    incremento
    Increment. A new capability or desktop added while every certified one is kept, through the gates CP0 onwards. See 19.1 “The increment method”.
    inquilino
    Tenant. A user being served. Tenants created by benches are named c&lt;n&gt;u&lt;n&gt; so that cleanup never touches a person's account. See 16.3 “Rules every bench follows”.
    lastra
    Slab. On labwc, a GBM buffer REMOTIX owns on the compositor's render node, into which the compositor copies each frame. See 6.7 “Slabs: zero copy on labwc”.
    LETTERA, POSIZIONE_TASTO
    Letter, key position. Text travels as characters, commands as evdev key positions; the child turns a letter into the keys that produce it on the session's layout. See 10.6 “Keyboard: letters and positions”, 10.10 “From a letter to key positions”.
    linea morta
    Dead line. The detector that closes a connection which has stopped carrying anything: 5 s of stalled video output, or 10 s without a client packet. See 8.9 “The dead line”.
    maglie
    Meshes. The checks of the safety net, C1 to C24. See 16.5 “The meshes C1 to C24”.
    marca
    Mark. The bench marker BANCO_MARCA (a coloured square painted after a known delay, refused in the product), and the image mark read by 03-marca.py. See 5.16 “The bench marker: BANCO_MARCA”.
    motore
    Engine. remotix-install, the only place with installation logic; the TUI and the command line are its faces. See 15.1 “The installer at a glance”.
    catalogo
    Catalogue. catalogo.json, the supported distributions, desktops, minimum versions and rules, compiled into the engine. See 15.13 “The catalogue of platforms”.
    operazione
    Operation. One installation, upgrade or uninstallation of the engine, with its folder, state, plan and write-ahead log. See 15.5 “Operation states”.
    pacchetto unico
    Single package. The remotix-X.Y.Z-R.run file: a shell header and a tar.gz with the engine and the REMOTIX packages of every target. See 17.14 “The .run file format”.
    palco
    Stage. What the child mounts on the user's desktop: virtual monitor, capture, input, clipboard, cursor. It belongs to the session and outlives every client (invariant I4); the cap counts stages (palchi_quanti()). See 3.5 “The stage and the virtual monitor”.
    parlantina
    Chatter. --parlantina: frame-by-frame detail lines from transport, capture and encoder, never sent to the journal. See 13.11 “Diagnostic instruments”.
    piano
    Plan. The list of steps the installer will do, with how each is done, verified and undone, shown before the single question. See 15.14 “The installation plan”.
    ponte
    Bridge. struct ponte, which carries the transport and the children table to the callbacks; main.c is the only file that knows both. See 2.3 “The parent process”.
    posto
    Attach slot. A user's place in RCP's registry: one per user, freed on detach or after 30 s of silence. See 3.6 “Detach and reattach”.
    presenza
    Presence. The table of main.c that runs each user's abandonment clock, from the birth of the stage to its end. See 2.9 “Where state lives”.
    registro
    Register, log. In the server, the log module (registro.c), the only place that writes lines. In the installer, the write-ahead log of an operation (registro.go). See 13.1 “The log module”, 15.7 “The write-ahead log and resume”.
    riserva
    Reserve. --riserva: the share of an idle tenant's worst case the budget keeps aside. See 8.12 “Admission: the session cap and the budget”.
    ritmo
    Rate (frame rate). The rate regulator holds a frame back when two live deltas are still queued (arretrato); the only mechanism that lowers the frame rate. See 8.7 “The rate regulator”.
    ritrovo, ritrovati
    Finding again, found again. Live REMOTIX desktops that no child holds, found at startup after a restart and counted until their user returns. See 3.7 “Desktops found again after a restart”.
    salita
    Climb. One ramp of the stress campaign, adding users level by level (16-salita.py). See 16.10 “Stress and capacity benches”.
    SBLOCCA
    Unblock. The request on the unlock socket that lifts an address ban. See 14.6 “The unlock command socket”.
    scatole
    Boxes. The podman containers with systemd and the real graphics card in which the safety net runs, one per desktop (rete11-gnome … rete11-lxqt). See 16.4 “The boxes of the safety net”.
    sentinella
    Sentinel. The code that asks logind whether a user has a local graphical session, and checks that the remote one has no seat. See 2.7 “The logind sentinel”.
    sessione
    Session. Two meanings: the RCP session of one connection, and the user's graphical session, started headless by the child (sessione.c). See 3.4 “Birth of a session”.
    sfratto
    Eviction. Ghost eviction (--sfratto-ms, 15 s): a slot held by a silent client goes to a new client of the same user. See 8.10 “Ghost eviction and audio silence”.
    sgombra
    Clear out. The video queue threshold (--sgombra-soglia-ms): an old delta is abandoned only if the queue cannot drain in time. See 8.6 “The video queue threshold”.
    strade
    Routes. The hardware encoding paths, vulkan and vaapi; the installer requires at least one with a capable card. See 15.11 “Encoding routes and the card verdict”.
    suite
    The functional suite: what a user does, on four desktops with real Firefox and Chrome. See 16.8 “The functional suite”.
    suono
    Sound. The session's virtual sink and the capture of its monitor (suono.c). See 11.3 “The session sink and its capture”.
    tastiera
    Keyboard. tastiera.c, from a character to the key positions that produce it. See 10.10 “From a letter to key positions”.
    tela
    Canvas. The size of the remote desktop, agreed at attach (ADATTA_TELA, TELA), 320×240 to 4096×2304. See 9.7 “Canvas and view”.
    terreno
    Terrain. What a bench needs before it can judge (users, boxes, server, scene); exit code 2 means the terrain does not hold. See 16.3 “Rules every bench follows”.
    testimone
    Witness. An independent observer a bench uses to see an effect from outside the piece being judged — never the sender's own log.
    tetto
    Ceiling, cap. A hard limit: --tetto-sessioni (10 stages), TETTO_FOTOGRAMMA (16 MiB per frame), the handshake ceilings. See 8.12 “Admission: the session cap and the budget”, 5.9 “Handshake deadlines and session states”.
    utenti-negati
    Denied users. The list read by pam_listfile in the PAM file; it holds root. Missing, it makes PAM refuse everyone. See 14.4 “The PAM service files”.
    verdetto
    Verdict. PAM's yes or no, handed back to the server; never sent sooner than one second after CREDENZIALI. See 5.7 “Credentials, the fixed delay and the address ban”.
    vista
    View. The size at which the page draws the canvas; it follows the window and never touches the desktop (VISTA). See 9.7 “Canvas and view”.

    24.2 · Technical terms A–L

    Protocol and technology terms used in the manual, with what they mean for REMOTIX.

    Annex B
    The H.264/HEVC stream form with a start code before every NAL unit. REMOTIX sends pure Annex B, with parameter sets before every keyframe and no description. See 7.8 “Bytes, levels and the confession”.
    Attach
    Asking for a desktop after admission: ATTACCA carries the wanted canvas, the view and the layout; SESSIONE answers new or resumed. See 5.8 “ATTACCA and SESSIONE: attaching to a desktop”.
    AV1
    A video codec offered until phase 18; its RCP number 2 is reserved forever and never reused. See 7.2 “Codecs and their negotiation”.
    BT.709
    The colour matrix of every REMOTIX stream: full-range RGB to limited-range YUV 4:2:0. See 7.6 “BT.709 colour conversion”.
    Bubble Tea
    The Go terminal interface library the installer's TUI is built on, with lipgloss. See 15.21 “The installer TUI”.
    CDP
    Chrome DevTools Protocol: how the benches drive real Chrome, without a WebDriver server. See 16.9 “Driving real browsers”.
    Capability
    A name-value pair exchanged in CIAO and ECCOMI; within RCP/1 the protocol grows only through capabilities. See 5.6 “CIAO and ECCOMI: capability negotiation”.
    D-Bus
    The system and session message buses. The installer talks to systemd, logind and firewalld over the system bus; the child talks to Mutter and KWin over the user's session bus, which root cannot join. See 2.5 “The per-user child process”.
    Datagram
    An unreliable QUIC message. Only audio uses datagrams, one block each. See 4.9 “Streams versus datagrams”, 5.15 “Audio datagrams”.
    Decision numbers
    References such as DECISIONI §10.36, D1–D14 (installer decisions) or D-006 (page decisions) point to the decision register. See 20.3 “The decision register”.
    Delta frame
    A frame predicted from the previous ones (V_DELTA); losing one ruins the following ones until a keyframe. See 5.11 “Key frames and abandonment”.
    DeX
    Samsung's desktop mode for Android phones, with mouse and keyboard: the main Android use of REMOTIX. See 9.15 “Browsers supported and untested”.
    DMA-BUF
    A Linux buffer shared between devices and processes by file descriptor; how frames stay on the GPU from compositor to encoder. See 6.8 “Zero copy and the memory fallback”.
    Drop-in
    A systemd override file. REMOTIX writes user-unit drop-ins that make gnome-shell headless and give KWin a virtual output of the canvas size. See 12.4 “GNOME sessions”, 12.5 “KDE Plasma sessions”.
    EIS, libei
    Emulated input: the library and protocol through which a sender injects input into a compositor. Used on GNOME and KDE; labwc has none. See 10.12 “Injection through libei”.
    Evidence marks
    [M] measured, [R] read in reference code, [S] read in a specification, [?] assumed. See 20.2 “Evidence marks”.
    Exp-Golomb
    The variable-length integer coding of H.264/HEVC headers, written by scrittore_bit.c. See 7.7 “Writing the bitstream headers”.
    Extended CONNECT
    The HTTP/3 request (RFC 9220) that opens a WebTransport session, here on /rcp/1. See 4.8 “The WebTransport layer”.
    GBM
    Generic Buffer Management: the Mesa API used to allocate the slabs on labwc. See 6.7 “Slabs: zero copy on labwc”.
    GOP
    Group of pictures. REMOTIX uses an infinite GOP: keyframes only when one is owed. See 7.9 “Keyframes on demand”.
    H.264, HEVC
    The two video codecs REMOTIX encodes, numbered 3 and 1 in RCP. Firefox on Linux receives H.264 only. See 7.2 “Codecs and their negotiation”.
    Headless
    Without a physical monitor or seat: every REMOTIX session is born headless, with one virtual monitor. See 3.4 “Birth of a session”.
    HTTP/3
    HTTP over QUIC, provided by nghttp3; WebTransport runs on top of it. See 4.1 “The transport stack at a glance”.
    Invariants I1–I8
    The eight rules of CODER.md §2, quoted throughout the code (I1 the rate falls only on measure, I3 the guard starts from denied, I4 the stage outlives the client…). See 2.1 “Architectural principles”, 20.5 “Writer and reviewer”.
    Keyframe
    A frame decodable on its own (IDR, V_CHIAVE), carrying its parameter sets; about ten times a delta. See 7.9 “Keyframes on demand”, 8.8 “Keyframe request pacing”.
    KWin
    The KDE Plasma compositor. REMOTIX starts it with --virtual and captures through zkde_screencast_unstable_v1. See 6.4 “KDE: the KWin screencast protocol”.
    labwc
    The wlroots compositor under which REMOTIX runs XFCE and LXQt. See 12.6 “XFCE sessions on labwc”.
    logind
    systemd's login manager: sessions, seats, local-session checks, and the termination of REMOTIX sessions at uninstall. See 2.7 “The logind sentinel”.

    24.3 · Technical terms M–Z

    Marionette
    Firefox's own remote-control protocol, used by the benches to drive real Firefox. See 16.9 “Driving real browsers”.
    Mesa, RADV
    The open graphics drivers; RADV is AMD's Vulkan driver, which encodes through Vulkan Video. See 7.5 “The Vulkan Video encoder”.
    MSE
    Media Source Extensions: an optional drawing path of the page, off because it adds hundreds of milliseconds. See 9.14 “The optional paths: video worker and MSE”.
    Mutter
    The GNOME compositor. REMOTIX uses its direct RemoteDesktop and ScreenCast D-Bus interfaces, not the portal. See 6.3 “GNOME: the Mutter D-Bus sequence”.
    netem
    The Linux queueing discipline that simulates bad networks; benches take a lock before using it. See 16.3 “Rules every bench follows”.
    ngtcp2, nghttp3
    The QUIC and HTTP/3 libraries, linked statically at pinned versions. See 4.2 “Why ngtcp2 and nghttp3”, 17.7 “Static ngtcp2 and nghttp3”.
    NV12, P010
    The 4:2:0 YUV layouts handed to the encoder, 8 and 10 bits. See 7.6 “BT.709 colour conversion”.
    Opus
    The audio codec: 48 kHz stereo, 20 ms blocks, 96 kbit/s; decoded in the page by libopus compiled to WebAssembly. See 11.5 “The Opus encoder”, 11.6 “Playing audio in the page”.
    PAM
    Pluggable Authentication Modules: the machine's own password check, service remotix, a copy of the distribution's sshd stack. See 14.3 “Authentication with PAM”, 14.4 “The PAM service files”.
    Phase
    A unit of the project's work with its bench and closing criterion, numbered 0 to 21 (phase 21, the licence, was closed without being built); bench file prefixes carry the phase number. See 20.4 “The documents of the project”.
    PipeWire
    The media server that carries the screen stream on GNOME and KDE and the session's sound. See 6.5 “PipeWire negotiation, resize and wake-up”.
    polkit
    The authorisation service; the first belt is a polkit rule that refuses power-off and its relatives. See 14.10 “The power belts, shipped inert”.
    QP
    Quantisation parameter. REMOTIX encodes at constant QP 26; the 16 MiB ceiling walks it to 35, 44, 51. See 8.3 “Encoder rate control”, 8.4 “The 16 MiB frame cap and the quality ladder”.
    QUIC
    The UDP transport (version 1, TLS 1.3 built in) under HTTP/3; one connection per client. See 4.4 “QUIC transport parameters”.
    RCP/1
    Remotix Control Protocol, version 1: what page and server say inside the WebTransport session — handshake, video, audio, input, clipboard, canvas, farewell. See 5.1 “RCP: the protocol model”.
    RESET_STREAM
    Abandoning a QUIC stream; how a video frame no longer useful is dropped. See 4.9 “Streams versus datagrams”.
    Rigor rule
    Whatever an RCP receiver does not understand closes the session with ERRORE_PROTOCOLLO; nothing is ignored. See 5.2 “RCP: the rigor rule”.
    RX- codes
    The installer's stable message codes, RX-&lt;AREA&gt;-&lt;NNN&gt;, never reused. See 15.23 “The RX- code catalogue”.
    SBOM
    Software bill of materials, produced per package by the release. See 17.15 “Reproducible builds, SBOM and licences”.
    screencopy
    zwlr_screencopy_manager_v1: the wlroots protocol with which REMOTIX pulls each frame on labwc. See 6.6 “XFCE and LXQt: wlroots screencopy”.
    SELinux
    On Fedora and Alma a policy module gives the server its domain and lets the child pass to the user's context. See 14.11 “The service unit and SELinux”.
    serverCertificateHashes
    The WebTransport option by which the browser accepts a certificate by its SHA-256, only if valid for less than 14 days; hence the 13-day session certificate. See 4.6 “serverCertificateHashes and the fingerprint”, 4.5 “TLS and the two certificates”.
    SPS, PPS, VPS
    The parameter sets in front of every keyframe, written by REMOTIX since phase 18. See 7.7 “Writing the bitstream headers”.
    TUI
    The installer's text interface, remotix-install tui. See 15.21 “The installer TUI”.
    uaccess
    The logind ACL that gives the seat owner the GPU; remote sessions have no seat, hence the card groups. See 14.8 “The graphics card groups”.
    VA-API, libva
    The video acceleration API used directly, without libavcodec, on Intel and AMD. See 7.4 “VA-API without libavcodec”.
    Vulkan Video
    The Vulkan encode extensions; the first route where the card supports it (AMD with RADV, NVIDIA proprietary). See 7.5 “The Vulkan Video encoder”.
    Wayland
    The display protocol of all four desktops REMOTIX serves; X11 is not served. See 12.1 “Desktops at a glance”.
    WebAssembly
    The page runs libopus compiled to WebAssembly instead of the browser's AudioDecoder. See 17.17 “The Opus decoder build”.
    WebCodecs
    The browser API that decodes the video (VideoDecoder); with WebTransport, the technical minimum of a client. See 9.10 “Decoding with WebCodecs”.
    WebGL2
    The default drawing path of the page. See 9.11 “Drawing paths: WebGL2, bitmaprenderer, 2D canvas”.
    WebTransport
    Streams and datagrams over HTTP/3 for web pages; server side, REMOTIX implements it itself in webtransport.c. See 4.8 “The WebTransport layer”.
    wlroots
    The compositor library labwc is built on; it has no PipeWire node and no libei. See 6.6 “XFCE and LXQt: wlroots screencopy”, 10.14 “Virtual keyboard and pointer on labwc”.
    XKB, xkbcommon
    Keyboard layouts and keymaps; tastiera.c reads the session's keymap with xkbcommon. See 10.10 “From a letter to key positions”.
    xrdp
    The X11 remote desktop server REMOTIX is compared against in the phase 20 campaign. See 16.4 “The boxes of the safety net”, 16.10 “Stress and capacity benches”.
